9.text: For there was no one that was able to understand any good doctrine: but were foolish and as unfit as young babes.

10.text: They must have one thing often repeated.

11.text: Let one teach what he can, yet they will no more understand him, than if he spoke in a strange language.

12.text: That is, the prophet, whom God would send.
This is the doctrine on which you ought to stay and rest.
Show to them that are weary and have need of rest, what the true rest is.

13.text: Because they will not receive the word of God, when it is offered, it comes of their own malice, if after their hearts are so hardened, that they care not for it, as before, Isaiah 6:9 .

15.text: They thought they had shifts to avoid God’s judgments, and that they could escape though all others perished.
Though the prophets condemned their idols and vain fruit of falsehood and vanity, yet the wicked thought in themselves that they would trust in these things.

16.text: That is, Christ, by whom all the building must be tried and upheld, Psalms 118:22 , Matthew 21:42 , Acts 4:11 , Romans 9:33 , 1 Peter 2:6 .
He will be quiet, and seek no other remedies, but be content with Christ.

17.text: In the restitution of his Church, judgment and justice will reign.
God’s corrections and affliction.
Affliction will discover their vain confidence, which they kept secret to themselves.

19.text: Terror and destruction will make you learn that which exhortations and gentleness could not bring you to.

20.text: Your affliction will be so sore, that you are not able to endure it.

21.text: When David overcame the Philistines, 2 Samuel 5:20 , 1 Chronicles 14:11 .
Where Joshua discomfited five kings of the Amorites, Joshua 10:12 .

25.text: As the plowman has his appointed time, and various instruments for his labour, so has the Lord for his vengeance: for he punishes some at one time, and some at another, some after one sort, and some after another, so that his chosen seed is beaten and tried, but not broken as are the wicked.

1.text: Or Ariel: the Hebrew word Ariel signifies the Lion of God, and signifies the Altar, because the altar seemed to devour the sacrifice that was offered to God, as in Ezekiel 43:16 .
Your vain confidence in your sacrifices will not last long.

2.text: Your city will be full of blood as an altar on which they sacrifice.

4.text: Your speech will be no longer be so lofty but abased and low as the very charmers who are in low places and whisper, so that their voice can scarcely by heard.

5.text: Your hired soldiers in whom you trusted, will be destroyed as dust or chaff in a whirlwind.

7.text: The enemies that I will bring to destroy you, and that which you place your vain trust in will come at unawares even as a dream in the night. Some read as if this was a comfort to the Church for the destruction of their enemies.

8.text: That is, he thinks that he eats.

9.text: Muse on this a long as ye like, yet you will find nothing but opportunity to be astonished for your prophets are blind, and therefore cannot direct you.

11.text: Meaning, that it is all alike, either to read, or not to read, unless God open the heart to understand.

13.text: Because they are hypocrites and not sincere in heart, as in Matthew 15:7-8 .
That is, their religion was learned by man’s doctrine, and not by my word.

14.text: Meaning, where God is not worshipped according to his word, both magistrates and ministers are fools and without understanding.

15.text: This is spoken of them who in heart despised God’s word, and mocked at the admonitions but outwardly bore a good face.

16.text: For all your craft says the Lord, you are not able to escape my hands any more than the clay that is in the potter’s hands has power to deliver itself.

17.text: Will there not be a change of all things? Carmel is a plentiful place in respect to what it will be then and may be taken for a forest, as in Isaiah 32:15 and thus he speaks to comfort the faithful.

21.text: They who went about to find fault with the prophets words, and would not abide admonitions, but would entangle them and bring them into danger.

24.text: Signifying that unless God gives understanding and knowledge, man cannot but still err and murmur against him.

1.text: Who contrary to their promise take not me for their protector and contrary to my commandment seek help from strangers.
They seek shifts to cloak their doings and not godly means.

4.text: The chief of Israel went into Egypt as an ambassador to seek help and abode at these cities.

6.text: That is, a heavy sentence or prophecy against the beasts that carried their treasures into Egypt, by the wilderness, which was south from Judah, signifying that if the beasts would not be spared, the men would be punished much more grievously.

7.text: That is, to Jerusalem.
And not to come to and fro to seek help.

8.text: That is, this prophecy.
That is may be a witness against them for all posterity.

9.text: He shows what was the cause of their destruction and brings also all misery to man: that is, because they would not hear the word of God, but delighted to be flattered and led in error.

10.text: Threaten us not by the word of God, neither be so rigorous, nor talk to us in the Name of the Lord, as in Jeremiah 11:21 .

12.text: Meaning, in their stubbornness against God and the admonitions of his prophets.

14.text: Signifying that the destruction of the wicked will be without recovery.

15.text: Often by his prophets he put you in remembrance of this, that you should only depend on him.

16.text: We will trust to escape by our horses.

17.text: Whereas all the trees are cut down save two or three to make masts.

18.text: judgment: blessed [are] all they that wait for him.
He commends the great mercies of God, who with patience waits to call sinners to repentance.
Not only in punishing but in using moderation in the same, as in Jeremiah 10:24 ; Jeremiah 30:11 .

21.text: God will direct all your ways and appoint you how to go either hither or thither.

22.text: You will cast away your idols which you have made of gold and silver with all that belongs to them, as a most filthy thing and polluted.
Showing that there can be no true repentance, unless both in heart and deed we show ourselves enemies to idolatry.

25.text: By these various manners of speech he shows that the happiness of the Church will be so great, that no one is able sufficiently to express it.

26.text: When the Church is restored, the glory of it will pass seven times the brightness of the sun: for by the sun and moon which are two excellent creations, he shows what will be the glory of the children of God in the kingdom of Christ.

27.text: This threatening is against the Assyrians the chief enemies of the people of God.

28.text: To drive you to nothing: and thus God consumes the wicked by that means, by which he cleanses his.

29.text: You will rejoice at the destruction of your enemies, as they who sang for joy at the solemn feast, which began in the evening.

31.text: God’s plague.

32.text: It will destroy.
With joy and assurance of the victory.
Against Babel, meaning the Assyrians and Babylonians.

33.text: Here it is taken for hell, where the wicked are tormented, read 2 Kings 23:10 .
So that their estate or degree cannot exempt the wicked.
By these figurative speeches he declares the condition of he wicked after this life.

1.text: There were two special reasons why the Israelites should not join with the Egyptians: first, because the Lord had commanded them never to return there, De 17:16,28:68 lest they should forget the benefit of their redemption: and secondly, lest they should be corrupted with the superstition and idolatry of the Egyptians, and so forsake God, Jeremiah 2:18 .
Meaning, that they forsake the Lord, if they put their trust in worldly things: for they cannot trust in both.

2.text: And knows their crafty enterprises, and will bring all to nought.

3.text: Meaning, both the Egyptians and the Israelites.

4.text: He shows the Jews that if they would put their trust in him, he is so able, that no one can resist his power and so care over them, as a bird over her young, which ever flies about them for their defence: which similitude the scripture uses in various places, as in De 32:11, Matthew 23:37 .

6.text: He touches their conscience that they might earnestly feel their grievous sins, and so truly repent, for as much as now they are almost drowned and past recovery.

7.text: By these fruits your repentance will be known, as in Isaiah 2:20 .

8.text: When your repentance appears.

9.text: This was accomplished soon after when Sennacherib’s army was discomfited, and he fled to his castle in Nineveh for comfort.
To destroy his enemies.

1.text: This prophecy is of Hezekiah, who was a figure of Christ, and therefore it should chiefly be referred to him.
By judgment and justice is meant an upright government, both in policy and religion.

2.text: Where men are weary with travelling for lack of water.

3.text: He promises to give the true light which is the pure doctrine of God’s word, and understanding, and zeal of the same, are contrary to the threatenings against the wicked, Isaiah 6:9 ; Isaiah 29:10 .

5.text: Vice will no more be called virtue, nor virtue esteemed by power and riches.

9.text: He prophecies of such calamity to come that they will not spare the women and children, and therefore wills them to take heed and provide.

10.text: Meaning that the affliction would continue long and when one year was past, yet they should look for new plagues.
God will take from you the means and opportunities, which made you contemn him: that is, abundance of worldly goods.

12.text: By the breasts he means the plentiful fields, by which men are nourished as children with the breast: or, the mothers for sorrow and heaviness will lack milk.

15.text: That is, when the Church will be restored, thus the prophets after they have denounced God’s judgments against the wicked, used to comfort the godly, lest they should faint.

The field which is now fruitful, will be but as a barren forest in comparison to what it will be then as in Isaiah 29:17 which will be fulfilled in Christ’s time, for then they who were before as the barren wilderness, being regenerate will be fruitful and they who had some beginning of godliness, will bring forth fruit in such abundance, that their former life will seem but as a wilderness where no fruit was.

19.text: They will not need to build it in high places for fear of the enemy: for God will defend it, and turn away the storms from hurting their conveniences.

20.text: That is, upon fat ground and well watered, which brings forth in abundance, or in places which before were covered with waters, and now made dry for your uses.
The fields will be so rank, that they will send out their cattle to eat up the first crop, which abundance will be signs of God’s love and favour toward them.

1.text: Meaning, the enemies of the Church, as were the Chaldeans and Assyrians, but chiefly of Sennacherib, but not only.
When your appointed time will come that God will take away your power: and that which you have wrongfully gained, will be given to others, as in Amos 5:11 .
The Chaldeans will do the same to the Assyrians, as the Assyrians did to Israel, and the Medes and Persians will do the same to the Chaldeans.

2.text: He declares by this what is the chief refuge of the faithful, when troubles come, to pray, and seek help from God.
Which helped our fathers as soon as they called on you.

3.text: That is, the Assyrians fled before the army of the Chaldeans, or the Chaldeans for fear of the Medes and Persians.
When you, O Lord, lifted up your arm to punish your enemies.

4.text: You who as caterpillars destroyed with your number the whole world, will have no strength to resist your enemies the Chaldeans: but will be gathered on a heap and destroyed.
Meaning, the Medes and Persians against the Chaldeans.

6.text: That is, in the days of Hezekiah.

7.text: Sent from Sennacherib.
Whom they of Jerusalem sent to intreat of peace.

8.text: These are the words of the ambassadors, when they returned from Sennacherib.

9.text: Which was a plentiful country, meaning, that Sennacherib would destroy all.

10.text: To help and deliver my Church.

11.text: This is spoken against the enemies, who thought all was their own, but he shows that their enterprise will be in vain, and that the fire which they had kindled for others would consume them.

13.text: His vengeance will be so great that all the world will talk of it.

14.text: Which do not believe the words of the prophet, and the assurance of their deliverance.

16.text: Meaning, that God will be a sure defence to all them that live according to his word.

17.text: They will see Hezekiah delivered from his enemies and restored to honour and glory.
They will be no more shut in as they were by Sennacherib, but go where it pleases them.

18.text: Before this liberty comes you will think that you are in great danger: for the enemy will so sharply assail you that one will cry "Where is the clerk that writes the names of them who are taxed?" another, "Where is the receiver?" another will cry for him that values the rich houses, but God will deliver you from this fear.

21.text: Let us be content with this small river of Shiloah and not desire the great streams and rivers, by which the enemies may bring in ships and destroy us.

23.text: He derides the Assyrians and enemies of the Church, declaring their destruction as they who perish by shipwreck.
He comforts the Church, and shows that they will be enriched with all benefits both of body and soul.

1.text: He prophecies of the destruction of the Edomites and other nations which were enemies to the Church.

2.text: God has determined in his counsel and has given sentence for their destruction.

4.text: He speaks this in respect to man’s judgment, who in great fear and horrible troubles, think that heaven and earth perishes.

5.text: I have determined in my secret counsel and in the heavens to destroy them till my sword is weary with shedding blood.
They had an opinion of holiness, because they came from the patriarch Isaac, but in effect were cursed by God, and enemies to his Church as the papists are.

6.text: That is, both of young and old, poor and rich of his enemies.
That famous city will be consumed as a sacrifice burnt to ashes.

7.text: The mighty and rich will be as well destroyed as the inferiors.

9.text: He alludes to the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, Genesis 19:24 .

11.text: Read Isaiah 13:21 , Zephaniah 2:14 .
In vain will any man go about to build it again.

12.text: Meaning, here will be neither order nor policy nor state of commonwealth.

14.text: Read Isaiah 13:21 .

15.text: Signifying that Idumea would be a horrible desolation and barren wilderness.

16.text: That is, in the law where such curses are threatened against the wicked.
That is, beasts and souls.
That is, the mouth of the Lord.

17.text: He has given the beasts and souls Idumea for an inheritance.

1.text: He prophecies of the full restoration of the Church both of the Jews and Gentiles under Christ, which will be fully accomplished at the last day: although as yet it is compared to a desert and wilderness.

2.text: The Church which was before compared to a barren wilderness will by Christ be made most plenteous and beautiful.
He shows that the presence of God is the reason that the Church brings forth fruit and flourishes.

3.text: He wills all to encourage one another, and especially the ministers to exhort and strengthen the weak, that they may patiently abide the coming of God, which is at hand.

4.text: To destroy your enemies.

5.text: When the knowledge of Christ is revealed.

6.text: They who were barren and destitute of the graces of God, will have them given by Christ.

8.text: It will be for the saints of God and not for the wicked.
God will lead and guide them, alluding to the bringing forth of Egypt.

9.text: As he threatens the wicked with destruction by this, Isaiah 30:6 .

10.text: Whom the Lord will deliver from the captivity of Babylon.

1.text: This history is rehearsed because it is as a seal and confirmation of the doctrine before, both for the threatenings and promises: that is, that God would permit his Church to be afflicted, but at length would send deliverance.
When he had abolished superstition, and idolatry, and restored religion, yet God would exercise his Church to try their faith and patience.

3.text: For he was now restored to his office, as Isaiah had prophesied in Isaiah 22:20 .
This declares that there were few godly to be found in the king’s house, when he was driven to end this wicked man in such a weighty matter.

4.text: Sennacherib’s chief captain.

5.text: He speaks this in the person of Hezekiah, falsely charging him that he put his trust in his wit and eloquence, while his only confidence was in the Lord.

6.text: Satan laboured to pull the godly king from one vain confidence to another: that is, from trust in the Egyptians, whose power was weak and would deceive them, to yield himself to the Assyrians, and so not to hope for any help from God.

9.text: He reproaches Hezekiah’s small power, which is not able to resist one of Sennacherib’s least captains.

10.text: Thus the wicked to deceive us, will pretend the Name of the Lord: but we must try the spirits, whether they are of God or not.

11.text: They were afraid, lest by his words, he should have stirred up the people against the king, and also pretended to grow to some appointment with him.

16.text: The Hebrew word signifies blessing, by which this wicked captain would have persuaded the people, that their condition would be better under Sennacherib than under Hezekiah.

19.text: That is, of Antioch in Syria, of which these two other cities also were: by which we see how every town had its peculiar idol, and how the wicked make God an idol because they do not understand that God makes them his scourge, and punishes cities for sin.

21.text: Not that they did not show by evident signs that they detested his blasphemy: or they had now rent their clothes, but they knew it was in vain to use long reasoning with this infidel, whose reign they would have so much more provoked.

1.text: In sign of grief and repentance.

2.text: To have comfort from him by the word of God, that his faith might be confirmed and so his prayer be more earnest: teaching by it that in all dangers these two are the only remedies to seek to God and his ministers.

3.text: We are in as great sorrow as a woman in labour who cannot be delivered.

4.text: That is, will declare by effect that he has heard it: for when God defers to punish, it seems to the flesh, that he knows not the sin, or hears not the cause.
Declaring that the ministers office stands not only in comforting by the word, but also in praying for the people.

7.text: Of the Egyptians and Ethiopians, who will come and fight against him.

8.text: Which was a city toward Egypt, thinking by it to have stayed the force of his enemies.

10.text: Thus God would have him utter a most horrible blasphemy before his destruction: as to call the author of all truth a deceiver: some gather by this that Shebna had disclosed to Sennacherib the answer that Isaiah sent to the king.

12.text: Which was a city of the Medes.
Called also Charre a city in Mesopotamia, from which Abraham came after his fathers death.

16.text: He grounds his prayer on God’s promise, who promised to hear them from between the Cherubims.

18.text: Meaning, the ten tribes.

20.text: He declares for what cause he prayed, that they might be glorified by it through all the world.

22.text: Whom God had chosen to himself as a chaste virgin, and over whom he had care to preserve her from the lusts of the tyrant, as a father would have over his daughter.

23.text: Declaring by this that they who are enemies to God’s Church fight against him whose quarrel his Church only maintains.

25.text: He boasts of his policy in that he can find means to nourish his army: and of his power in that his army is so great, that it is able to dry up whole rivers, and to destroy the waters which the Jews had closed in.

26.text: Signifying that God did not make his Church to destroy it, but to preserve it: and therefore he says that he formed it of old, even in his eternal counsel which cannot be changed.

27.text: He shows that the state and power of most flourishing cities endures but a moment in respect to the Church, which will remain forever, because God is the maintainer of it.

28.text: Meaning, his counsels and enterprises.

29.text: Because Sennacherib showed himself as a devouring fish and furious beast, he uses these similarities to teach how he will take him and guide him.
You will lose your labour.

30.text: God gives signs after two sorts: some go before the thing as the signs that Moses worked in Egypt, which were for the confirmation of their faith, and some go after the thing, as the sacrifice, which they were commanded to make three days after their departure: and these latter are to keep the blessings of God in our remembrance, of which sort this here is.
He promises that for two years the ground would feed them of itself.

31.text: They whom God has delivered out of the hands of the Assyrians will prosper: and this properly belongs to the Church.

35.text: For my promise sake made to David.

37.text: Which was the chiefest city of the Assyrians.

38.text: Who was also called Sardanapalus, in whose days ten years after Sennacherib’s death the Chaldeans overcame the Assyrians by Merodach their king.

1.text: Soon after that the Assyrians were slain: so that God will have the exercise of his children continually, that they may learn only to depend on God and aspire to the heavens.

2.text: For his heart was touched with fear of God’s judgment, seeing he had appointed him to die so quickly after his deliverance from so great calamity, as one unworthy to remain in that estate, and also foreseeing the great change that would come in the Church, as he left no son to reign after him: for as yet Manasseh was not born, and when he reigned, we see what a tyrant he was.

6.text: He not only promises to prolong his life, but to give him rest and quietness from the Assyrians, who might have renewed their army to revenge their former defeat.

7.text: For Hezekiah had asked for a sign for the confirmation of his faith, as in Isaiah 38:22 , 2 Kings 20:8 , to which he was moved by the singular motion of God’s spirit.

8.text: Read 2 Kings 20:8 .

9.text: He left this song of his lamentation and thanksgiving to all posterity, as a monument of his own infirmity and thankful heart for God’s benefits, as David did, Psalms 51:1 .

10.text: At which time it was told to me, that I would die.

11.text: I will no more praise the Lord here in this temple among the faithful thus God permits his dearest children to want his consolation for a time that his grace afterward may appear when they feel their own weakness.

12.text: By my sin I have provoked God to take my life from me.
That is, in one day, or shortly.

13.text: Overnight I thought that I would live till morning, but my pangs in the night persuaded me the contrary: he shows the horror that the faithful have when they apprehend God’s judgment against their sin.

14.text: I was so oppressed with sorrow, that I was not able to utter my words, but only to groan and sigh.

15.text: God has declared by his prophet that I will die and therefore I will yield to him.
I will have no release, but continual sorrows while I live.

16.text: They who will outlive the men that are now alive, and all they who are in these years will acknowledge this blessing.
That after that you had condemned me to death you restored me to life.

17.text: While I thought to have lived in rest and ease being delivered from my enemy, I had grief upon grief.
He values more the remission of his sins, and God’s favour than a thousand lives.

18.text: For as much as God has placed man in this world to glorify him, the godly take it as a sign of his wrath, when their days were shortened, either because they seemed unworthy for their sins to live longer in his service, or for their zeal to God’s glory, seeing that there are so few in earth who regard it as in Psalms 6:5 ; Psalms 115:17 .

19.text: All posterity will acknowledge and the fathers according to their duty toward their children will instruct them in your graces and mercies toward me.

20.text: He shows what is the use of the Congregation and Church, that is, to give the Lord thanks for his benefits.

21.text: Read 2 Kings 20:7 .

22.text: As in Isaiah 38:7 .

1.text: This was the first king of Babylon, who overcame the Assyrians in the tenth year of his reign.

2.text: Read 2 Kings 20:13 , 2 Chronicles 32:25 ; 2 Chronicles 32:31 .

4.text: He asks him of the particulars, to make him understand the craft of the wicked, which he before being overcome with their flattery and blinded with ambition, could not see.

6.text: By the grievousness of the punishment is declared how greatly God detested ambition and vain glory.

7.text: That is, officers and servants.

8.text: Read 2 Kings 20:19 .

1.text: This is a consolation for the Church, assuring them that they will never be destitute of prophets by which he exhorts the true ministers of God that then were, and those also that would come after him, to comfort the poor afflicted and to assure them of their deliverance both of body and soul.

2.text: The time of her affliction.
Meaning, sufficient as in Isaiah 61:7 and full correction, or double grace, while she deserved double punishment.

3.text: That is, of the prophets.
That is, in Babylonia and other places, where they were kept in captivity and misery.
Meaning Cyrus and Darius who would deliver God’s people out of captivity and make them a ready way to Jerusalem.

4.text: Whatever may prevent or hinder this deliverance will be removed.

5.text: This miracle will be so great, that it will be known through all the world.

6.text: The voice of God which spoke to the prophet Isaiah.
Meaning, all man’s wisdom and natural powers, James 1:10 , 1 Peter 1:24 .

7.text: The spirit of God will discover the vanity in all that seems to have any excellency of themselves.

8.text: Though considering the frailty of man’s nature many of the Jews would perish, and so not be partakers of this deliverance, yet God’s promise would be fulfilled, and they who remained, would feel the fruit of it.

9.text: To publish this benefit through all the world.
He shows in one word the perfection of all man’s happiness, which is to have God’s presence.

10.text: His power will be sufficient without help of any other, and will have all means in himself to bring his will to pass.

11.text: He will show his care and favour over them who are weak and tender.

12.text: Declaring that as only God has all power, so does he use the same for the defence and maintenance of his Church.

13.text: He shows God’s infinite wisdom for the same.

17.text: He speaks all this to the intent that they would neither fear man nor put their trust in any, save only in God.

18.text: By this he arms them against the idolatry with which they would be tempted in Babylon.

20.text: He shows the rage of the idolaters, seeing that the poor who do not have enough to meet their own needs will defraud themselves to serve their idols.

21.text: Do you not have the word of God, which plainly condemns idolatry?
Can you not learn by the visible creatures whom God has made for your use, that you should not serve them or worship them?

24.text: So that his power appears in every place we turn our eyes.

26.text: Who has set in order the infinite number of the stars.

27.text: He rebukes the Jews because they did not rest on the providence of God, but thought that he had forsaken them in their troubles.

28.text: And therefore all power is in his hand to deliver when his time comes.
Showing that men must patiently abide, and not curiously seek out the cause of God’s delay in our affliction.

30.text: They who trust in their own virtue, and do not acknowledge that all comes from God.

1.text: God as though he pleaded his cause with all nations requires silence, that he may be heard in his right.
That is, gather all their power and supports.

2.text: Who called Abraham (who was the pattern of God’s justice in delivering his Church) from the idolatry of the Chaldeans to go to and fro at his commandment and placed him in the land of Canaan.

4.text: Who has created man and maintained his succession.
Though the world set up many gods, yet they diminish nothing of my glory: for I am all one, unchangeable, which have ever been and will be for ever.

5.text: Considering my excellent works among my people.
They assembled themselves and conspired against me to maintain their idolatry.

6.text: He notes the obstinacy of the idolaters to maintain their superstitions.

8.text: And therefore ought not to pollute yourself with the superstition of the Gentiles.

10.text: That is, by the force of promise, in the performance of which I will show myself faithful and just.

12.text: Because they will be destroyed.

14.text: Thus he calls them because they were contemned of all the world, and that they considering their own poor estate should seek him for help.

15.text: I will make you able to destroy all your enemies no matter how mighty, and this chiefly is referred to the kingdom of Christ.

17.text: That is, they who will be afflicted in the captivity of Babylon.

18.text: God would rather change the order of nature than that they should want anything, who cry to him by true faith in their miseries: declaring to them by this that they will lack nothing by the way, when they return from Babylon.

20.text: That is, has appointed and determined that it will come to pass.

21.text: He bids the idolaters to prove their religion and to bring forth their idols, that they may be tried whether they know all things, and can do all things, which if they cannot do, he concludes that they are not gods, but vile idols.

24.text: So that a man cannot make an idol, without doing that which God detests and abhors for he chooses his own devises and forsakes the Lords.

25.text: Meaning, the Chaldeans.
That is, Cyrus, who will do all things in my name and by my direction: by which he means that both their captivity and deliverance will be ordered by God’s providence and appointment.
Both of the Chaldeans and others.

26.text: Meaning, that none of the Gentile gods can work any of these things.

27.text: That is, the Israelites who return from the captivity.
That is, a continual succession of prophets and ministers.

28.text: When I looked whether the idols could do these things, I found that they had neither wisdom nor power to do anything: therefore he concludes that all are wicked that trust in such vanities.

1.text: That is, Christ, who in respect to his manhood is called here servant. The prophets used to make mention of Christ after they declared any great promise, because he is the foundation on which all the promises are made and ratified.
For I have committed all my power to him, as to a most faithful steward: some read, I will establish him: that is, in his office by giving him the fulness of my Spirit.
Only he is acceptable to me and they that come to me by him: for there is no other means of reconciliation, Matthew 12:18 , Ephesians 4:1
He will declare himself governor over the Gentiles and call them by his word, and rule them by his Spirit.

2.text: His coming will not be with pomp and noise, as earthly princes.

3.text: He will not hurt the weak and feeble, but support and comfort them.
Meaning, the wick of a lamp or candle which is almost out, but he will cherish it and snuff it, that it may shine brighter.
Although he favours the weak, yet will he not spare the wicked, but will judge them according to truth and equity.

4.text: Till he has set all things in good order.
The Gentiles will desire to receive his doctrine.

6.text: Meaning, to a lawful and just calling.
To assist and guide you.
As him, by whom the promise made to all nations in Abraham will be fulfilled.

8.text: I will not permit my glory to be diminished: which I would do if I were not faithful.

9.text: As in time past I have been true in my promises, so will I be in time to come.

11.text: Meaning, the Arabians, under whom he comprehends all the people of the East.

13.text: He shows the zeal of the Lord, and his power in the conservation of his Church.

14.text: I will haste to execute my vengeance, which I have so long deferred as a woman that desires to be delivered, when she is in labour.

16.text: That is, my poor people, who are in perplexity and care.

19.text: That is, Israel, which would have most light because of my Law.
The priest to whom my word is committed, who would not only hear it himself but cause others to hear it.
As the priests and prophets that would be lights to others?

22.text: Because they will not acknowledge this blessing from the Lord, who is ready to deliver them, he permits them to be spoiled by their enemies through their own fault and incredulity.
There will be no one to comfort them , or to will the enemy to restore that which he has spoiled.

23.text: Meaning, God’s wrath.

1.text: After these threatenings he promises deliverance to his Church, because he has regenerated them, adopted them, and called them.
When you see dangers and conspiracies on all sides, remember this benefit and the love of your God, and it will encourage you.

2.text: By water and fire he means all kinds of trouble and peril.

3.text: I turned Sennacherib’s power against these countries, and made them suffer the affliction which you would have done, and so were as the payment of our ransom, Isaiah 37:9 .

4.text: I will not spare any man, rather than you should perish, for God values one of his faithful more than all the wicked in the world.

5.text: He prophecies of their deliverance from the captivity of Babylon, and so of the calling of the universal Church, alluding to that which is written in De 30:3 .

7.text: Meaning that he could not be unmindful of them, unless he would neglect his own Name and glory.

9.text: Signifying that no power can resist him in doing this miraculous work, nor are all their idols able to do the same, as in Isaiah 41:22 .
To prove that the things which are spoken of them are true.
Showing that the malice of the wicked hinders them in the knowledge of the truth, because they will not hear when God speaks by his word.

10.text: The prophets and people to whom I have given my law.
Meaning especially Christ, and by him all the faithful.

14.text: By Darius and Cyrus.
They will cry when they would escape by my water, seeing that the course of the Euphrates is turned another way by the enemy.

16.text: When he delivered Israel from Pharaoh, Exodus 14:22 .
When the Israelites passed through Jordan, Joshua 3:17 .

17.text: When he delivered his people out of Egypt.
Pharaoh and his mighty army.

19.text: Meaning, that their deliverance out of Babylon would be more famous than that from Egypt was, Jeremiah 23:7 , Haggai 2:10 , 2 Corinthians 5:17 , Revelation 21:5 ; Revelation 21:7 .

20.text: They will have such abundance of all things as they return home, even in the dry and barren places, that the very beasts will feel my blessings and will acknowledge them: much more men ought to be thankful for the same.

22.text: You have not worshipped me as you ought to have done.
Because you have not willingly received that which I commanded you, you grieved me. By which he shows that his mercies were the only reason for their deliverance, as they had deserved the contrary.

23.text: Meaning, in true faith and obedience.

24.text: Either for the composition of the sweet ointment Exodus 30:34 , or for the sweet incense Exodus 30:7 .

26.text: If I forget anything that may make for your justification, put me in remembrance and speak for yourself.

27.text: Your ancestors.
Your priests and your prophets.

28.text: That is, rejected, abhorred, and destroyed them in the wilderness and at other times.

2.text: He treated and chose you from the beginning of his own mercy, and before you could merit anything.
Whom God accepts as righteous: or who had opportunity to it because of the law, and your holy calling.

3.text: Because man of himself is as the dry and barren land, he promises to moisten him with the waters of his Holy Spirit, Joel 2:28 , John 7:38 , Acts 2:17 .

4.text: That is, your children and posterity will increase wonderfully after their deliverance from Babylon.

5.text: By this diversity of speech he means one thing, that is, that the people will be holy, and receive the true religion from God, as in Psalms 87:5 .

6.text: I am always like myself, that is, merciful toward my Church, and most able to maintain it, as in Isaiah 41:4 ; Isaiah 48:12 , Revelation 1:17 ; Revelation 22:13 .

7.text: And appoint them that will deliver the Church.
That is, tell me how I should proceed in this.
God calls the Israelites ancient, because he preferred them to all others in his eternal election.
Meaning, their idols.

8.text: Read Isaiah 43:10 .

9.text: Whatever they bestow on their idols, to make them seem glorious.
That is, the idolaters seeing that their idols are blind, are witnesses of their own blindness, and feeling that they are not able to help them, must confess that they have no power.

10.text: Meaning that whatever is made by the hand of man, if it is valued as a god, is most detestable.

By which appears their blasphemy, who call images the books of the laity, seeing that they are not only here called unprofitable, but in Isaiah 41:24 abominable. Jeremiah calls them the work of errors, Jeremiah 10:15 , Habakkuk, a lying teacher Habakkuk 2:18 .

11.text: That is, who in any way consent either to the making or worshipping.
Signifying, that the multitude will not then save the idolaters, when God will take vengeance, although they excuse themselves by it among men.

12.text: He describes the raging affection of the idolaters, who forget their own necessities to set forth their devotion toward their idols.

13.text: To place it in some Temple.

15.text: He sets forth the obstinacy and malice of the idolaters who though they see by daily experience that their idols are no better than the rest of the matter of which they are made, yet they refuse the one part, and make a god of the other, as the papists make their cake god, and the rest of their idols.

16.text: That is, he either makes a table or trenchers.

18.text: The prophet gives here an answer to all them who wonder how it is possible that any would be so blind as to commit such abomination, saying that God has blinded their eyes, and hardened their hearts.

20.text: He is abused as one that would eat ashes, thinking to satisfy his hunger.

21.text: Showing that man’s heart is most inclined to idolatry, and therefore he warns his people by these examples, that they should not cleave to any but to the living God, when they should be among the idolaters.

23.text: He shows that the work of the Lord toward his people will be so great, that the insensible creatures will be moved with it.

25.text: He arms them against the soothsayers of Babylon, who would have said that they knew by the stars that God would not deliver Israel, and that Babylon would stand.

26.text: Of Isaiah and the rest of his prophets, who assured the Church of God’s favour and deliverance.

27.text: He shows that God’s work would be no less notable in this their deliverance, than when he brought them out of Egypt, through the sea.

28.text: To assure them of their deliverance he names the person by whom it would be, more than a hundred years before he was born.

1.text: To assure the Jews of their deliverance against the great temptations that they would abide, he names the person and the means.
Because Cyrus would execute the office of a deliverer, God called him his anointed for a time, but after another sort than he called David.
To guide him in the deliverance of my people.

2.text: I will take away all impediments and hindrances.

3.text: Not that Cyrus knew God to worship him correctly, but he had a certain particular knowledge as profane men may have of his power, and so was compelled to deliver God’s people.

4.text: Not for anything that is in you, or for your worthiness.

5.text: I have given you strength, power and authority.

7.text: I send peace and war, prosperity and adversity, as in Amos 3:6 .

8.text: He comforts the Jews as if he would say, "Though when you look to the heavens and earth for comfort you see nothing now but signs of God’s wrath, yet will cause them to bring forth certain tokens of your deliverance, and of the performance of my promise": which is meant by righteousness.
I have appointed Cyrus to this use and purpose.

9.text: By this he bridles their impatience, who in adversity and trouble murmur against God, and will not tarry his pleasure: willing that man would match with his like, and not contend against God.
That is, it is not perfectly made.

11.text: Instead of murmuring, humble yourselves and ask what you will for the consolation of my children, and you will be sure of it as you are of these things which are at your command. Some read it with an interrogation, and make it the application of the comparison.

12.text: That is, the stars.

13.text: That is, Cyrus, that I may show by him the faithfulness of my promise in delivering my people.
Meaning, freely and without ransom, or any grievous condition.

14.text: These people were tributaries to the Persians, and so king Artahshashte gave this money toward the building of the temple, Ezra 7:27 .
While they were your enemies, they will now honour you and you will rule them: which was accomplished in the time of Christ.

15.text: By this he exhorts the Jews to patience, though their deliverance is deferred for a time: showing that they would not repent their long patience, but the wicked and idolaters will be destroyed.

18.text: That is, of men, but chiefly of his Church.

19.text: As do the false gods, who give uncertain answers.

20.text: All you idolaters who though you seem to have worldly dignity yet in God’s sight you are vile and abject.

22.text: He calls the idolaters to repentance, willing them to look on him with the eye of faith.

23.text: That is, that the thing which I have promise will be faithfully performed.

The knowledge of God and the true worshipping will be through all the world, Romans 14:11 , Philippians 2:10 by which he signifies that we must not only serve God in heart, but declare the same also by outward profession.

24.text: Meaning the faithful will feel and confess this.
All the contemners of God.

1.text: These were the chief idols of Babylon.
Because they were of gold and silver, the Medes and Persians carried them away.

2.text: The beasts that carried the idols fell down under their burden.
He derides the idols, who had neither soul nor sense.

3.text: He shows the difference between the idols and the true God; for they must be carried by others, but God himself carries his, as in De 32:11 .

4.text: Seeing I have begotten you, I will nourish and preserve you forever.

5.text: The people of God setting their own calamity, and the flourishing estate of the Babylonians, would be tempted to think that their God was not so mighty as the idols of their enemies: therefore he describes the original of all the idols to make them to be abhorred by all men: showing that the most that can be spoken in their commendation, is but to prove them vile.

8.text: Become wise, meaning, that all idolaters are without wit or sense, like mad men.

11.text: That is, Cyrus, who will come as swift as a bird and fight against Babylon.
Him by whom I have appointed to execute that which I have determined.

12.text: Who by your incredulity would prevent the performance of my promise.

13.text: He shows that man’s incredulity cannot abolish the promise of God, Romans 3:3 .

1.text: Which has lived in wealth and wantonness and has not yet been overcome by any enemies.
Your government will be taken from you.

2.text: You will be brought to most vile servitude: for to turn the mill was the office of slaves.
The things in which she sets her greatest pride, will be made vile, even from the head to the foot.

3.text: I will use no humanity nor pity toward you.

4.text: The Israelites will confess that the Lord does this for his Church’s sake.

5.text: For shame, and hide yourself.

6.text: They abused God’s judgments, thinking that he punished the Israelites, because he would completely cast them off, and therefore instead of pitying their misery, you increased it.

9.text: So that your punishment will be so great, as is possible to be imagined.

10.text: You thought that your own wisdom and policy would have saved you.

12.text: He derides their vain confidence, who put their trust in anything but in God, condemning also such vain sciences, which serve no use, but to delude the people, and to bring them from depending only on God.

14.text: They will utterly perish, and no part of them remain.

15.text: They will flee everyone to that place, which he thought by his speculations to be most sure: but that will deceive them.

1.text: He detects their hypocrisy who claimed to be Israelites, but were not so.
Meaning, the fountain and stock.

2.text: They make a show, as though they would have no other God.

3.text: He shows that they could not accuse him in anything, as he had performed whatever he had promised.

4.text: I have done for you more than I promised, that your stubbornness and impudency might have been overcome.

5.text: How you should be delivered out of Babylon.

6.text: Will you not acknowledge my blessing, and declare it to others?

7.text: Showing that man’s arrogancy is the reason God does not declare all things at once, lest they should attribute this knowledge to their own wisdom.

8.text: From the time that I brought you of Egypt: for that deliverance was as the birth of the Church.

9.text: As it was my free mercy that I chose you: so it is my free mercy that must save you.

10.text: For I had respect to your weakness and infirmity: for in silver there is some pureness, but in us there is nothing but dross.
I took you out of the furnace where you would have been consumed.

11.text: God joins the salvation of his with his own honour: so that they cannot perish, but his glory would be diminished, as in De 32:27 .
Read Isaiah 42:8 .

12.text: Read Isaiah 41:4 .

13.text: To obey me, and to do whatever I command them.

14.text: Meaning, Cyrus, whom he had chosen to destroy Babylon.

16.text: Since the time that I declared myself to your fathers.
Thus the Prophet speaks for himself, and to assure them of these things.

17.text: What things will do you good.

19.text: That is, the prosperous estate of Israel.

20.text: After he had forewarned them of their captivity and of the reason for it, he shows them the great joy that will come of their deliverance.

21.text: He shows that it will be as easy to deliver them, as he did their fathers out of Egypt.

22.text: Thus he speaks that the wicked hypocrites should not abuse God’s promise, in whom was neither faith nor repentance, as in Isaiah 57:21

1.text: This is spoken in the person of Christ, to assure the faithful that these promises should come to pass: for they were all made in him and in him would be performed.
This is meant of the time that Christ would be manifested to the world, as in Psalms 2:7 .

2.text: By the sword and shaft, he signifies the virtue and efficacy of Christ’s doctrine.
God has taken me to his protection and defence: this chiefly is meant of Christ, and may also be applied to the ministers of his word.

3.text: By Israel is meant Christ, and all the body of the faithful, as the members and their head.

4.text: Thus Christ in his members complains that his labour and preaching take no effect, yet he is contented that his doings are approved by God.

5.text: Though the Jews refuse my doctrine, yet God will approve my ministry.

6.text: To declare my gospel to the Gentiles, as in Isaiah 42:6 , Acts 13:47 , Lu 2:32 .

7.text: Meaning, the Jews whom tyrants kept in bondage.
The benefit of their deliverance will be so great, that great and small will acknowledge it, and revere God for it.

8.text: Thus he speaks of his Church when he would show his mercy toward it, 2 Corinthians 6:2 .
Meaning, Christ alone.
Signifying that before Christ renewed the earth by his word, there is nothing but confusion and disorder.

9.text: To them who are in the prison of sin and death.
Being in Christ’s protection, they will be safe against all dangers, and free from fear of the enemies.

10.text: Meaning, that there would be nothing in their way from Babylon that would hinder or hurt them: but this is accomplished spiritually. Isaiah 49:12
Meaning, the south country, so that Christ will deliver his from all the parts of the world.

13.text: Read Isaiah 44:23 .

14.text: He objects what the faithful might say in their long affliction and answers to comfort them with a most proper comparison and full of consolation.

16.text: Because I would not forget you.
Meaning, the good order of policy and discipline.

17.text: I have continual care to build you up again and to destroy your enemies.

18.text: He shows what are the ornaments of the Church: to have many children, who are assembled by the word of God, and governed by his Spirit.

22.text: He shows that Christ will not only gather this great number from the Jews but also from the Gentiles.

23.text: Meaning, that kings will be converted to the gospel, and bestow their power and authority for the preservation of the Church.
Being joined with the Church, they will humble themselves to Christ their head, and give him all honour.

24.text: He makes this as an objection as though the Chaldeans were strong, and had them in just possession.

25.text: This is the answer to their objection, that no one is stronger than the Lord, neither has a more just title to them.

26.text: I will cause them to destroy one another as in Jud 7:22, 2 Chronicles 20:22 , Isaiah 19:2 .

1.text: Meaning, that he has not forsaken her, but through her own opportunity as in Hosea 2:2 .
Who would declare that I have cut her off: meaning, that they could show no one.
Signifying, that he sold them not for any debt or poverty, but that they sold themselves to sins to buy their own lusts and pleasures.

2.text: He came by his prophets and ministers, but they would not believe their doctrine and convert.
Am I not able to help you, as I have helped your fathers of old, when I dried up the Red sea, and killed the fish in the rivers, and also afterward in Jordan?

3.text: As I did in Egypt in token of my displeasure, Exodus 10:21 .

4.text: The prophet represents here the person and charge of them that are justly called to the ministry by God’s word.
To him that is oppressed by affliction and misery.
As they who are taught, and made meet by him.

6.text: I did not shrink from God for any persecution or calamity. By which he shows that the true ministers of God can look for no other recompense of the wicked, but after this sort, and also that is their comfort.

10.text: Showing that it is a rare thing that any should obey correctly God’s true ministers, though they labour to bring them from hell to heaven.

11.text: You have sought consolation by your own devises, and have refused the light and consolation which God has offered: therefore you will remain in sorrow and not be comforted.

1.text: He comforts the Church, that they would not be discouraged for their small number.
That is, to Abraham, of whom you were begotten, and to Sarah of whom we were born.

3.text: As plentiful as paradise, Genesis 2:8-9 .

4.text: I will rule and govern my Church by my word and doctrine.

5.text: The time that I will accomplish my promise.
My power and strength.

6.text: Forewarns them of the horrible changes and mutations of all things, and how he will preserve his church in the midst of all these dangers.

9.text: He puts them in remembrance of his great benefit for their deliverance out of Egypt, that by it they might learn to trust in him constantly.
Meaning, Egypt, Psalms 87:4 .
That is, Pharaoh, Ezekiel 29:3 .

11.text: From Babylon.

14.text: He comforts them by the short time of their banishment: for in seventy years they were restored and the greatest empire of the world destroyed.

16.text: Meaning, of Isaiah and of all true ministers who are defended by his protection.
That all things may be restored in heaven and earth, Ephesians 1:10 .

17.text: You have been justly punished and sufficiently as Isaiah 40:2 and this punishment in the elect is by measure, and according as God gives grace to hear it: but in the reprobate it is the just vengeance of God to drive them to an insensibleness and madness, as Jeremiah 25:15-16 .

19.text: Of which the one is outward as of the things that come to the body, as war, and famine and the other is inward, and belongs to the mind: that is, to be without comfort: therefore he says "How will you be comforted?"

21.text: But with trouble and fear.

1.text: No wicked tyrant, who will subvert God’s true religion and oppress the conscience.

2.text: Put off the garments of sorrow and heaviness and put on the apparel of joy and gladness.

3.text: The Babylonians paid nothing to me for you: therefore I will take you again without ransom.

4.text: When Jacob went there in times of famine.

The Egyptians might pretend some reason to oppress my people because they went there and remained among them, but the Assyrians have no title to excuse their tyranny by, and therefore I will punish them more than I did the Egyptians.

5.text: That is, by the wicked, who think that I have no power to deliver them.

7.text: Signifying that the joy and good tidings of their deliverance would make their affliction in the mean time more easy: but this is chiefly meant of the spiritual joy, as in Nahum 1:15 , Romans 10:15 .

8.text: The prophets who are your watchmen will publish your deliverance: this was begun under Zerubbabel, Ezra and Nehemiah, but was accomplished under Christ.

10.text: As ready to smite his enemies and to deliver his people.

11.text: He warns the faithful not to pollute themselves with the superstitions of the Babylonians, as Isaiah 48:20 , 2 Corinthians 6:17 .

For the time is at hand that the priests and Levites chiefly (and so by them all the people, who will be as the Levites in this office) will carry home vessels of the temple which Nebuchadnezzar had taken away.

12.text: As your fathers did out of Egypt.

13.text: Meaning Christ, by whom our spiritual deliverance would be wrought of which this was a sign.

14.text: In the corrupt judgment of man, Christ in his person was not valued.

15.text: He will spread his word through many nations.
In sign of reverence, and as being astonished at his excellency.
By the preaching of the gospel.

1.text: The prophet shows that very few will receive their preaching from Christ, and from their deliverance by him, John 12:38 , Romans 10:16 .
Meaning, that no one can believe but whose hearts God touches with the virtue of his Holy Spirit.

2.text: The beginning of Christ’s kingdom will be small and contemptible in the sight of man, but it will grow wonderfully and flourish before God.
Read Isaiah 11:1 .

3.text: Which was by God’s singular providence for the comfort of sinners, Hebrews 4:15 .

4.text: That is, the punishment due to our sins, for which he has both suffered and made satisfaction, Matthew 8:17 , 1 Peter 2:24 .
We judge evil, thinking that he was punished for his own sins, and not for ours.

5.text: He was chastised for our reconciliation, 1 Corinthians 15:3 .

6.text: Meaning, the punishment of our iniquity, and not the fault itself.

7.text: But willingly and patiently obeyed his father’s appointment, Matthew 26:63 , Acts 8:32 .

8.text: From the cross and grave, after that he was condemned.
Though he died for sin, yet after his resurrection he will live forever and this his death is to restore life to his members, Romans 6:9 .

9.text: God the Father delivered him into the hands of the wicked, and to the powers of the world to do with him what they would.

10.text: Christ by offering up himself will give life to his Church, and so cause them to live with him forever.

11.text: That is, the fruit and effect of his labour, which is the salvation of his Church.
Christ will justify by faith through his word, while Moses could not justify by the law.

12.text: Because he humbled himself, therefore he will be extolled to glory, Philippians 2:7-12 .
That is, of all that believe in him.

1.text: After he has declared the death of Christ, he speaks to the Church, because it would feel the fruit of the same, and calls her barren, because in the captivity she was a widow without hope to have any children.

The Church in this her affliction and captivity will bring forth more children, than when she was free, or this may be spoken by admiration, considering the great number that would come from her. Her deliverance under Cyrus was as her childhood, and therefore this was accomplished when she came of age, which was under the gospel.

2.text: Signifying that for the great number of children that God would give her, she would seem to lack room to lodge them.

4.text: The afflictions which you suffered at the beginning.
When you were refused for your sins, Isaiah 50:1 .

5.text: That regenerated you by his Holy Spirit.
His glory will shine through the whole world, which seemed before to be shut up in Judea.

6.text: As a wife who was forsaken in your youth.

9.text: As sure as the promise that I made to Noah, that the waters would no longer overflow the earth.

11.text: By this he declares the excellent estate of the Church under Christ.

13.text: By the hearing of his word and inward moving of his spirit.

14.text: In stability and sureness, so that it will stand forever.

15.text: And therefore will not prevail.
Meaning, the domestic enemies of the Church, as are the hypocrites.

16.text: Signifying by this that man can do nothing, but so far as God gives power: for seeing that all are his creatures, he must govern and guide them.

1.text: Christ by proposing his graces and gifts to his Church, exempts the hypocrites who are full with their imagined works, and the Epicureans who are full with their worldly lusts, and so do not thirst after these waters.
Signifying that God’s benefits cannot be bought for money.
By waters, wine, milk and bread, he means all things necessary to the spiritual life, as these are necessary to this corporal life.

2.text: He reproves their ingratitude, who refuse those things that God offers willingly, and in the mean time spare neither cost nor labour to obtain those which are not profitable.
You will be fed abundantly.

3.text: The same covenant which through my mercy I ratified and confirmed to David, that it would be eternal, 2 Samuel 7:13 , Acts 13:34 .

4.text: Meaning Christ, of whom David was a figure.

5.text: That is, the Gentiles, who before you did not receive to be your people.

6.text: When he offers himself by the preaching of his word.

7.text: By this he shows that repentance must be joined with faith, and how we cannot call on God correctly, unless the fruits of our faith appear.

8.text: Although you are not soon reconciled one to another and judge me by yourselves, yet I am easy to be reconciled, yea, I offer my mercies to you.

11.text: If these small things have their effect, as daily experience shows much more will my promise which I have made and confirmed, bring to pass the things which I have spoken for your deliverance.

12.text: Read Isaiah 44:23 ; Isaiah 49:13

13.text: To set forth his glory.
Of God’s deliverance, and that he will never forsake his Church.

1.text: God shows what he requires of them after he has delivered them: that is, the works of charity by which true faith is declared.
Which I will declare toward you, and pour into your hearts by my Spirit.

2.text: Under the Sabbath he comprehends the whole service of God and true religion.

3.text: Let no one think himself unfit to receive the graces of the Lord: for the Lord will take away all impediments, and will forsake no one who will keep his true religion, and believe in him.

5.text: Meaning, in his Church.
They will be called after my people, and be of the same religion: yea, under Christ the dignity of the faithful will be greater than the Jews were at that time.

7.text: By this he means the spiritual service of God, to whom the faithful offer continual thanksgiving, yea themselves and all that they have, as a lively and acceptable sacrifice.
Not only for the Jews, but for all others, Matthew 21:13 .

9.text: Meaning, the enemies of the Church, as the Babylonians, Assyrians, etc thus he speaks to scare the hypocrites and to assure the faithful that when this comes they may know it was told to them before.

10.text: He shows that this affliction will come through the fault of the governors, prophets and pastors, whose ignorance, negligence, greed and obstinacy provoked God’s wrath against them.

12.text: We are well yet, and to morrow will be better: therefore let us not fear the plagues before they come: thus the wicked contemned the admonition and exhortations which were made to them in the Name of God.

1.text: From the plague that is at hand, and also because God will punish the wicked.

2.text: The soul of the righteous will be in joy, and their body will rest in the grave to the time of the resurrection, because they walked before the Lord.

3.text: He threatens the wicked hypocrites, who under the pretence of the name of God’s people, derided God’s word and his promises: boasting openly that they were the children of Abraham, but because they were not faithful and obedient as Abraham was, he calls them bastards and the children of sorcerers, who forsook God, and fled to wicked means for comfort.

5.text: Read Leviticus 18:21 , 2 Kings 23:10 .

6.text: Meaning every place was polluted with their idolatry: or every fair stone they found they made into an idol.
In the sacrifices which you offering before these idols thought you served God.

7.text: That is, your altars in an open place, like an impudent harlot, that cares not for the sight of her husband.

8.text: Instead of setting up the word of God in the open places on the posts and doors to have it in remembrance, De 6:9,27:1 you have set up signs and marks of your idolatry in every place.
That is, increased your idolatry more and more.

9.text: You sought the favour of the Assyrians by gifts and presents to help you against the Egyptians and when they failed you sought the Babylonians, and more and more tormented yourself.

10.text: Although you saw all your labours to be in vain, yet would you never acknowledge your fault and leave off.
He derides their unprofitable diligence, who thought to have made all sure, and yet were deceived.

11.text: Broken promises with me.
Meaning, that the wicked abuse God’s leniency, and grow to further wickedness.

12.text: That is, your naughtiness, idolatry and impiety which the wicked call God’s service: thus he derides their obstinacy.

13.text: Meaning, the Assyrians and others, whose help they looked for.

14.text: God will say to Darius and Cyrus.

16.text: I will not use my power against frail man, whose life is but a blast.

17.text: That is, for the vices and faults of the people, which is here meant by covetousness.

18.text: Though they were obstinate, yet I did not withdraw my mercy from them.

19.text: That is, I frame the speech and words of my messengers who will bring peace.
As well to him that is in captivity as to him that remains at home.

20.text: Their evil conscience always torments them and therefore they can never have rest, Isaiah 48:22 .

1.text: The Lord thus speaks to the prophet willing him to use all diligence and severity to rebuke the hypocrites.

2.text: They will seem to worship me and have outward holiness.

3.text: He sets forth the malice and disdain of the hypocrites, who grudge against God, if their works are not accepted.
Thus he convinces the hypocrites by the second table and by their duty toward their neighbour, that they have neither faith nor religion.

4.text: So long as you use contention and oppression, your fasting and prayers will not be heard.

6.text: That you leave off all your extortions.

7.text: For in him you see yourself as in a mirror.

8.text: That is, the prosperous estate with which God will bless you.
The testimony of your goodness will appear before God and man.

9.text: By which is meant all manner of injury.

10.text: That is, have compassion on their miseries.
Your adversity will be turned into prosperity.

12.text: Signifying that of the Jews would come such as would build again the ruins of Jerusalem and Judea: but chiefly this is meant of the spiritual Jerusalem, whose builders were the Apostles.

13.text: If you refrain yourself from your wicked works.

3.text: Read Isaiah 1:15 .

4.text: All men wink at the injuries and oppressions and none go about to remedy them.
According to their wicked devices, they hurt their neighbours.

5.text: Whatever comes from them is poison, and brings death.
They are profitable to no purpose.

9.text: That is, God’s vengeance to punish our enemies.
God’s protection to defend us.

10.text: We are altogether destitute of counsel, and can find no end to our miseries.

11.text: We express our sorrows by outward signs, some more and some less.

12.text: This confession is general to the Church to obtain remission of sins, and the prophets did not exempt themselves from the same.

13.text: That is, against our neighbours.

14.text: There is neither justice nor uprightness among men.

15.text: The wicked will destroy him.

16.text: Meaning, to do justice, and to remedy the things that were so far out of order.
That is, his Church or his arm helped itself and did not seek aid from any other.

17.text: Signifying that God has all means at hand to deliver his Church and to punish their enemies.

18.text: That is, your enemies who dwell in various places, and beyond the sea.

19.text: He shows that there will be great affliction in the Church, but God will always deliver his.

20.text: By which he declares that the true deliverance from sin and Satan belongs to none but to the children of God, whom he justifies.

21.text: Because the doctrine is made profitable by the virtue of the Spirit, he joins the one with the other, and promises to give them both to his Church for ever.

1.text: The time of your prosperity and happiness: while speaking of Babylon, he commanded her to go down, Isaiah 47:1 .

2.text: Signifying, that all men are in darkness till God gives them the light of his Spirit, and that this light shines to no one, but to those that are in his Church.

3.text: Meaning, that Judea would be as the morning star, and that the Gentiles would receive light from her.

4.text: An infinite number from all countries as in Isaiah 49:18 .

5.text: For joy, as the heart is drawn in for sorrow.

6.text: Meaning, that everyone will honour the Lord with that with which he is able: Signifying that it is no true serving of God unless we offer ourselves to serve his glory, and all that we have.

7.text: That is the Arabians, that have great abundance of cattle.
Because the altar was a figure of Christ, Hebrews 13:10 , he shows that nothing can be acceptable to him, which is not offered to him by this altar, who was both the offering and the altar itself.

8.text: Showing what great number will come to the Church, and with what great diligence and zeal.

9.text: The Gentiles that are now enemies, will become friends and set forth the Church.

10.text: Meaning Cyrus and his successors, but chiefly this is accomplished in them that serve Christ, being converted by his gospel.

12.text: He shows that God has given all power and authority here in earth for the use of his Church, and that they who will not serve and profit the same will be destroyed.

13.text: There is nothing so excellent which will not serve the needs of the Church.
Signifying that God’s majesty is not included in the temple, which is but the place for his feet, that we may learn to rise to the heavens.

14.text: To worship their head Christ, by obeying his doctrine.

16.text: Both high and low will be ready to help and comfort you.

17.text: Your governors will love you, and seek your wealth and prosperity.

18.text: Meaning not an earthly happiness, but spiritual, which is fulfilled in Christ’s kingdom.

19.text: Signifying that all worldly means will cease, and that Christ will be all in all, as in Revelation 21:23 ; Revelation 22:5 .

21.text: The children of the Church.

22.text: Meaning, that the Church would be miraculously multiplied.

1.text: Thus belongs to all the prophets and ministers of God, but chiefly to Christ, of whose abundant graces everyone receives according as it pleases him to distribute.
To them that are lively touched with the feeling of their sins.
Who are in the bondage of sin.

2.text: The time when it pleased God to show his good favour to man, which Paul calls the fulness of time, Galatians 4:4 .
For when God delivers his Church, he punishes his enemies.

3.text: Which was the sign of mourning.
Trees that bring forth good fruits, as in Matthew 3:8 .

4.text: That is, for a long time.

5.text: They will be ready to serve you in all your needs.

6.text: This is accomplished in the time of Christ, by whom all the faithful are made priests and kings, 1 Peter 2:9 , Revelation 1:6 ; Revelation 5:10 .
Read Isa 6:11:16 .

7.text: Abundant recompence as this word is used, Isaiah 40:2 .
That is, the Jews.
That is, of the Gentiles.
While the Gentiles had dominion over the Jews in times past, now they will have double authority over them and possess twice as much.

8.text: I will not receive their offerings who are extortioners, deceivers, hypocrites or that deprive me of my glory.

9.text: That is, of the Church.

10.text: He shows what will be the affection, when they feel their deliverance.

1.text: The prophet says that he will never cease to declare to the people the good tidings of their deliverance.
Till they have full deliverance: and this the prophet speaks to encourage all other ministers to the setting forth of God’s mercies toward his Church.

2.text: You will have a more excellent fame than you have had till now.

3.text: He will value you as dear and precious as a king does his crown.

4.text: You will no longer be contemned as a woman forsaken by her husband.
That it may be replenished with children.

5.text: As they confess one faith and religion with you, they are in the same bond of marriage with you, and they are called the children of the Church, as Christ makes her plentiful to bring forth children to him.

6.text: Prophets, pastors and ministers.
He exhorts the ministers never to cease to call on God by prayer for the deliverance of his Church and to teach others to do the same.

7.text: For the restoration of which all the world will praise him.

10.text: Signifying the great number that would come to the Church, and what means he would prepare for the restitution of the same, as in Isaiah 57:14 .

11.text: You prophets and ministers show the people of this their deliverance: which was chiefly meant of our salvation by Christ, Zechariah 9:9 , Matthew 21:5 .
He will have all power to bring his purpose to pass, as in Isaiah 40:10 .

12.text: That is, one over whom God has had a singular care to recover her when she was lost.

1.text: This prophecy is against the Idumeans and enemies who persecuted the Church, on whom God will take vengeance, and is here set forth all bloody after he has destroyed them in Bozrah, the chief city of the Idumeans: for these were their greatest enemies,and under the title of circumcision and the kindred of Abraham.
God answers them that asked this question, "Who is this?" etc. and says "You see now performed in deed the vengeance which my prophets threatened."

2.text: Another question, to which the Lord answers.

4.text: Showing that when God punishes his enemies, it is for the profit and deliverance of his Church.

5.text: God shows that he has no need of man’s help for the deliverance of his, and though men refuse to do their duty through negligence and ingratitude, yet he himself will deliver his Church, and punish the enemies, Isaiah 59:16 .

6.text: I will so astonish them and make them so giddy that they will not know which way to go.

7.text: The prophet speaks this to move the people to remember God’s benefits in times past, that they may be confirmed in their troubles.

8.text: For I chose them to be mine, that they should be holy, and not deceive my expectation.

9.text: He bore their afflictions and griefs as though they had been his own.
Which was a witness of God’s presence, and this may be referred to Christ, to whom belongs the office of salvation.

11.text: That is, the people of Israel being afflicted, called to mind God’s benefits, which he had bestowed on their fathers in times past.
Meaning, Moses.
That is, in Moses that he might well govern the people: some refer this giving of the spirit to the people.

13.text: Peaceably and gentle, as a horse is led to his pasture.

15.text: Having declared God’s benefits showed to their forefathers, he turned himself to God by prayer, desiring him to continue the same graces toward them.
Your great affection, which you bore for us.
Meaning, from the whole body of the Church.

16.text: Though Abraham would refuse us to be his children, yet you will not refuse to be our father.

17.text: By taking away the Holy Spirit from us, by whom we were governed, and so for our ingratitude delivered us up to our own concupiscence, and punished sin by sin according to your just judgment.
Meaning, for the covenant’s sake made to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob his servants.

18.text: That is, in respect to the promise, which is perpetual: even though they had now possessed the land of Canaan for 1400 years: and thus they lament, to move God rather to remember his covenant, than to punish their sins.

1.text: The prophet continues his prayer, desiring God to declare his love toward his Church by miracles and mighty power, as he did in mount Sinai.

2.text: Meaning, the rain, hail, fire, thunder and lightning.

4.text: Paul uses the same kind of admiration, 1 Corinthians 2:9 marvelling at God’s great benefit showed to his Church, by the preaching of the gospel.

5.text: You showed favour toward our fathers, when they trusted in you and walked after your commandments.
They considered your great mercies.
That is, in your mercies, which he calls the ways of the Lord.
You will have pity on us.

6.text: We are justly punished and brought into captivity, because we have provoked you to anger, and though we would excuse ourselves, yet our righteousness, and best virtues are before you as vile cloths, or (as some read) like the menstruous cloths of a woman.

8.text: Even though O Lord by your just judgment you may utterly destroy us as the potter may his pot, yet we appeal to your mercies, by which it has pleased you to adopt us to be your children.

9.text: For so the flesh judges when God does not immediately send comfort.

10.text: Who were dedicated to your service, and to call on your Name.

11.text: In which we rejoiced and worshipped you.

12.text: That is, at the contempt of your own glory? Though our sins have deserved this, yet you will not permit your glory thus to be diminished.

1.text: Meaning, the Gentiles who know not God, would seek him, when he had moved their heart with his Holy Spirit, Romans 10:20 .

2.text: He shows the reason for the rejection of the Jews, because they would not obey him or any admonition of his prophets, by whom he called them continually and stretch out his hand to draw them.
He shows that to delight in our own fantasies is the declining from God and the beginning of all superstitions and idolatry.

3.text: Which were dedicated to idols.
Meaning their altars, which he thus named by contempt.

4.text: To consult with spirits, and to conjure devils, which was forbidden.
Which was contrary to God’s commandment, Leviticus 11:7 , De 14:8 .

5.text: He shows that hypocrisy is always joined with pride and contempt of others.
Their punishment will never have an end.

6.text: So that the remembrance of it cannot be forgotten.

7.text: Will be both punished together: and this declares how the children are punished for their fathers faults, that is, when the same faults or like are found in them.

8.text: That is, it is profitable: meaning that God will not destroy the faithful branches of his vineyard, when he destroys the rotten stocks, that is, the hypocrites.

10.text: Which was a plentiful place in Judea to feed sheep, as Achor was for cattle.

11.text: By the multitude and number he means their innumerable idols of whom they thought they could never have enough.

12.text: Seeing you cannot number your gods, I will number you with the sword.
By my prophets, whom you would not obey.

13.text: By these words, eat and drink, he means the blessed life of the faithful, who have always had consolation and full contentment of all things in their God, though sometimes they lack these corporal things.

15.text: Meaning, that he would call the Gentiles, who would abhor even the very name of the Jews for their infidelities sake.
Than by the name of the Jews.

16.text: By blessing, and by swearing is meant the praising of God for his benefits, and the true worshipping of him, who will not be only in Judea, but through all the world.
I will no longer permit my Church to be desolate as in times past.

17.text: I will so altar and change the state of my church, that it will seem to dwell in a new world.

20.text: Meaning, in this wonderful restoration of the Church there would be no weakness of youth, nor infirmities of age, but all would be fresh and flourishing: and this is accomplished in the heavenly Jerusalem, when all sins will cease, and the tears will be wiped away.
By which he shows that the infidels and unrepentant sinners have no part of this benediction.

21.text: He proposes to the faithful the blessings which are contained in the law, and so under temporal things comprehends the spiritual promises.

25.text: Read Isaiah 11:6 .

1.text: My majesty is so great, that it fills both heaven and earth, and therefore cannot be included in a temple like an idol, condemning by this their main confidence which trusted in the temple and sacrifices.

2.text: Seeing that both the temple and the things in it, with the sacrifices were made and done by his appointment, he shows that he has no need of it, and that he can be without them, see Geneva " Psalms 50:10 ".
To him that is humble and pure in heart, who receives my doctrine with reverence and fear.

3.text: Because the Jews thought themselves holy by offering their sacrifices, and in the mean season had neither faith or repentance, God shows that he no less detests these ceremonies than he does the sacrifices of the heathen, who offered men, dogs and swine to their idols, which things were expressly forbidden in the law.

4.text: I will discover their wickedness and hypocrisy, with which they think to blind my eyes to all the world.
