5.text: He encourages the faithful by promising to destroy their enemies, who pretended to be as brethren, but were hypocrites, and hated them that feared God.

7.text: Meaning, that the restoration of the church would be so sudden and contrary to all men’s opinions as when a woman is delivered before she looked for it, and without pain in travail.

8.text: This will pass the capacity of man to see such a multitude that will come up at once, meaning under the preaching of the gospel of which they who came out of Babylon were a sign.

9.text: Declaring by this that as by his power and providence women travailed and delivered so he gives power to bring forth the Church at his appointed time.

11.text: That is may rejoice for all the blessings that God bestows on his Church.

12.text: I will give her happiness and prosperity in great abundance.
Read Isaiah 60:16 .
You will be cherished as her dearly beloved children.

14.text: You will have new strength and new beauty.

15.text: This vengeance God began to execute at the destruction of Babylon and has always continued it against the enemies of his Church, and will do till the last day, which will be the accomplishment of it.

17.text: Meaning, the hypocrites.
By which are meant them that maliciously transgressed the law, by eating beasts forbidden, even to the mouse which nature abhors.

18.text: The Gentiles will be partakers of that glory, which before I showed to the Jews.

19.text: I will make these that I chose, that they perish not with the rest of the infidels: by which he alludes to the marking of the posts of his people, whom he preserved, Exodus 12:7 .
I will scatter the rest of the Jews, who escaped destruction, into various nations.
That is, Cecilia.
Meaning Africa.
That is Lydia, or Asia minor.
Signifying the Parthians.
Italy.
Greece.
Meaning, the apostles, disciples and others who he first chose of the Jews to preach to the Gentiles.

20.text: That is the Gentiles, who by faith will be made the children of Abraham as you are.
By which he means that no necessary means will want, when God will call the Gentiles to the knowledge of the gospel.

21.text: That is, of the Gentiles, as he did Luke, Timothy and Titus first, and others after to preach his word.

22.text: By this he signifies the kingdom of Christ in which his Church will be renewed, and where before there were appointed seasons to sacrifice in this there will be one continual Sabbath, so that all times and seasons will be meet.

24.text: As he who declared the happiness that will be within the Church for the comfort of the godly, so does he show what horrible calamity will come to the wicked, that are out of the Church.
Meaning, a continual torment of conscience, which will always gnaw them, and never permit them to be at rest, Mr 9:44 .
This is the just recompense for the wicked, who contemning God and his word, will be by God’s just judgments abhorred by all his creatures.

1.text: That is, the sermons and prophecies.
Who is thought to be he that found the book of the law under king Josiah, 2 Kings 22:8 .
This was a city about three miles from Jerusalem and belonged to the priests, the sons of Aaron, Joshua 21:18 .

2.text: This is spoken to confirm his calling and office, as he did not presume of himself to preach and prophecy, but was called to it by God.

3.text: Meaning the nephew of Josiah: for Jehoahaz was his father, who reigned but three months, and therefore is not mentioned, nor is Jehoiakim that reigned no longer.
Of the eleventh year of Zedekiah, who was also called Mattaniah, and at this time the Jews were carried away into Babylon by Nebuchadnezzar.

5.text: The scripture uses this manner of speech to declare that God has appointed his minsters to their offices before they were born, as in Isaiah 49:1 , Galatians 1:15 .
For Jeremiah did not only prophecy against the Jews, but also against the Egyptians, Babylonians, Moabites and other nations.

6.text: Considering the great judgments of God which according to his threatening would come on the world, he was moved with a certain compassion on the one hand to pity them that would thus perish, and on the other hand by the infirmity of man’s nature, knowing how hard a thing it was to enterprise such a charge, as in Isaiah 6:11 , Exodus 3:21 ; Exodus 4:1 .

9.text: Which declares that God makes them meet and assures them, whom he calls to set forth his glory, giving them all means necessary for the same, Exodus 4:12 , Isaiah 6:7 .

10.text: He shows what is the authority of God’s true ministers, who by his word have power to bear down whatever lifts itself up against God: and to plant and assure the humble and such as give themselves to the obedience of God’s word, 2 Corinthians 10:4-5 , Hebrews 4:12 , and these are the keys which Christ has left to loose and bind, Matthew 18:18 .

11.text: He joins the sign with the word, for a more ample confirmation: signifying by the rod of the almond tree, which first buds, the hasty coming of the Babylonians against the Jews.

13.text: Signifying that the Chaldeans and Assyrians would be as a pot to seethe the Jews who boiled in their pleasures and lust.

14.text: Syria and Assyria were northward in respect to Jerusalem, which was the Chaldeans dominion.

16.text: I will give them charge and power to execute my vengeance against the idolaters who have forsaken me for their idols.

17.text: Which declares that God’s vengeance is prepared against them who do not execute their duty faithfully, either for fear of man, or for any other reason, 1 Corinthians 9:16 .

18.text: Signifying on the one hand that the more that Satan and the world rage against God’s ministers, the more present will he be to help them, Joshua 1:5 , Hebrews 13:5 and on the other hand, that they are utterly unfit to serve God in his Church, who are afraid and do not resist wickedness, whatever danger depend on it, Isaiah 50:7 , Ezekiel 3:8 .

2.text: According to that grace and favour which I showed you from the beginning, when I first chose you to be my people, and married you to myself, Ezekiel 16:8 .
When I had delivered you out of Egypt.

3.text: Chosen above all others to serve the Lord only and the first offered to the Lord of all other nations.
Whoever challenged this people, or else annoyed them, was punished.

5.text: That is, fallen to vile idolatry.
Altogether given to vanity, and are become blind and insensible as the idols that they serve.

6.text: Where for lack of all things needed for life, you could look for nothing every hour but present death.

7.text: By your idolatry and wicked manners, Psalms 78:58 ; Psalms 106:38 .

8.text: They did not teach the people to seek after God.
As the scribes, who would have expounded the law to the people.
Meaning, the princes and ministers: signifying, that all estates were corrupt.
That is, spoke vain things, and brought the people from the true worship of God to serve idols: for by Baal, which was the chief idol of the Moabites, are meant all idols.

9.text: Signifying that he would not as he might, straightway condemn them, but shows them by evident examples their great ingratitude that they might be ashamed and repent.

10.text: Meaning, the Grecians and Italians.
To Arabia.

11.text: That is, God who is their glory, and who makes them glorious above all other people, reproving the Jews that they were less diligent to serve the true God, than were the idolaters to honour their vanities.
Meaning the idols who were their destruction, Psalms 106:36 .

12.text: He shows that the insensible creatures abhor this vile ingratitude, and as it were tremble for fear of God’s great judgments against the same.

13.text: Signifying that when men forsake God’s word, which is the fountain of life, they reject God himself, and so fall to their own inventions, and vain confidence, and procure to themselves destruction, Jonah 2:8 , Zechariah 10:2 .

14.text: Have I ordered them like servants and not like dearly beloved children? Exodus 4:22 therefore it is their fault only, if the enemy spoil them.

15.text: The Babylonians, Chaldeans, and Assyrians.
Not one will be left to dwell there.

16.text: That is, the Egyptians, for these were two great cities in Egypt.
Have grievously vexed you at various times.

17.text: Showing that God would have still led them correctly, if they would have followed him.

18.text: That is, Euphrates.

19.text: Meaning, that the wicked are insensible, till the punishment for their sin waken them as in Jeremiah 2:26 , Isaiah 3:9 .

20.text: When I delivered you out of Egypt, Exodus 19:8 , De 5:27, Joshua 24:16 , Ezra 10:12 , Hebrews 8:6 .

22.text: Though you use all the purifications and ceremonies of the law, you cannot escape punishment.

23.text: Meaning that hypocrites deny that they worship the idols, but that they honour God in them, and therefore they call their doings God’s service.
He compares the idolaters to these beasts, because they never cease running to and fro: for both valleys and hills are full of their idolatry.

24.text: He compares the idolaters to a wild ass: for she can never be tamed nor yet wearied: for as she runs she can take her wind at every opportunity.

That is, when she is with foal, and therefore the hunters wait their time: so though you cannot be turned back now from your idolatry, yet when your iniquity will be at the fall, God will meet with you.

25.text: By this he warns them that they should not go into strange countries to seek help: for they should but spend their labour, and hurt themselves, which is here meant by the bare foot and thirst, Isaiah 57:10 .

26.text: As a thief will not acknowledge his fault, till he is taken with the deed, and ready to be punished, so they will not confess their idolatry, till the plagues due to the same light on them.

27.text: Meaning, that idolaters rob God of his honour: and where as he has taught to call him the father of all flesh, they attribute this title to their idols.

28.text: You thought that your gods of blocks and stones could have helped you, because they were many in number and present in every place: but now let us see whether either the multitude or their presence can deliver you from my plague, Jeremiah 11:13 .

29.text: As though I did you injury in punishing you, seeing that your faults are so evident.

30.text: That is, you have killed your prophets, that exhorted you to repentance, as Zechariah, Isaiah, etc.

31.text: Have I not given them abundance of all things?
But will trust in our own power and policy.

33.text: With strangers.

34.text: The prophets and the faithful are slain in every corner of your country.

36.text: For the Assyrians had taken away the ten tribes out of Israel and destroyed Judah even to Jerusalem: and the Egyptians slew Josiah, and vexed the Jews in various ways.

37.text: In sign of lamentation, as in 2 Samuel 13:19 .

1.text: According as it is written, De 24:4 .
If he take such a one to wife again.
That is, with idols, and with them whom you have put your confidence in.
And I will not cast you off, but receive you, according to my mercy.

2.text: Who dwells in tent and waits for them that pass by to rob them.

3.text: As God threatened by his law, De 28:24 .
You would never be ashamed of your acts and repent: and this impudency is common to idolaters, who will not cease, though they are openly convicted.

4.text: He shows that the wicked in their miseries will cry to God and use outward prayer as the godly do, but because they do not turn from their evil, they are not heard, Isaiah 58:3-4 .

6.text: Meaning the ten tribes.

8.text: And gave her into the hands of the Assyrians.

9.text: The Hebrew word may either signify lightness and wantonness, or noise and brute.

10.text: Judah pretended for a time that she returned, as under Josiah and other good kings, but she was never truly touched, or wholly reformed, as appeared when opportunity was offered by any wicked prince.

11.text: Israel has not declared herself as wicked as Judah, who yet has had more admonitions and examples to call her to repentance.

12.text: While the Israelites were now kept in captivity by the Assyrians, to whom he promises mercy, if they will repent.

13.text: There was no way which you did not hunt to seek after the idols, and to go on a pilgrimage.

16.text: This is to be understood of the coming of Christ: for then they will not seek the Lord by ceremonies, and all figures will cease.

17.text: Meaning, the Church, where the Lord will be present to the world’s end, Matthew 28:20 .

18.text: Where they are now in captivity.

20.text: The Hebrew word signifies a friend or companion, and here may be taken for a husband, as it is used also in Hosea 3:1 .

21.text: Signifying, that God, whom they had forsaken, would bring their enemies to them, who would lead them captive, and make them to cry and lament.

22.text: This is spoken in the person of Israel to the shame of Judah, who stayed so long to turn to God.

24.text: For their idolatry God’s vengeance has light on them and theirs.

25.text: They justify not themselves, or say that they would follow their fathers, but condemn their wicked doings and desire forgiveness for the same, as in Ezra 9:7 , Psalms 106:6 , Isaiah 64:6 .

1.text: That is, wholly and without hypocrisy, not dissembling to turn and serve God as they do who serve him by halves, Hosea 7:16 .

2.text: You will detest the name of idols, Psalms 16:4 and will with reverence swear by the living God, when your oath may advance God’s glory, and profit others: and here by swearing he means the true religion of God.

3.text: He wills them to pluck up the impiety and wicked affection and worldly respects out of their heart, that the true seed of God’s word may be sown in it, Hosea 10:12 and this is the true circumcision of the heart, De 10:16, Romans 2:29 , Colossians 2:11 .

5.text: He warns them of the great dangers that will come on them by the Chaldeans, unless they repent and turn to the Lord.

6.text: He speaks this to admonish them of the great danger when every man will prepare to save himself, but it will be too late, 2 Kings 25:4 .

7.text: Meaning Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, 2 Kings 24:1 .

9.text: That is, the false prophets who still prophesied peace and security.

10.text: By the false prophets who promised peace and tranquillity: and thus you have punished their rebellious stubbornness by causing them to hearken to lies who would not believe your truth, 1 Kings 22:23 , Ezekiel 14:9 , 2 Thessalonians 2:11 .

11.text: The north wind by which he means Nebuchadnezzar.
But to carry away both corn and chaff.

13.text: Meaning that Nebuchadnezzar would come as suddenly as a cloud that is carried with the wind.
This is spoken in the person of all the people, who in their affliction would cry thus.

15.text: Which was a city in the utmost border of Israel north toward Babylon.
Which was in the middle between Dan and Jerusalem.

17.text: Who keep the fruits so straitly, that nothing can come in or out so would the Babylonians compass Judah.,

19.text: He shows that the true ministers are lively touched with the calamities of the Church, so that all the parts of their body feel the grief of their heart, even though with zeal to God’s glory they pronounce his judgments against the people.

20.text: Meaning, the cities which were as easily cast down as a tent.

22.text: Their wisdom and policy tend to their own destruction and pulls them from God.

23.text: By this manner of speech he shows the horrible destruction that would come on the land and also condemns the obstinacy of the people who do not repent at the fear of these terrible kings, seeing that the insensible creatures are moved therewith, as if the order of nature would be changed, Isaiah 13:10 ; Isaiah 24:23 , Ezekiel 32:7 , Joel 2:31 ; Joel 3:15 .

27.text: But for his mercies sake, he will reserve himself a residue to be his Church, and to praise him in earth, Jeremiah 5:18 .

30.text: Neither your ceremonies nor rich gifts will deliver you.

31.text: As the prophets were moved to pity the destruction of their people, so they declared it to the people to move them to repentance, Isaiah 22:4 , Jeremiah 9:1 .

1.text: That is, the city.

2.text: Though they pretend religion and holiness, yet all is but hypocrisy: for under this kind of swearing is contained the true religion.

3.text: Do you not love uprightness and faithful dealing?
You have often punished them, but all is in vain, Isaiah 9:13 .

5.text: He speaks this to the reproach of them who would govern and teach others, and yet are farther out of the way than the simple people.

6.text: Meaning, Nebuchadnezzar and his army.

7.text: He shows that to swear by anything other than by God is to forsake him.

10.text: He commands the Babylonians and enemies to destroy them.
Read Jeremiah 4:27 .

12.text: Because they gave no credit to the words of his prophets, as in Isaiah 28:15 .

13.text: Their words will be of no effect, but vain.
They are not sent from the Lord, and therefore that which they threaten to us will come on them.

14.text: Meaning, Jeremiah.

15.text: That is, the Babylonians and Chaldeans.

16.text: Who will kill many with their arrows.

18.text: Here the Lord declares his unspeakable favour toward his Church, as in Jeremiah 4:27 .

19.text: Meaning, the prophet Jeremiah.

25.text: If there is any stay, that we receive not God’s blessings in abundance, we must consider that it is for our own iniquities, Isaiah 59:1-2 .

28.text: They feel not the plague of God for it.

31.text: Meaning that there could be nothing but disorder, where the ministers were wicked and corrupt.

1.text: He speaks to them chiefly because they should take heed by the example of their brethren the other half of their tribe, who were now carried away prisoners.
Which was a city in Judah, six miles from Bethlehem, 2 Chronicles 11:6 .
Read Nehemiah 3:14 .

2.text: I have intreated her gently, and given her abundance of all things.

3.text: She will be so destroyed that the sheep may be fed in her.

4.text: He speaks this in the person of the Babylonians, who complain that the time fails them before they have brought their enterprises to pass.

7.text: He shows the reason why it would be destroyed, and how it comes from themselves.

8.text: He warns them to amend by his correction, and turn to him by repentance.

9.text: He exhorts the Babylonians to be diligent to search out all and to leave none.

10.text: They delight to hear vain things, and to shut up their ears to true doctrine.

11.text: As the Lord had given him his word to be as a fire of his indignation to burn the wicked, Jeremiah 5:14 so he kindles it now when he sees that all remedies are past.
No one will be spared.

14.text: When the people began to fear God’s judgments, the false prophets comforted them by flatterings, showing that God would send peace and not war.

16.text: In which the patriarchs and prophets walked, directed by the word of God: signifying that there is no true way, but that which God prescribes.

17.text: Prophets who would warn you of the dangers that were at hand.

18.text: God takes all the world to witness and the insensible creatures of the ingratitude of the Jews.

20.text: Read Isaiah 1:11 , Amos 5:21 .

22.text: From Babylon by Dan, which was north of Jerusalem.

24.text: For fear of the enemy: he speaks this in the person of the Jews.

27.text: Meaning, Jeremiah, whom God had appointed to try out the godly from the wicked, as a founder does the pure metal from the dross.

29.text: All the pain and labour that has been taken with them is lost.

4.text: Believe not the false prophets, who say that for the temple’s sake, and the sacrifices there the Lord will preserve you, and so nourish you in your sin, and vain confidence.

7.text: God shows on what condition he made his promise to this temple that they would be a holy people to him, as he would be a faithful God to them.

11.text: As thieves hidden in holes and dens think themselves safe, so when you are in my temple, you think to be covered with the holiness of it, and that I cannot see your wickedness, Matthew 21:13 .

12.text: Because they depended so much on the temple, which was for his promise, that he would be present and defend them where the ark was, he sends them to God’s judgments against Shiloh, where the ark had remained about 300 years, and after was taken, the priests slain, and the people miserably discomfited, 1 Samuel 4:11 , Jeremiah 26:6 .

13.text: That is, I never ceased to warn you, as in Isaiah 65:2 , Proverbs 1:23 .
He shows the only remedy to redress our faults: to allow God to lead us in the way, and to obey his calling, Isaiah 66:4 .

15.text: I will send you into captivity as I have done Ephraim, that is, the ten tribes.

16.text: To assure them that God had determined with himself to punish their wickedness, he shows the prayer of the godly cannot help them, while they remain in their obstinacy against God, and will not use the means that he uses to call them to repentance, Jeremiah 11:14 ; Jeremiah 14:11 .

18.text: That is, they sacrifice to the sun, moon and stars, which they called the queen of heaven, Jeremiah 44:17 , 2 Kings 23:5 .

22.text: Showing that it was not his chief purpose and intent, that they should offer sacrifices, but that they should regard, why they were ordained: that is, to be joined to the word as seals and confirmations of remissions of sins in Christ: for without the word they were vain and unprofitable.

25.text: Which was about fourteen hundred years.
Read Jeremiah 7:13 .

27.text: By which he shows that the pastors should not leave their flocks in their obstinacy, for the Lord will use the means of his servants to make the wicked more faulty and to prove his.

29.text: In sign of mourning, as in Job 1:20 .
Against whom he had just opportunity to pour out his wrath Micah 1:6 .

31.text: Of Topheth, read 2 Kings 23:10 .
But commanded the opposite, as in Leviticus 18:21 ; Leviticus 20:3 , De 18:10 .

1.text: The enemy for greediness will rifle your graves and lay you before those idols, who in your life you worshipped, to see if they can help you.

3.text: Because of the afflictions that they will feel through God’s judgments.

4.text: Is there no hope that they will return?

6.text: They are full of hypocrisy, and everyone follows his own fantasy without any consideration.

7.text: He accuses them in that they are more ignorant of God’s judgments, than these birds are of their appointed seasons to discern the cold and heat.

8.text: The law does not profit you neither need it to have been written for all that you have learned by it.

9.text: They who seem wise may be ashamed of their ignorance for all wisdom consists in God’s word.

11.text: See Geneva " Jeremiah 6:14 "

14.text: He speaks in the person of the people, who when the enemy comes will turn about to hide themselves and acknowledge that it is God’s hand.
That is, has brought us into extreme affliction, and thus they will not attribute this plague to fortune, but to God’s just judgment, Jeremiah 9:15 ; Jeremiah 23:15 .

16.text: Read Geneva " Jeremiah 4:15 "

17.text: God threatens to send the Babylonians among them who will utterly destroy them in such sort, as by no means they will escape.

18.text: Read Jeremiah 4:19 .

19.text: Thus the Lord speaks.

20.text: The people wonder that they have for so long a time looked for comfort in vain.

21.text: The prophet speaks this.

22.text: Meaning,that no man’s help or means could save them: for in Gilead was precious balm, Jeremiah 46:11 or else deriding the vain confidence of the people, who looked to their priests for help, who would have been the physicians of their soul, and dwelt at Gilead, Hosea 6:8 .

1.text: The prophet shows the great compassion that he had toward this people, seeing that he could never sufficiently lament the destruction that he saw to hang over them, which is a special note to discern the true pastors from the hirelings. See Geneva " Jeremiah 4:19 "

2.text: He shows that there was more peace and greater safety for him to dwell among the wild beasts than among this wicked people except that God has given him this charge.
Utterly turned from God.

3.text: To belie and slander their neighbours.

4.text: Meaning, that all were corrupt, and none could find an honest man.

5.text: They have so practised deceit, that they cannot forsake it.

6.text: They would rather have forsaken God than left their wicked trade.

7.text: With the fire of affliction.

10.text: Signifying that all the places about Jerusalem would be destroyed.

12.text: Meaning that they are all without sense and understanding and that God has taken his spirit from them.

14.text: He shows that the children cannot excuse themselves by their fathers: for both father and child if they are wicked will perish.

15.text: Read Jeremiah 8:14 .

17.text: Seeing you cannot lament your own sins, call for those foolish women, whom of a superstition you have to lament for the dead, that they by their feigned tears may provoke you to some sorrow.

19.text: As though they were weary of us, because of our iniquities, Leviticus 18:28 ; Leviticus 20:22 .

20.text: He derides the superstition of the women who made an art of mourning, and taught to weep with feigned tears.

21.text: Signifying that there is no means to deliver the wicked from God’s judgments: but when they think to be most sure, and most far off, then they are soonest taken.

23.text: As none can save himself by his own labour, or any worldly means, he shows that it is vain to put our trust in it, but that we trust in the Lord, and rejoice in him, who only can deliver.

24.text: These three points are necessary to know correctly his mercy, in which consists our salvation: his judgment, which he executes continually against the wicked, and his justice, by which he defends and maintains the faithful.

25.text: Meaning, both Jews and Gentiles, as in this next verse he shows the cause, Jeremiah 4:4 .

2.text: God forbids his people to give credit or fear the constellations and conjunctions of stars and planets which have no power of themselves but are governed by him, and their secret motions and influences are not known to man and therefore there can be no certain judgment of it, De 18:9 .

3.text: Meaning not only in the observation of the stars, but their laws and ceremonies by which they confirm their idolatry, which is forbidden, De 12:30 .

4.text: The prophets use thus plainly and simply to set forth the vile absurdity of the idolaters that men might learn to be ashamed of that to which their corrupt nature is most subject, Isaiah 44:12 .

6.text: He teaches the people to lift up their eyes to God, who has all power and therefore ought only to be feared: and in this he shows them not only the evil that they ought to hate: but the good which they ought to follow, Revelation 15:4 .

8.text: Because the people thought that to have images was a means to serve God, and to bring them to the knowledge of him, he shows that nothing more displeases God, nor brings man into greater errors and ignorance of God: and therefore he calls them the doctrine of vanity, the work of errors, Jeremiah 10:15 . Habakkuk 2:18 calls them the teachers of lies: contrary to that wicked opinion, that they are the books of the lay people.

9.text: Where they found the best gold; showing that they thought nothing too dear for their idols, some read Ophir as in 1 Kings 9:28 .

11.text: This declares that all that has been spoken of idols in this chapter, was to arm the Jews when they would be in Chaldea among the idolaters, and now with one sentence he instructs them both how to protest their own religion against the idolaters and how to answer them to their shame who would exhort them to idolatry, and therefore he writes this sentence in the Chaldean tongue for a memorial while all the rest of his writing is in Hebrew.

14.text: The more man thinks to do anything well by his own wisdom, and not as God instructs him, the more he proves himself to be a vile beast.

16.text: By these words, portion and rod, he signifies their inheritance, meaning that God would be all sufficient for them: and that their happiness consisted in him alone, and therefore they ought to renounce all other help and comfort as of idols, etc. De 32:9, Psalms 16:5 .

17.text: The prophet wills the Jews to prepare themselves for this captivity, showing that it was now at hand that they would feel the things of which he had told them.

19.text: It is my just plague, and therefore I will take it patiently: by which he teaches the people how to behave themselves toward God.

20.text: He shows how Jerusalem will lament.

21.text: The governors and ministers.

22.text: Read Jeremiah 4:15 .

23.text: He speaks this because Nebuchadnezzar purposed to have made war against the Moabites and Ammonites, but hearing of Zedekiah’s rebellion he turned his power to go against Jerusalem, Ezekiel 21:21 therefore the prophet says that this was the Lord’s direction.

24.text: Considering that God had revealed to him the certainty of their captivity Jeremiah 7:16 he only prays that he would punish them with mercy which Isaiah calls in measure, Isaiah 27:8 measuring his rods by their infirmity 1 Corinthians 10:13 for here by judgment is meant not only the punishment but also the merciful moderation of the same as in Jeremiah 30:11 .

25.text: As God cannot only be known and glorified by his mercy that he uses toward his Church, but also by his justice in punishing his enemies, he prays that this glory may fully appear both in the one and the other, Psalms 79:6 .

3.text: He calls the Jews to the consideration of God’s mercy, who freely chose them, made a covenant of eternal happiness with them and how he ever performed it on his behalf and how they ever showed themselves rebellious and ingrate toward him, and broke it on their part, and so are subject to the curse of the law, De 27:26 .

5.text: Thus he speaks in the person of the people, who agreed to the covenant.

7.text: Read Jeremiah 7:13 .

8.text: According to his own fantasy, and not as my word appointed him.
Meaning, the menaces and curses contained in the law, Leviticus 26:14 , De 28:16 .

9.text: That is, general consent to rebel against me.

11.text: Because they will not pray with true faith and repentance, but for the pain and grief which they feel, Proverbs 1:28 .

13.text: Read Jeremiah 2:28 .

14.text: Read Jeremiah 7:16 ; Jeremiah 14:11 .

15.text: My people of Israel whom I have greatly loved till now.
Meaning, that they offer not in the temple to God, but on the altars of Baal and the idols and so rejoiced in their wickedness.

16.text: Of the Babylonians and Chaldeans.

18.text: Who went about secretly to conspire my death.

19.text: Let us destroy the prophet and his doctrine. Some read "Let us corrupt his meat with wood", meaning poison.

20.text: Thus he spoke not out of hatred, but being moved with the Spirit of God, he desires the advancement of God’s glory, and the verifying of his word, which is by the destruction of his enemies.

21.text: That is, both the priests and the rest of the people: for this town was the priests, and they dwelt in it, Jeremiah 1:1 .

Not that they could not abide to hear God named; (for in this they would show themselves most holy) but because they could not abide to be sharply reproved, and therefore desired to be flattered Isaiah 30:10 , to be maintained in their pleasures Micah 2:11 and not to hear vice condemned Amos 7:12 .

1.text: The prophet confesses God to be just in all his doings, although man is not able to give a reason for all his actions.

This question has been always a great temptation to the godly, to see the wicked enemies of God in prosperity, and his dear children in adversity, as in Job 21:7 , Psalms 37:1 ; Psalms 73:3 , Habakkuk 1:3 .

2.text: They profess God in mouth, but deny him in heart, which is here meant by the reins, Isaiah 29:13 , Matthew 15:8 .

3.text: The Hebrew word is "sanctify them", meaning that God would be sanctified in the destruction of the wicked to whom God for a while gives prosperity, that afterward they would the more feel his heavy judgment when they lack their riches which were a sign of his mercy.

4.text: Abusing God’s leniency and his promises, they flattered themselves as though God would ever be merciful and not utterly destroy them therefore they hardened themselves in sin, till at length the beasts and insensible creatures felt the punishment of their stubborn rebellion against God.

5.text: Some think that God reproves Jeremiah, in that he would reason with him, saying that if he was not able to march with men, then he was far unable to dispute with God. Others, by the footmen mean them of Anathoth: and by the horsemen, them of Jerusalem who would trouble the prophet worse than his own countrymen did.

7.text: God wills the prophet to denounce his judgments against Jerusalem, even though they will both by threatenings and flatteries labour to silence him.

8.text: Ever ranting and raging against me and my prophets.

9.text: Instead of bearing my livery and wearing only my colours, they have change and diversity of colours of their idols and superstitions therefore their enemies as thick as the fowls of the air will come about them to destroy them.

10.text: He prophecies of the destruction of Jerusalem, by the captain of Nebuchadnezzar, whom he calls pastors.

11.text: Because no man regards my word, or the plagues that I have sent on the land.

13.text: That is, the prophets.
They lamented the sins of the people.
For instead of amendment, you grew worse and worse, as God’s plagues testified.

14.text: Meaning the wicked enemies of his Church who blasphemed his Name, and whom he would punish after he had delivered his people.

15.text: After I have punished the Gentiles I will have mercy on them.

16.text: The true doctrine and manner to serve God.
Read Jeremiah 4:2 .
They will be of the number of the faithful, and have a place in my Church.

4.text: Because this river was far from Jerusalem, it is evident that this was a vision, by which it was signified that the Jews would pass over the Euphrates to be captives in Babylon, and there for length of time would seem to be rotten, although they were joined to the Lord before as a girdle about a man.

12.text: Every one of you will be filled with spiritual drunkenness, and be without all knowledge to seek how to help yourselves.

14.text: It will be as easy for me to destroy the greatest and the strongest as it is for a man to break earthen bottles.

16.text: That is, affliction and misery by the Babylonians, Isaiah 8:22 .
Meaning, for help and support of the Egyptians.

17.text: You will surely be led away captive and I, according to my affection toward you, will weep and lament for your stubbornness.

18.text: For Jehoiachin and his mother rendered themselves by Jeremiah’s counsel to the king of Babylon, 2 Kings 24:12 .

19.text: That is, of Judah, which lies south of Babylon.

20.text: He asks the king, where his people is become.

21.text: By seeking to strangers for help, you have made them skilful to fight against you.

22.text: The cloak of hypocrisy will be pulled off, and your shame seen.

26.text: As your iniquities have been revealed to all the world, so shall your shame and punishment.

27.text: He compares idolaters to horses inflamed after mares.
There is no place so high nor low, where the marks and signs of your idolatry do not appear.

1.text: Which came for lack of rain as in Jeremiah 14:4 .

2.text: The word signifies extreme sorrow.

3.text: That is, with ashes in token of sorrow.

5.text: Meaning, that the brute beasts for drought were compelled to forsake their young, contrary to nature, and to go seek water which they could not find.

6.text: Who are so hot by nature, that they cannot be cooled by drinking water, but still gasp for the air to refresh them.

7.text: He shows the only way to remedy God’s plagues, which is by true confession of our sins, and returning to him by repentance.

8.text: That takes no care for us.

9.text: That takes no care for us.

11.text: Read Jeremiah 7:16 ; Jeremiah 11:14 .

13.text: He pities the people, and accuses the false prophets who deceived them: but the Lord answered that both the prophets who deceived and the people who permitted themselves to be seduced, will perish, Jeremiah 23:15 ; Jeremiah 27:8-9 ; Jeremiah 29:8 .

17.text: The false prophets promised peace and assurance, but Jeremiah calls to tears, and repentance for their affliction, which is at hand, as in Jeremiah 9:1 , Lamentations 1:16 ; Lamentations 2:18 .

18.text: Both high and low will be led captive into Babylon.

19.text: Though the prophet knew that God had cast off the multitude, who were hypocrites and bastard children, yet he was assured that for his promise sake he would still have a Church, for which he prays.

20.text: He teaches the Church a form of prayer to humble themselves to God by true repentance, which is the only way to avoid this famine, which was the beginning of God’s plagues.

22.text: Meaning their idols, read Jeremiah 10:15 .

1.text: Meaning that if there were any man living moved with so great zeal toward the people as were these two, yet he would not grant this request, as he had determined the contrary, Ezekiel 14:14 .

3.text: The dogs, birds and beasts would devour them that were slain.

4.text: The word signifies to run to and fro for fear and unquietness of conscience as Cain did.
Not that the people were punished for the king’s sin only, but for their own sins also, because they consented to his wickedness.

6.text: That is, I will not call back my plagues or spare you any more.

7.text: Meaning, the cities.

8.text: Because I had slain their husbands.

9.text: She who had many lost all her children.
She was destroyed in the midst of her prosperity.

10.text: By these are the prophet’s words, complaining of the obstinacy of the people and that he was reserved to so wicked a time: in which also he shows what is the condition of God’s ministers, that is, to have all the world against them, though they give no opportunity.
Which is an opportunity for contention and hatred.

11.text: In this perplexity the Lord comforted me, and said that my last days would be quiet: and by the enemy he means here Nebuzaradan the captain of Nebuchadnezzar, who gave Jeremiah the choice either to remain in his country or to go where he would; or by the enemy he means the Jews, who would later know Jeremiah’s faithfulness, and therefore favour him.

12.text: As for the people, though they seemed strong as iron, yet they would not be able to resist the hard iron of Babylon, but would be led captives.

15.text: He does not speak this out of a desire for revenge, but wishing that God would deliver his Church from them who he knew to be hardened and incorrigible.

16.text: I received them with a great joy, as he that is famished eats meat.

17.text: I had nothing to do with the wicked contemners of your word, but lamented bitterly for your plagues: showing what the faithful should do when they see tokens of God’s anger.

18.text: And have not assisted me according to the promise? In which it appears that in the saints of God is imperfection of faith, which through impatience is often assailed as in Jeremiah 20:7 .

19.text: If you forget these carnal considerations and faithfully execute your charge.
That is, seek to win the good from the bad.
That is, as my mouth has pronounced, Jeremiah 1:18 and as here follows in Jeremiah 15:20 .
Do not conform yourself to their wickedness, but let them follow your godly example.

20.text: I will teach you with an invincible strength and constancy, so that all the powers of the world will not overcome you.

2.text: Meaning that the affliction would be so horrible in Jerusalem that a wife and children would only increase his sorrow.

5.text: Signifying that the affliction would be so great that one would not have leisure to comfort another.

6.text: That is, should not tear their clothes in sign of mourning.

7.text: For in these great extremities all consolation and comfort will be in vain.

10.text: Because the wicked are always rebellious and conceal their own sins and murmur against God’s judgments, as though he had no just cause to punish them, he shows him what to answer.

15.text: Signifying that the blessing of their deliverance out of Babylon would be so great that it would abolish the remembrance of their deliverance from Egypt: but he has here chiefly respect to the spiritual deliverance under Christ.

16.text: By the fishers and hunters are meant the Babylonians and Chaldeans who would destroy them in such sort, that if they escaped the one, the other would take them.

18.text: That is, their sons and daughters, who they offered to Molech.

19.text: He wonders at the great mercy of God in this deliverance which will not only extend to the Jews but also to the Gentiles.
Our fathers were most vile idolaters therefore it comes only of God’s mercy that he performs his promise and has not utterly cast us off.

21.text: They will once again feel my power and mercy for their deliverance that they may learn to worship me.

1.text: The remembrance of their contempt of God cannot pass, although for a time he defers the punishment, for it will be revealed to men and angels.
Instead of the law of God, they have written idolatry and all abomination in their heart.
Your sins appear in all the altars that you have erected to idols.

2.text: Some read, "So that their children remember their altars", that is, follow their father’s wickedness.

3.text: Zion that was my mountain, will now be left as a waste field.

4.text: Because you would not give the land rest, at such times, days and years as I appointed, you will after this be carried away and it will rest for lack of labourers.

5.text: The Jews were given to worldly policies and thought to make themselves strong by the friendship of the Egyptians, Isaiah 31:3 and strangers and in the mean time did not depend on God, and therefore he denounces God’s plagues against them, showing that they prefer corruptible man to God, who is immortal, Isaiah 2:22 , Jeremiah 48:6-7 .

8.text: Read Psalms 1:3 .

9.text: Because the wicked always have some excuse to defend their doings he shows that their own lewd imaginations deceive them and bring them to these hardships: but God will examine their deeds by the malice of their hearts, 1 Samuel 16:7 , 1 Chronicles 28:9 , Psalms 7:10 , Jeremiah 11:20 ; Jeremiah 10:12 , Revelation 2:13 .

11.text: As the patriarch by calling gathered others who forsake her when they see she is not their mother: so the covetous man is forsaken of his riches because he comes by them falsely.

12.text: Showing that the godly ought to glory in nothing, but in God who exalts his, and has left a sign of his favour in his temple.

13.text: Their names will not be registered in the book of life.

14.text: He desires God to preserve him that he fall not into temptation, considering the great contempt of God’s word, and the multitude that fall from God.

15.text: The wicked say that my prophecy will not come to pass, because you deferred the time of your vengeance.

16.text: I am assured of my calling, and therefore know that the thing which you speak by me will come to pass, and that I speak not of any worldly affection.

17.text: However the wicked deal rigorously with me, yet let me find comfort in you.

18.text: Read Jeremiah 11:20 .

19.text: While your doctrine may best be understood both by high and low.

21.text: By naming the Sabbath day, he comprehends the thing that is signified by it, for if they transgressed in the ceremony, they must be guilty of the rest, read Exodus 20:8 and by the breaking of this one commandment, he makes them transgressors of the whole law, as the first and second table are contained in it.

4.text: As the potter has power over the clay to make what pot he will, or to break them, when he has made them: so have I power over you to do with you as seems good to me, Isaiah 45:9 , Romans 9:20-21 .

8.text: When the Scripture attributes repentance to God, it is not that he does contrary to that which he has ordained in his secret counsel: but when he threatens it is a calling to repentance, and when he gives man grace to repent, the threatening (which ever contains a condition in it) takes no place: and this the scripture calls repentance in God, because it so appears to man’s judgment.

12.text: As men who had no remorse but were altogether bent to rebellion and to their own selfwill.

14.text: As no man that has thirst refuses fresh waters which he has at home, to go and seek waters abroad to quench his thirst: so they should not seek help and comfort from strangers and leave God who was present with them.

15.text: That is, the way of truth which God had taught by his law, Jeremiah 6:16 .

17.text: I will show my anger and not my favour toward them.

18.text: This argument the wicked have always used against the servants of God. The church cannot err: we are the Church, and therefore whoever speaks against us, they ought to die, 1 Kings 22:24 , Jeremiah 7:4 ; Jeremiah 20:2 , Malachi 2:4 and thus the false Church persecutes the true Church, which stands not in outward pomp, and in multitude, but is known by the graces of the Holy Spirit.
Let us slander him and accuse him: for we will be believed.

21.text: Seeing the obstinate malice of the adversaries, who grew daily more and more, the prophet being moved with God’s Spirit, without any carnal affection prays for their destruction because he knew that it would be to God’s glory, and profit of his Church.

3.text: By kings here and in other places are meant counsellors and governors of the people; who he calls the ancients, Jeremiah 19:1 .
Read of this phrase in 1 Samuel 3:11 .

5.text: By which is declared that whatever is not commanded by God’s word concerning is service is against his word.

6.text: Read Jeremiah 7:31 , 2 Kings 23:10 , Isaiah 30:33 .

11.text: This visible sign was to confirm them concerning the assurance of this plague, which the Lord threatened by his prophet.

13.text: He notes the great rage of the idolaters who left no place free from their abominations, in that they polluted their own houses with it, as we see yet among the papists.
Read De 22:8 .

2.text: Thus we see that the thing which neither the king nor the princes nor the people dared to undertake against the prophet of God, this priest as a chief instrument of Satan first attempted, read Jeremiah 18:18 .

6.text: Who have allowed themselves to be abused by your false prophecies.

7.text: In this appears the impatiency which often overcomes the servants of God when they do not see their labours profit, and also feel their own weakness. See Geneva " Jeremiah 15:18 "
You thrust me forth to this work against my will.

8.text: He shows that he did his office in that he reproved the people of their vices and threatened them with God’s judgments: but because he was derided and persecuted for this, he was discouraged, and would have stopped preaching, except that God’s spirit forced him to it.

10.text: Thus the enemies conferred together to know what they had heard him say, that they might accuse him of it, read Isaiah 29:21 .

11.text: Here he shows how his faith strove against temptation and sought the Lord for strength.

14.text: How the children of God are overcome in this battle of the flesh and the Spirit, and into what inconveniences they fall till God raises them up again: read Job 3:1 , Jeremiah 15:10 .

16.text: Alluding to the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah, Genesis 19:25 .

17.text: Meaning that the fruit of it might never come to profit.

2.text: Not that the king was touched with repentance of his sins and so sought God, as did Hezekiah when he sent for Isaiah, 2 Kings 19:1 , Isaiah 37:2 but because the prophet might pray to God to take this present plague away, as Pharaoh sought Moses Exodus 9:28 .

4.text: That is, from your enemies to destroy yourselves.

8.text: By yielding yourselves to Nebuchadnezzar.
By resisting him.

9.text: As a thing recovered from extreme danger, Jeremiah 37:2 ; Jeremiah 39:18 ; Jeremiah 45:5 .

12.text: Be diligent to do justice.

13.text: Meaning, Jerusalem which was built part on the hill and part in the valley and was compassed about with mountains.

14.text: That is, in the houses of it, which stood as thick as trees in the forest.

3.text: This was his ordinary manner of preaching before the kings from Josiah to Zedekiah which was about forty years.

5.text: Showing that there is no one greater than he is, Hebrews 6:13 and that he will most certainly perform his oath.

6.text: He compares Jerusalem to Gilead which was beyond Jordan and the beauty of Judea to Lebanon.

7.text: The Hebrew word signifies to sanctify because the Lord dedicates to his use and purpose such as he prepares to execute his work, Isaiah 13:3 , Jeremiah 6:4 ; Jeremiah 12:3 .
Your buildings made from cedar trees.

8.text: As they who wonder at a thing which they thought would never have come to pass, De 29:24, 1 Kings 9:8 .

10.text: Signifying that they would lose their king: for Jehoiachin went forth to meet Nebuchadnezzar and yielded himself, and was carried into Babylon, 2 Kings 24:12 .

11.text: Whom some think to be Jehoiachin and that Josiah was his grandfather: but it seems this was Jehoiakim, as in Jeremiah 22:18 .

13.text: By bribes and extortion.

15.text: Meaning Josiah, who was not given to ambition and superfluity, but was content with mediocrity, and only delighted in setting forth God’s glory, and to do justice to all.

18.text: For everyone will have enough to lament for himself.

19.text: Not honourably among his fathers, but as carrion are cast in a hole, because their stink should not infect, read 1 Kings 14:10 . Josephus writes that the enemy slew him in the city and commanded him to be cast before the walls unburied, see Jeremiah 36:30 .

20.text: To call to the Assyrians for help.
For this was the way out of India to Assyria, by which is meant that all help would fail: for the Chaldeans have subdued both them and the Egyptians.

22.text: Both your governors and they that would help you will vanish away as wind.

24.text: Who was called Jehoiachin or Jeconiah, whom he calls here Coniah in contempt who thought his kingdom could never depart from him, because he came of the stock of David, and therefore for the promise sake could not be taken from his house, but he abused God’s promise and therefore was justly deprived of the kingdom.

29.text: He shows that all posterity will be witnesses of his just plague, as though it were registered for perpetual memory.

30.text: Not that he had no children (for later he begat Salathiel in the captivity, Matthew 1:12 ) but that none would reign after him as king.

1.text: Meaning the prince’s governors and false prophets as in Ezekiel 34:2 .
For which I have special care, and have prepared good pastures for them.

2.text: Whose charge is to feed the flock but they eat the fruit of it, Ezekiel 34:3 .

3.text: Thus the prophets always used to mix the promises with the threatenings lest the godly should be too much beaten down and therefore he shows how God will gather his Church after this dispersion.

5.text: This prophecy is of the restitution of the Church in the time of Jesus Christ, who is the true branch, read Isaiah 11:1 ; Isaiah 45:8 , Jeremiah 35:15 , Daniel 9:24 .

7.text: Read Jeremiah 16:14 .

9.text: Meaning, the false prophets who deceive the people: in which appears his great love toward his nation, read Jeremiah 14:13 .

10.text: They run headlong to wickedness and seek vain help.

11.text: My temple is full of their idolatry and superstitions.

14.text: They who should have profited by my rods against Samaria, are become worse than they.
Though to the world they seem holy fathers, yet I detest them as I did these abominable cities.

15.text: Read Jeremiah 8:14 .

16.text: Which they have invented of their own brain.

17.text: Read Jeremiah 6:14 ; Jeremiah 8:11 .

18.text: Thus they derided Jeremiah as though the word of God was not revealed to him, so also spoke Zedekiah to Micaiah, 1 Kings 22:24 .

20.text: Both that God has sent me, and that my words will be true.

22.text: He shows the difference between the true prophets and the false, between the hireling and the true minister.

23.text: Do I not see your falsehood, however you cloak it, and wherever you commit it?

25.text: I have a prophecy revealed to me as in Numbers 12:6 .

27.text: He shows that Satan raises up false prophets to bring the people from God.

28.text: Let the false prophet declare that it is his own fantasy, and not slander my word as though it were a cloak to cover his lies.

Meaning, that it is not enough for God’s ministers to abstain from lies and to speak the word of God but that there is judgment in alleging it, and that it may appear to be applied to the same purpose that it was spoken, Ezekiel 3:27 , 1 Corinthians 2:13 ; 1 Corinthians 4:2 , 2 Timothy 2:25 .

30.text: Who set forth in my Name that which I have not commanded.

31.text: That is, the Lord.

33.text: The prophets called their threatenings God’s burden, which the sinners were not able to sustain, therefore the wicked in deriding the word, would ask of the prophets, what was the burden as though they would say, "You seek nothing else, but to lay burdens on our shoulders" and thus they rejected the word of God as a grievous burden.

34.text: Because this word was brought to contempt and derision, he will teach them another manner of speech, and will cause this word burden to cease and teach them to ask with reverence, "What says the Lord?"

36.text: The thing which they mock and contemn will come on them.

1.text: The good figs signified them that were gone into captivity and so saved their life, as in Jeremiah 21:8 , and the bad figs them that remained, who were yet subject to the sword, famine and pestilence.

5.text: By which he approves the yielding of Jeconiah and his company because they obeyed the prophet, who exhorted them to it.

7.text: Which declares that man of himself can know nothing till God gives the heart and understanding.

8.text: Who fled there for comfort.

1.text: That is, in the third year accomplished and in the beginning of the fourth: for though Nebuchadnezzar began to reign in the end of the third year of Jehoiakim’s reign yet that year is not counted here because it was almost over, Daniel 1:1 .

3.text: Which was the fifth year and the ninth month of Jehoiakim’s reign.
That is, I have spared no diligence or labour, Jeremiah 7:13 .

5.text: He shows that the prophets, wholly with one consent laboured to pull the people from those vices, which then reigned, that is, from idolatry and the vain confidence of men: for under these two all others were contained, 2 Kings 17:13 , Jeremiah 18:11 ; Jeremiah 35:15 , Jonah 3:8 .

9.text: The Chaldeans and all their power.
So the wicked and Satan himself are God’s servants, because he makes them serve him by constraint and turns that which they do out of malice to his honour and glory.
As the Philistines, Ammonites, Egyptians and others.

10.text: Meaning that bread and all things that would serve to their feasts would be taken away.

12.text: This revelation was for the confirmation of his prophecy because he told them of the time that they would enter and remain in captivity, 2 Chronicles 36:22 , Ezra 1:1 , Jeremiah 29:10 , Daniel 9:2 .
For seeing the judgment began at his own house, the enemies must be punished most grievously, Ezekiel 9:6 , 1 Peter 4:17 .

14.text: That is of the Babylonians as in Jeremiah 27:7 .

15.text: Signifying the extreme affliction that God had appointed for everyone, Psalms 75:8 , Isaiah 51:17 and this cup which the wicked drink, is more bitter than that which he gives to his children, for he measures the one by mercy, and the other by justice.

18.text: For now it begins and will so continue till it is accomplished.

20.text: Read Job 1:1 .
Which were cities of the Philistines.

21.text: Edom is here taken for the whole country and Uz for a part of it.

22.text: As Greece, Italy and the rest of those countries.

23.text: These were people of Arabia which came of Dedan the son of Abraham and Keturah.

24.text: For there were two countries so named, the one called plentiful and the other barren, or desert.

26.text: That is of Babylon, as in Jeremiah 51:41 .

29.text: That is Jerusalem, read Jeremiah 25:12 .

33.text: They who are slain at the Lord’s appointment.

34.text: You that are chief rulers, and governors.
Which are most easily broken.

35.text: It will not help them to seek to flee.

2.text: That is, in that place of the temple to which the people resort out of all Judah to sacrifice.
To the intent that they should pretend no ignorance, as in Acts 20:27 .

3.text: See Geneva " Jeremiah 7:12 "

6.text: See Geneva " Jeremiah 7:12 "
So that when they would curse any, they will say, "God do to you as to Jerusalem."

9.text: Because of God’s promises to the temple, Psalms 132:14 that he would forever remain there, hypocrites thought this temple could never perish and therefore thought it blasphemy to speak against it, Matthew 26:61 , Acts 6:13 not considering that this was meant of the Church where God will remain forever.

10.text: So called, because it was repaired by Jotham, 2 Kings 15:35 .

12.text: He both shows the cause of his doings plainly and also threatens them that nothing would help, though they should put him to death, but heap greater vengeance on their heads.

18.text: That is, of the House of the Lord, that is, Zion, and these examples the godly alleged to deliver Jeremiah out of the priests hands, whose rage else would not have been satisfied but by his death.

19.text: So that the city was not destroyed, but by a miracle was delivered out of the hands of Sennacherib.

22.text: Here is declared the fury of tyrants who cannot stand to hear God’s word declared but persecute the ministers of it, and yet in the end they prevail nothing but provoke God’ judgments so much more.

23.text: As in the first Hezekiah’s example is to be followed, so in this other Jehoiakim’s act it to be abhorred: for God’s plague descended on him and his household.

24.text: Which declares that nothing could have appeased their fury if God had not moved this noble man to stand valiantly in his defense.

1.text: Concerning the disposition of these prophecies, they who gathered them into a book, did not altogether observe the order of times, but saw some before, which should be after, and contrary wise which if the reader mark well it will avoid many doubts and make the reading much easier.

2.text: By such signs the prophets used sometimes to confirm their prophecies which they could not do of themselves but in as much as they had a revelation for the same, Isaiah 20:2 and therefore the false prophets to get more credit, used also such visible signs but they had no revelation, 1 Kings 22:12 .

6.text: Read Jeremiah 25:9 .

7.text: Meaning, Evilmerodach and his son Belshazzar.
They will bring him and his kingdom in subjection as in Jeremiah 25:14 .

16.text: Which were taken when Jeconiah was led captive into Babel.

18.text: For it was not only the prophet’s office to show the word of God, but also to pray for the sins of the people, Genesis 20:7 which these could not do because they had no express word: for God had pronounced the contrary.

22.text: That is, for the space of seventy years till I have caused the Medes and Persians to overcome the Chaldeans.

1.text: When Jeremiah began to bear these bonds and yokes.
After the land had rested, as in Leviticus 25:2 .
This was a city in Benjamin belonging to the sons of Aaron, Joshua 21:17 .

5.text: He was so esteemed though he was a false prophet.

6.text: That is, I would wish the same for God’s honour and wealth of my people but he has appointed the contrary.

8.text: Meaning, that the prophets that denounced war or peace were tried either true or false by the success of their prophecies, even though God makes to come to pass sometimes that which the false prophet speaks to try the faith of his, De 13:3 .

10.text: This declares the impudency of the wicked hirelings who have no zeal to the truth but are led with ambition to get the favour of men and therefore cannot abide any that might discredit them but burst forth into rages and contrary to their own conscience, pass not what lies they report or how wickedly they do so that they may maintain their estimation.

14.text: That is, a hard and cruel servitude.
Signifying that all would be his as in Daniel 2:38 .

17.text: Seeing this thing was evident in the eyes of the people and yet they returned not to the Lord, it is manifest that miracles cannot move us, neither the word itself, unless God touch the heart.

1.text: For some died in the way.

2.text: Meaning Jeconiah’s mother.

3.text: To entreat of some equal condition.

4.text: That is, the Lord whose work this was.

7.text: The prophet does not speak this for the affection that he bore to the tyrant, but that they should pray for the common rest and quietness that their troubles might not be increased, and that they might with more patience and less grief wait for the time of their deliverance, which God had appointed most certain: for not only the Israelites but all the world yea and the insensible creatures would rejoice when these tyrants would be destroyed, as in Isaiah 24:4 .

13.text: When your oppression will be great, and your afflictions cause you to repent your disobedience and also when the seventy years of your captivity will be expired, 2 Chronicles 36:22 , Ezra 1:1 , Jeremiah 25:12 , Daniel 9:2 .

15.text: As Ahab, Zedekiah and Shemaiah.

17.text: By which he assures them that there will be no hope of returning before the appointed time.
According to the comparison, Jeremiah 24:1-2 .

18.text: Read Jeremiah 26:6 .

19.text: Read Jeremiah 7:13 ; Jeremiah 25:3 ; Jeremiah 26:5 .

22.text: Because they gave the people hope of speedy returning.

23.text: Which was adultery and falsifying the word of God.

26.text: Shemaiah the false prophet flatters Zephaniah the chief priest as though God had given him the spirit and zeal of Jehoiada to punish whoever trespassed against the word of God, of that he would have made Jeremiah one, calling him a raver and a false prophet.

32.text: He and his seed will be destroyed so that none of them would see the blessing of this deliverance.

2.text: Because they would be assured and their posterity confirmed in the hope of this deliverance promised.

5.text: He shows that before this deliverance will come, the Chaldeans would be extremely afflicted by their enemies, and that they would be in such perplexity and sorrow as a woman in her travail as Isaiah 13:8 .

7.text: Meaning that the time of their captivity would be grievous.

8.text: When I will visit Babylon.
Of the king of Babylon.
That is, of Jacob.

9.text: That is, Messiah who would come of the stock of David according to the flesh and would be the true pastor, Ezekiel 34:23 who is set forth and his kingdom would be everlasting in the person of David, Hosea 3:5 .

11.text: In this is commanded God’s great mercy toward his, who does not destroy them for their sins, but corrects and chastises them till he has purged and pardoned them and so burns the rods by which he punished them, Isaiah 33:1 .

18.text: Meaning that the city and the temple would be restored to their former estate.

19.text: He shows how the people will with praise and thanksgiving acknowledge this blessing.

21.text: Meaning, Zerubbabel, who was the figure of Christ in whom this was accomplished.
Signifying that Christ willingly submits himself to the obedience of God his father.

23.text: Lest the wicked hypocrites should flatter themselves with these promises the prophet shows what will be their portion.

24.text: When this Messiah and deliverer is sent.

1.text: When this noble governor will come, meaning Christ, not only Judah and Israel, but the rest of the world will be called.

2.text: Who were delivered from the cruelty of Pharaoh.
That is, God.

3.text: The people thus reason as though he were not so beneficial to them now as he had been of old.
Thus the Lord answers that his love is not changeable.

4.text: You will still have opportunity to rejoice which is meant by tabrets and dancing as their custom was after notable victories, Exodus 15:20 , Jud 11:34 .

5.text: Because the Israelites who were the ten tribes never returned to Samaria, therefore this must be spiritually understood under the kingdom of Christ, which was the restoration of the true Israel.
That is, will eat the fruit of it, as in Leviticus 19:23-25 , De 20:6 .

6.text: The ministers of the word.
They will exhort all to the embracing of the gospel, as in Isaiah 2:3 .

7.text: He shows what will be the concord and love of all under the gospel when none will be refused for their infirmities: and everyone will exhort one another to embrace it.

9.text: That is, lamenting their sins which had not given ear to the prophets and therefore it follows that God received them to mercy, Jeremiah 50:4 . Some take it that they should weep for joy.
Where they found no impediments, but abundance of all things.
That is, my dearly beloved as the first child is to the father.

11.text: That is, from the Babylonians and other enemies.

12.text: By these temporal benefits he means the spiritual graces which are in the Church, and of which there would ever be plenty, Isaiah 58:11-12 .

13.text: In the company of the faithful, who ever praise God for his benefits.

14.text: Meaning, the spirit of wisdom, knowledge and zeal.

15.text: To declare the greatness of God’s mercy in delivering the Jews, he shows them that they were like the Benjamites of the Israelites, that is, utterly destroyed and carried away, so much so that if Rachel the mother of Benjamin could have risen again to seek her children she would have found none remaining.

18.text: That is, the people who were led captive.
Which was wanton and could not be subject to the yoke.
He shows how the faithful used to pray, that is, desire God to tame them as they cannot turn of themselves.

19.text: In sign of repentance and detestation of my sin.

20.text: As though he would say no for by his iniquity he did what lay in him to cast me off.

21.text: Mark by what way you went into captivity and you will turn again by the same.

22.text: Because their deliverance from Babylon was a figure of their deliverance from sin, he shows how this would be procured that is, by Jesus Christ, whom a woman would conceive and bear in her womb. Which is a strange thing in earth, because he would be born of a virgin without man or he means that Jerusalem which was like a barren woman in her captivity would be fruitful as she that is joined in marriage and whom God blesses with children.

26.text: Having understood this vision of the Messiah to come, in whom the two houses of Israel and Judah would be joined, I rejoiced.

27.text: I will multiply and enrich them with people and cattle.

29.text: The wicked used this proverb when they murmured against God’s judgments pronounced by the prophets, saying that their fathers had committed the fault and that the children were punished, Ezekiel 18:2-3 .

31.text: Though the covenant of redemption made to the fathers and this which was given later seemed varied, yet they are all one and grounded on Jesus Christ, save that this is called new, because of the manifestation of Christ and the abundant graces of the Holy Spirit given to his Church under the gospel.

32.text: And so were the opportunity of their own divorcement through their infidelity, Isaiah 50:1 .

33.text: In the time of Christ, my law will instead of tables of stone be written in their hearts by my Holy Spirit, Hebrews 8:10 .

34.text: Under the kingdom of Christ there will be no one blinded with ignorance, but I will give them faith, and acknowledge God for remission of their sins and daily increase the same: so that it will not seem to come so much by the preaching of my ministers as by the instruction of my Holy Spirit, Isaiah 54:13 but the full accomplishing of it is referred to the kingdom of Christ, when we will be joined with our head.

35.text: If the sun, moon and stars cannot but glue light according to my ordinance, so long as this world lasts, so shall my church never fail, neither shall anything hinder it: and as sure as I will have a people, so certain is it, that I will leave them my word forever to govern them with.

37.text: The one and the other is impossible.

38.text: As it was performed, Nehemiah 3:1 . By this description he shows that the city would be as ample and beautiful as it ever was: but he alludes to the spiritual Jerusalem whose beauty would be incomparable.

1.text: So that Jeremiah had now prophesied from the thirteenth year of Josiah to the last year save one of Zedekiah’s reign, which was almost forty years.

5.text: Till I take Zedekiah away by death: for he will not die by the sword as in Jeremiah 34:4 .

7.text: By which was meant that the people would return again out of captivity and enjoy their possessions and vineyards as in Jeremiah 32:15 ; Jeremiah 32:44 .
Because he was next of the kindred, as in Ruth 4:4 .

8.text: Of the possession of the Levites, read Leviticus 25:32 .

9.text: Which amounts to about ten shillings six pence in our money if this shekel were the common shekel, see Geneva " Genesis 23:15 ", for the shekel of the temple was of double value, and ten pieces of silver were half a shekel, for twenty made the shekel.

11.text: According to the custom the instrument or evidence was sealed up with the common seal and a copy of it remained which contained the same in effect but was left open to be seen if anything should be called into doubt.

14.text: And so to hide them in the ground, that they might be reserved as a token of their deliverance.

18.text: Because the wicked are subject to the curse of God, he shows that their posterity who by nature are under this malediction will be punished both for their own wickedness and that the iniquity of their fathers which is likewise in them, will be also avenged on their head.

20.text: Meaning that his miracles in delivering his people would never be forgotten.

24.text: The word signifies anything that is cast up, as a mount or rampart, and is also used for engines of war, which were laid on a high place to shoot into a city before guns were in use.

27.text: That is, of every creature: who as they are his work, so does he govern and guide them as pleases him, by which he shows that as he is the author of their captivity for their sins, so will he for his mercies be their redeemer to restore them again to liberty.

30.text: From the time that I brought them out of Egypt and made them my people and called them my firstborn.

33.text: 2 Chronicles 36:15 , Isaiah 65:2 , Jeremiah 7:13 ; Jeremiah 7:13 ; Jeremiah 3, 26; Jeremiah 5:1-31 ; Jeremiah 29:19 ; Jeremiah 35:14 ; Jeremiah 44:4 .

35.text: That is, the altars which were made to offer sacrifices to their idols on.
Read Jeremiah 7:31 , 2 Kings 21:4 ; 2 Kings 21:6 .
Read 2 Kings 16:3 .

36.text: Read Jeremiah 30:16 .

39.text: One consent and one religion, as in Ezekiel 11:19 ; Ezekiel 36:26 .

40.text: Read Jeremiah 31:1 to Jeremiah 33:26 .

44.text: This is the declaration of that which was spoken of in Jeremiah 32:8 .

1.text: Which was in the king’s house at Jerusalem, as in Jeremiah 32:1-2 .

2.text: That is, of Jerusalem, who as he made it, so will he preserve it, read Isaiah 37:26 .

4.text: Read Jeremiah 32:24 .

5.text: The Jews think to overcome the Chaldeans, but they seek their own destruction.
He shows that God’s favour is cause of all prosperity, as his anger is of all adversity.

6.text: In the midst of his threatenings God remembers his, and comforts them.

8.text: Declaring that there is no deliverance nor joy, but where we feel remission of sins.

9.text: By which he shows that the Church in which is remission of sins, is God’s honour and glory, so that whoever is enemy to it, labours to dishonour God.

11.text: Which was a song appointed for the Levites to praise God by, 1 Chronicles 16:8 Ps 105:1 106:1 107:1 118:1 136:1 Isaiah 12:4

13.text: Meaning that all the country of Judah will be inhabited again.

15.text: That is, I will send the Messiah, who will come of the house of David, of whom this prophecy is meant, as testify all the Jews and that which is written, Jeremiah 23:5 .

16.text: That is, Christ that will call his Church.
That is, Christ is our Lord God, our righteousness, sanctification and redemption, 1 Corinthians 1:30 .

18.text: That is, chiefly meant of the spiritual sacrifice of thanksgiving which is left to the Church in the time of Christ, who was the everlasting priest and the everlasting sacrifice figured by the sacrifices of the law.

10.text: He speaks this in the reproach of this wicked king, in whose blood, that is in the race of his predecessors, Jerusalem would have been blessed according to God’s promise and flourished as a fruitful vine.

12.text: Meaning, that the Chaldeans would destroy them as the east wind does the fruit of the vine.

14.text: Destruction is come by Zedekiah, who was the opportunity for this rebellion.

1.text: Of the captivity of Jeconiah.

4.text: This declares the great leniency and patience of God who calls sinners to repentance before he condemns them.

5.text: I swore that I would be their God, which manner of oath was observed from all antiquity, where they used to lift up their hands toward the heavens, acknowledging God to be the author of truth and the defender of it, and also the judge of the heart, wishing that he would take vengeance, if they concealed anything which they knew to be truth.

7.text: God had forbidden them to make mention of the idols, Exodus 23:13 , Psalms 16:4 .

8.text: Which declares the wickedness of man’s heart, who judge God’s service by their eyes and outward senses.

9.text: God had ever this respect to his glory, that he would not have evil spoken of his Name among the Gentiles for the punishment that his people deserved, in confidence of which the godly ever prayed, as in Exodus 32:12 , Numbers 14:13 .

14.text: Who might by it take an opportunity to blaspheme my Name and to accuse me of lack of ability, or else that I had sought a means to destroy them more conveniently.

16.text: That is, my true religion, which I had commanded them, and gave themselves to serve me according to their own fantasies.

18.text: By which the Holy Spirit confuses them that say that they will follow the religion and example of their fathers, and not measure their doings by God’s word whether they are approved by it or not.

24.text: Meaning that they set their delight on them.

25.text: Because they would not obey my laws, I gave them up to themselves that they should obey their own fantasies, as in Ezekiel 20:39 , Romans 1:21 ; Romans 1:24 .

26.text: I condemned those things, and counted them as abominable, which they thought had been excellent and to have declared most zeal, Lu 16:15 for that which God required as most excellent they gave to their idols.
