That is, the synagogue in which you boast.

6.text: That is, the priests will be cast off, because for lack of knowledge they are not able to execute their charge, and instruct others; De 33:3, Malachi 2:7 .
Meaning the whole body of the people, who were weary with hearing the word of God.

7.text: The more I was beneficial to them.

8.text: That is, the priests seek to eat the people’s offerings, and flatter them in their sins.

9.text: Signifying that as they have sinned together, so will they be punished together.

10.text: Showing that their wickedness will be punished in all ways: for even though they think by the multitude of wives to have many children, yet they will be deceived of their hope.

11.text: In giving themselves to pleasures, they become like brute beasts.

12.text: Thus he speaks by derision in calling them his people, who now because of their sins they were not his people: for they sought help from stocks or wooden images and sticks or idols.
They are carried away with madness.

13.text: Because they take away God’s honour, and give it to idols: therefore he will give them up to their lusts, so that they will dishonour their own bodies; Romans 1:28 .

14.text: I will not correct your shame to bring you to proper living, but will let you run headlong to your own damnation.

15.text: God complains that Judah is infected, and wants them to learn to return in time.
For even though the Lord had honoured this place by his presence, yet because it was abused by their idolatry, he did not want his people to resort there.
He calls Bethel, that is, the house of God, Bethaven, that is, the house of iniquity, because of their abominations set up there, signifying that no place is holy, where God is not purely worshipped.

16.text: God will so disperse them, that they will not remain in any certain place.

18.text: They are so shameless in receiving bribes, that they command men to bring them to them.

19.text: To carry them suddenly away.

1.text: The priests and princes caught the poor people in their snares, as the fowlers did the birds, in these two high mountains.

2.text: Even though they seemed to be given altogether to holiness, and to sacrifices which here he calls slaughter in contempt.
Though I had admonished them continually by my Prophets.

3.text: They boasted themselves not only to be Israelites, but also Ephraimites, because their King Jeroboam came from that tribe.

5.text: Meaning their condemning of all admonitions.

7.text: That is, their children are degenerate, so that there is no hope in them.
Their destruction is not far off.

8.text: That is, all of Israel that was included under this tribe, signifying that the Lord’s plagues would pursue them from place to place until they were destroyed.

9.text: By the success they will know that I have surely determined this.

10.text: They have turned upside down all political order and all manner of religion.

11.text: That is, after King Jeroboam’s commandment, and did not rather follow God.

13.text: Instead of seeking for remedy from God’s hand.
Who was king of the Assyrians.

1.text: He shows the people that they ought to turn to the Lord, so that he might stop his plagues.

2.text: Though he correct us from time to time, yet his help will not be far off, if we return to him.

4.text: You seem to have a certain holiness and repentance, but it is very sudden, and as a morning cloud.

5.text: I have still laboured by my prophets, and as it were prepared you to bring you to correction, but all was in vain: for my word was not food to feed them, but a sword to slay them.
My doctrine which I taught you, was most evident.

6.text: He shows to what his doctrine was aimed at, that they should unite the obedience of God, and the love of their neighbour, with outward sacrifices.

7.text: That is, like small and weak persons.

8.text: Which was the place where the priests dwelt, and which should have been best instructed in my word.

11.text: That is, imitates your idolatry, and has taken grafts of your trees.

1.text: Meaning that there was no one type of vice among them, but that they were subject to all wickedness, both secret and open.

3.text: They esteem their wicked king Jeroboam above God, and seek how to flatter and please him.

4.text: He compares the rage of the people to a burning oven which the baker heats, until his dough is leavened and raised.

5.text: They used all indulgence and excess in their feasts and solemnities, by which their king was overcome with being fed too much, and brought into diseases, and who delighted in flatteries.

7.text: By their doing God has deprived them of all good rulers.

8.text: That is, he counterfeited the religion of the Gentiles, yet is but as a cake baked on the one side, and raw on the other, that is, neither thoroughly hot, nor thoroughly cold, but partly a Jew, and partly a Gentile.

9.text: Which are a token of his manifold afflictions.

11.text: That is, without all judgment, as those that cannot tell whether it is better to cleave only to God, or to seek the help of man.

12.text: According to my curses made to the whole congregation of Israel.

13.text: That is, at different times redeemed them, and delivered them from death.

14.text: When they were in affliction, and cried out in pain, they did not seek me for help.
They only seek their own benefit and wealth, and care not for me their God.

16.text: Because they boast of their own strength, and do not care what they speak against me and my servants; Psalms 73:9 .

1.text: God encourages the Prophet to signify the speedy coming of the enemy against Israel, which was once the people of God.

2.text: They will cry like hypocrites, but not from the heart, as their deeds declare.

4.text: That is, Jeroboam, by whom they sought their own liberty, and to obey my will.

5.text: That is, upright judgment and a godly life.

6.text: Meaning the calf was invented by themselves, and by their fathers in the wilderness.

7.text: Showing that their religion has but a show, and in itself is but vanity.

9.text: They never cease, but run to and fro to seek help.

10.text: That is, for the king and the princes will lay upon them: and by this means the Lord brings them to repentance.

12.text: In this way the idolaters consider the word of God as strange with regard to their own invention.

13.text: Saying that they offer it to the Lord, but he accepts no service which he himself has not appointed.

1.text: For even though all other people should escape, yet you will be punished.
You have committed idolatry in hope of reward, and to have your barns filled ( Jeremiah 44:17 ), as a harlot that had rather live by playing the whore, than to be provided for by her own husband.

2.text: These outward things that you seek will be taken from you.

4.text: All their doings both with regard to administration and religion, will be rejected as polluted things.
The meat offering which they offered for themselves.

5.text: When the Lord will take away all the occasions of serving him, which will be the most grievous part of your captivity, when you will see yourselves cut off from God.

6.text: Even though they think to escape by fleeing the destruction that is at hand, yet they will be destroyed in the place where they flee for help.

7.text: Then they will know that they were deluded by those who claimed themselves to be their prophets and spiritual men.

8.text: The Prophet’s duty is to bring men to God, and not to be a snare to pull them from God.

9.text: This people is so rooted in their wickedness, that Gibeah, which was similar to Sodom, was never more corrupt; Jud 19:22 .

10.text: Meaning, that he esteemed them and delighted in them in this way.
They were as abominable to me, as their lovers the idols.

11.text: Signifying that God would destroy their children by these different means, and so consume them by little and little.

13.text: As they kept tender plants in their houses in Tyrus to preserve them from the cold air of the sea, so was Ephraim at the first to me: but now I will give him to the slaughter.

14.text: The Prophet seeing the great plagues of God toward Ephraim, prays to God to make them barren, rather than that this great slaughter should come upon their children.

15.text: The chief cause of their destruction is that they commit idolatry, and corrupt my religion in Gilgal.

1.text: Of which though the grapes were gathered, yet always as it gathered new strength it increased in new wickedness, so that the correction which should have brought them to obedience, only proclaimed their stubbornness.
As they were rich and had abundance.

2.text: That is, from God, by serving their false gods.

3.text: The day will come that God will take away their king, and then they will feel the fruit of their sins, and how they trusted in him in vain; 2 Kings 17:6-7 .

4.text: In promising to be faithful toward God.
In this way their integrity and fidelity which they pretended, was nothing but bitterness and grief.

5.text: When the calf will be carried away.
These were certain idolatrous priests, who wore black apparel during their sacrifices, and cried with a loud voice: which superstition Elijah derided, 1 Kings 18:27 . See Geneva " 2 Kings 23:5 "

8.text: This he speaks in contempt of Bethel. Read Geneva (t) " Hosea 4:15 "

9.text: In those days you were as wicked as the Gibeonites, as God there partly declared: for your zeal could not be good in executing God’s judgments, seeing your own deeds were as wicked as theirs.
That is, to fight, or, the Israelites remained in that stubbornness from that time.
The Israelites were not moved by the example of the Gibeonites to cease from their sins.

10.text: Because they are so desperate, I will delight to destroy them.
That is, when they have gathered all their strength together.

11.text: In which is pleasure, whereas in plowing there is labour and pain.
I will lay my yoke upon her fat neck.

12.text: Read Geneva " Jeremiah 4:3 " See Jeremiah 4:4

14.text: That is, Shalmaneser in the destruction of that city spared neither type nor age.

1.text: While the Israelites were in Egypt, and did not provoke my wrath by their malice and ingratitude.

2.text: They rebelled and went a contrary way when the Prophets called them to repentance.

4.text: That is, friendly, and not as beasts or slaves.

5.text: Seeing that they condemn all this kindness, they will be led captive into Assyria.

7.text: That is, the Prophets.

8.text: God considers with himself, and that with a certain grief, how to punish them.
Which were two of the cities that were destroyed with Sodom; De 29:23 .

Meaning that his love with which he first loved them positioned him between doubt and assurance in terms of what to do: and in this appears his Fatherly affection, that his mercy toward his own will overcome his judgments, as he declares in the next verse.

9.text: To consume you, but will cause you to yield, and so have mercy on you: and this is meant of the final number who will walk after the Lord.

11.text: The Egyptians and the Assyrians will be afraid when the Lord maintains his people.

12.text: Governs their state according to God’s word, and does not degenerate.

1.text: That is, flatters himself with vain confidence.
Meaning presents to get friendship.

2.text: Which in those points was similar to Ephraim, but not in idolatry.

3.text: Seeing that God in this way preferred Jacob their father, Judah’s ingratitude was the more to be abhorred.

4.text: Read Genesis 32:24-32 .
God found Jacob as he lay sleeping in Bethel Genesis 28:12 , and spoke with him there in such a way that the fruit of that speech appertained to the whole body of the people, of which we are.

7.text: As for Ephraim, he is more like the wicked Canaanites than godly Abraham or Jacob.

8.text: Thus way the wicked measure God’s favour by outward prosperity, and like hypocrites cannot endure that any should reprove their doings.

9.text: Seeing you will not acknowledge my benefits, I will bring you again to dwell in tents, as in the feast of the Tabernacles, which you now condemn.

11.text: The people thought that no man dare have spoken against Gilead, that holy place, and yet the Prophet says that all their religion was but vanity.

12.text: If you boast of your riches and nobility, you seem to reproach your father, who was a poor fugitive and servant.

13.text: Meaning Moses, by which appears that whatever they have, it comes from God’s free goodness.

1.text: He shows the excellency and authority that this tribe had above all the rest.
He made a king of his tribe.
The Ephraimites are not far from destruction, and have lost their authority.

2.text: "Let the men that sacrifice" or "while they sacrifice men". The false prophets persuaded the idolaters to offer their children after the example of Abraham, and he shows how they would exhort one another to the same, and to kiss and worship these calves which were their idols.

4.text: He calls them to repentance, and reproves their ingratitude.

9.text: Your destruction is certain, and my benefits toward you declare that it comes not from me: therefore your own malice, idolatry, and vain confidence in men must necessarily be the cause of it.

10.text: I am all one; James 1:17 .

12.text: It is surely laid up to be punished, as in Jeremiah 17:1 .

13.text: But would come out of the womb, that is out of these dangers in which he is, and not wait to be suppressed.

14.text: Meaning that no power will resist God when he will deliver his own, but even in death he will give them life.
Because they will not turn to me, I will change my purpose.

1.text: He exhorts them to repentance to avoid all these plagues, exhorting them to declare by words their obedience and repentance.

2.text: He shows them that they ought to confess their sins.
Declaring that this is the true sacrifice that the faithful can offer, even thanks and praise; Hebrews 13:15 .

3.text: We will forsake all vain confidence and pride.

4.text: He declares how ready God is to receive those that do repent.

7.text: Whoever unites themselves to this people will be blessed.

8.text: God shows how prompt he is to hear his own when they repent, and to offer himself as a protection and safeguard for them, as a most sufficient fruit and benefit.

9.text: Signifying that the true wisdom and knowledge consists in this, even to rest upon God.

2.text: Signifying the princes, the priests, and the governors.
He calls the Jews to the consideration of God’s judgments, who had now plagued the fruits of the ground for the space of four years, which was because of their sins, and to call them to repentance.

5.text: Meaning, that the reason for their excess and drunkenness was taken away.

6.text: This was another plague with which God had punished them when he stirred up the Assyrians against them.

8.text: Mourn grievously as a woman who has lost her husband, to whom she has been married in her youth.

9.text: The signs of God’s wrath appeared in his temple, in so much that God’s service was discontinued.

10.text: All comfort and substance for nourishment is taken away.

13.text: He shows that the only means to avoid God’s wrath, and to have all things restored, is true repentance.

15.text: We see by these great plagues that utter destruction is at hand.

20.text: That is, drought.

1.text: He shows the great judgments of God which are at hand, unless they repent.

2.text: Of affliction and trouble.
Meaning, the Assyrians.

3.text: The enemy destroyed our plentiful country, wherever he went.

6.text: They will be pale and black because of fear, as in Nahum 2:10 .

8.text: For none will be able to resist them.

10.text: Read Joel 2:31 Isaiah 13:10 Ezekiel 32:7 Joel 3:15 Matthew 24:29

11.text: The Lord will stir up the Assyrians to execute his judgments.

13.text: Mortify your affections and serve God with pureness of heart, and not with ceremonies.

14.text: He speaks this to stir up their slothfulness, and not that he doubted of God’s mercies, if they did repent. For the way in which God repents, read Geneva " Jeremiah 18:8 "

16.text: That as all have sinned, so all may show forth signs of their repentance, so that men seeing the children who are not free from God’s wrath, might be the more deeply touched with the consideration of their own sins.

18.text: If they repent he shows that God will preserve and defend them with a most fervent affection.

20.text: That is, the Assyrians your enemies.
Called the Salt Sea, or Persian Sea: meaning, that even though this army was so great that it filled all from this sea to the Mediterranean Sea, yet he would scatter them.

23.text: That is, such as would come by just measure, and would be sent when God was reconciled with them.

28.text: That is, in greater abundance, and more broadly than in times past. And this was fulfilled under Christ, when God’s graces and his Spirit under the Gospel were abundantly given to the Church; Isaiah 44:3 Acts 2:17 John 7:38-39 .
As they had visions and dreams in ancient times, so will they now have clearer revelations.

30.text: He warns the faithful what terrible things would come, with the intent that they should not look for continual quietness in this world: and yet in all these troubles he would preserve them.

31.text: The order of nature will seem to be changed because of the horrible afflictions that will be in the world; Isaiah 13:10 Ezekiel 32:7 Joel 3:15 Matthew 24:29 .

32.text: God’s judgments are for the destruction of the unbelievers, and to exhort the godly to call upon the name of God, who will give them salvation.
Meaning the Gentiles by this; Romans 10:13 .

1.text: When I will deliver my Church, which consists of both Jews and Gentiles.

2.text: It appears that he alludes to the great victory of Jehoshaphat, whom God used without man’s help to destroy the enemies, 2 Chronicles 20:20-26 ; also he is referring to this word Jehoshaphat, which signifies pleading or judgment, because God would judge the enemies of his Church, as he did there.

3.text: That which the enemy received for the sale of my people, they bestowed upon harlots and drink.

4.text: He takes the cause of his Church in hand against the enemy, as though the injury were done to himself.
Have I done you wrong, that you will render me the same?

8.text: For afterward God sold them by Nebuchadnezzar and Alexander the Great, because of the love he had for his people, and by this they were comforted, as though they themselves had sold them.

10.text: When I will execute my judgments against my enemies, I will cause everyone to be ready, and to prepare their weapons to destroy one another, for my Church’s sake.

13.text: In this way he will encourage the enemies when their wickedness is completely ripe to destroy one another, which he calls the valley of God’s judgment.

16.text: God assures his own against all trouble, that when he destroys his enemies, his children will be delivered.

17.text: The strangers will no longer destroy his Church: and if they do, it is the fault of the people, who by their sins make the breach for the enemy.

18.text: He promises to his Church abundance of graces, see Geneva " Ezekiel 47:1 ", which would water and comfort the most barren places; Amos 9:13 .

19.text: The malicious enemies will have no part of these graces.

21.text: He had allowed his Church before this to lie in their filthiness, but now he promises to cleanse them and to make them pure unto himself.

1.text: Which was a town five miles from Jerusalem in Judea, but he prophesied in Israel.
In his days the kingdom of Israel flourished the most.
Which as Josephus writes, was when Uzziah would have usurped the priest’s office, and therefore was smitten with leprosy.

2.text: Whatever is fruitful and pleasant in Israel, will shortly perish.

3.text: He shows first that all the people round about would be destroyed for their manifold sins: which are meant by three and four, which make seven, so that the Israelites would the more deeply consider God’s judgments toward them.

If the Syrians will not be spared for committing this cruelty against one city, it is not possible that Israel would escape punishment, which has committed so many and such grievous sins against God and man.

4.text: The antiquity of their buildings will not avoid my judgments. Read Geneva " Jeremiah 49:27 "

5.text: Tiglath Pileser led the Assyrians captive, and brought them to Cyrene, which he here calls Kir.

6.text: They united themselves with the Edomites their enemies, who carried them away captive.

9.text: For Esau (from whom came the Edomites) and Jacob were brothers, therefore they ought to have admonished them by their brotherly friendship, and not to have provoked them to hatred.

11.text: He was a continual enemy to him.

13.text: He notes the great cruelty of the Ammonites, that did not spare the women, but most tyrannously tormented them, and yet the Ammonites came from Lot, who was of the household of Abraham.

1.text: For the Moabites were so cruel against the King of Edom, that they burnt his bones after he was dead: which declared their barbarous rage, that they would avenge themselves upon the dead.

4.text: Seeing that the Gentiles who did have as much knowledge were punished in this way, Judah which was so fully instructed by the Lord’s will, should not think that they would escape.

6.text: If he did not spare Judah unto whom his promises were made, much more he will not spare this degenerate kingdom.
They esteemed most vile bribes more than men’s lives.

7.text: When they have robbed him and thrown him to the ground, they open wide their mouths for his life.

8.text: Thinking that by these ceremonies, that is, by sacrificing, and by being near my altar, they may excuse all of their other wickedness.
They rob others and offer it to God, thinking that he will exempt them, when he is made partaker of their iniquity.

9.text: The destruction of their enemies and his mercy toward them, should have caused their hearts to melt because of love toward him.

11.text: You condemned my benefits, and abused my graces, and craftily went about to stop the mouths of my Prophets.

13.text: You have wearied me with your sins; Isaiah 1:14 .

14.text: None will be delivered by any means.

2.text: I have only chosen you to be mine among all other people, and yet you have forsaken me.

3.text: By this the Prophet signifies that he speaks not of himself, but as God guides and moves him, which is called the agreement between God and his Prophets.

4.text: Will God threaten by his Prophet, unless there is some great occasion?

5.text: Can anything come without God’s providence?
Will his threatenings be in vain?

6.text: Will the Prophet’s threaten God’s judgments and the people not be afraid?
Does any adversity come without God’s appointment? Isaiah 45:7

7.text: God does not deal with the Israelites as he does with other people: for he always warns them before of his plagues by his Prophets.

8.text: Because the people always murmured against the Prophets, he shows that God’s Spirit moved them to speak as they did.

9.text: He calls the strangers, such as the Philistines and Egyptians, to be witness of God’s judgments against the Israelites for their cruelty and oppression.

10.text: The fruit of their cruelty and theft appears by their great riches, which they have in their houses.

12.text: When the lion has satisfied his hunger, the shepherd finds a leg or a piece of an ear, to show that the sheep have been torn by his teeth.
Where they thought to have had a sure stronghold, and to have been in safety.

1.text: Thus he calls the princes and governors, who being overwhelmed with the great abundance of God’s benefits, forgot God, and therefore he calls them by the name of beasts and not of men.
They encourage those who have authority over the people to oppress them, so that they may have profit by it.

2.text: He alludes to fishers, who catch fish by hooks or thorns.

4.text: He speaks this in contempt of those who resorted to those places, thinking that their great devotion and good intention was sufficient to have bound God to them.
Read De 14:28 .

5.text: As Leviticus 7:13 .
You only delight in these outward ceremonies and care for nothing else.

6.text: That is, lack of bread and meat.

7.text: I stopped the rain until the fruits of the earth were destroyed with drought, and yet you would not consider to return to me by repentance.

8.text: They could not find enough water where they had heard that it had rained.

10.text: As I plagued the Egyptians; Exodus 9:10 .

11.text: You were almost all consumed, and a few of you were wonderfully preserved; 2 Kings 14:26 .

12.text: Turn to him by repentance.

2.text: He so calls them, because they so boasted of themselves, or because they were given to lustfulness and daintiness.

3.text: Meaning, that the tenth part would hardly be saved.

5.text: In those places they worshipped new idols, which before served for the true honour of God: therefore he says that these will not save them.

7.text: Instead of judgment and fairness they execute cruelty and oppression.

8.text: He describes the power of God; Job 9:9 .

10.text: They hate the Prophets, who reprove them in the open assemblies.

11.text: You take both his money and also his food, with which he should live.

13.text: God will so plague them that they will not allow the godly to open their mouths once to admonish them of their faults.

16.text: So that people of all types will have reason to lament because of the great plagues.

18.text: He speaks in this way because the wicked and hypocrites said they were content to endure God’s judgments, whereas the godly tremble and fear; Jeremiah 30:7 , Joel 2:2 ; Joel 2:11 , Zephaniah 1:15 .

22.text: Because you have corrupted my true service, and remain obstinate in your vices; Isaiah 1:11 , Jeremiah 6:10 .

24.text: Do your duty to God, and to your neighbour, and so you will plentifully feel his grace, if you show your abundant affections according to God’s word.

26.text: That idol which you esteemed as your king, and carried about as you did Chiun, in which images you thought that there was a certain divinity.

1.text: The Prophet threatens the wealthy, who did not regard God’s plagues, nor threatenings by his Prophets.

These two cities were famous from their first inhabitants the Canaanites: and seeing that before they did not avail those that were born here, why should you think that they should save you who were brought in to dwell in other men’s possessions?

2.text: If God has destroyed these excellent cities in three different kingdoms, that is Babylon, Syria, and that of the Philistines, and has narrowed their wide borders more than yours yet are, do you think that you are better, or that you will escape?

3.text: You that continue still in your wickedness, and think that God’s plagues are not at hand, but give yourselves to all idleness, lustfulness, and disorder.

5.text: As he caused different types of instruments to be made to serve God’s glory, so these did strive to invent as many to serve their unrestrained affections and lusts.

6.text: They did not pity their brethren, of which many were now slain and carried away captive.

7.text: Some read "the sorrow of them that stretched themselves is at hand".

8.text: Read Jeremiah 51:14 .
That is, the riches and pomp.

10.text: The destruction will be so great, that almost none will be left to bury the dead: and therefore they will burn them at home, to carry out the burnt ashes with more ease.
That is, to some neighbour that dwells near by.

They will be so astonished at this destruction, that they will not boast any more of the name of God, and that they are his people: but they will be silent when they hear God’s name, and abhor it, as those that are desperate, or reprobate.

12.text: He compares them to barren rocks, upon which it is in vain to bestow labour: showing that God’s benefits can have no place among them.
Read Amos 5:7 .

13.text: That is, power and glory.

14.text: From one corner of the country to another.

1.text: To devour the land: and he alludes to the invading of the enemies.
After the public commandment for mowing was given: or as some read, when the kings sheep were shorn.

3.text: That is, stopped this plague at my prayer.

4.text: Meaning, that God’s indignation was inflamed against the stubbornness of this people.

7.text: Signifying that this would be the last measuring of the people, and that he would defer his judgment no longer.

10.text: That is, when Amos had prophesied that the king would be destroyed: for the wicked priest more for hatred he had for the Prophet than for love toward the king, thought this accusation sufficient to condemn him. However, only what the Prophet said could take place.

12.text: When this instrument of Satan was not able to accomplish his purpose by the king, he tried by another practice, that was, to scare the Prophet, that he might depart, and not reprove their idolatry there openly, and so hinder his profit.

14.text: Thus he shows by his extraordinary calling, that God had given him a charge, which he must necessarily execute.

17.text: In this way God used to approve the authority of his Prophets, by his plagues and judgments against those who were malicious enemies as in Jer 28:12-17 29:21-26, as this day he does against those that persecute the ministers of his Gospel.

2.text: Which signified the ripeness of their sins, and the readiness of God’s judgments.

3.text: There will be none left to mourn for them.

4.text: By stopping the sale of food and necessary things which you have gotten into your own hands, and so cause the poor to spend quickly that little that they have, and at length because of need to become your slaves.

5.text: When the scarcity had come they were so greedy for gain, that they thought the holy day to be a hindrance to them.
That is, the measure small, and the price great.

8.text: That is, the inhabitants of the land will be drowned, as the Nile drowns many when it overflows.

9.text: In the midst of their prosperity, I will send great affliction.

12.text: By which he shows that they will not only perish in body, but also in soul for lack of God’s word, which is the food of it.

14.text: For the idolaters used to swear by their idols, which here he calls their sin: and the papists yet swear by theirs.
That is, the common manner of worshipping, and the service or religion used there.

1.text: Which was at Jerusalem: for he did not appear in the idolatrous places of Israel.
Both the most important of them, and also the common people.

3.text: He shows that God will declare himself as an enemy to them in all places, and that his elements and all his creatures will be enemies to destroy them.

6.text: He declares by the wonderful power of God, by the making of the heavens and the elements, that it is not possible for man to escape his judgments when he punishes.

7.text: Am I more bound to you than to the Ethiopians, or other people? Yet I have bestowed upon you greater benefits.
Read Jeremiah 47:4 .

8.text: Though he destroys the rebellious multitude, yet he will always reserve the remnant of his Church to call upon his name.

9.text: Meaning that none of his own would perish in his wrath.

11.text: I will send the promised Messiah, and restore by him the spiritual Israel; Acts 15:16 .

12.text: Meaning, the very enemies (as were the Edomites) and others would be united with the Jews in one society and body, of which Christ would be the head.

13.text: Signifying, that there will be great abundance of all things, so that when one type of fruit is ripe, another would follow, and every one in order; Leviticus 26:5 .
Read Joel 3:18 .

14.text: The accomplishment of this is under Christ, when they are planted in this Church, out of which they can never be pulled, after they have once been grafted into it.

1.text: God has certainly revealed to his prophets, that he will raise up the heathen to destroy the Edomites, concerning which the rumour is now proclaimed; Jeremiah 49:14 .
Thus the heathen encourage themselves to rise against Edom.

3.text: Which despises all others in respect of yourself, and yet you are but a handful in comparison with others, and you are shut up among the hills as separate from the rest of the world.

5.text: God will so destroy them that he will leave none, even though thieves when they come take but until they have enough, and they that gather grapes always leave some behind them. See Geneva " Jeremiah 49:9 "

7.text: Those in whom you trusted to have help and friendship, will be your enemies and destroy you.
That is, your familiar friends and guests have by secret practices destroyed you.

10.text: He shows the reason why the Edomites were so severely punished: that is, because they were enemies to his Church, whom he now comforts by punishing their enemies.

11.text: When Nebuchadnezzar came against Jerusalem, you joined with him, and had part of the spoil, and so rejoiced when my people (that is, your brother), were afflicted, whereas you should have pitied and helped your brother.

12.text: When the Lord deprived them of their former dignity, and delivered them to be carried into captivity.

15.text: When he will summon all the heathen, and send them to destroy you.

16.text: That is, rejoiced and triumphed.
The Edomites will be utterly destroyed, and yet in spite of all the enemies I will reserve my Church and restore it.

18.text: God attributes this power to consume his enemies to his Church, which power properly belongs only to himself; Isaiah 10:17 , De 4:24, Hebrews 12:29 .

19.text: He describes how the Church will be enlarged and have great possessions: but this is mainly accomplished under Christ, when that faithful are made heirs and lords of all things by him who is their head.

20.text: By the Canaanites, the Jews mean the Dutchmen, and by Zarephath, France, and by Sepharad, Spain.

21.text: Meaning that God will raise up in his Church those who will rule and govern for the defence of it, and for the destruction of his enemies under the Messiah, whom the Prophet here calls the Lord and head of this kingdom.

1.text: After he had preached a long time in Israel: and so Ezekiel, after he had prophesied in Judah for a time, had visions in Babylon; Ezekiel 1:1 .

2.text: For seeing the great obstipation of the Israelites, he sent his Prophet to the Gentiles, that they might provoke them to repentance, or at least make them inexcusable: for Nineveh was the chief city of the Assyrians.
For as authors write, it contained in circuit about forty-eight miles, and had 1500 towers, and at this time there were 120,000 children in it; Jonah 4:11 .

3.text: By which he declares his weakness, that would not promptly follow the Lord’s calling, but gave place to his own reason, which persuaded him that he would not profit these people at all, seeing he had done such little good among his own people; Jonah 4:2 .
Which was the haven, and port to take shipping there, also called Joppa.
From that vocation to which God had called him, and in which he would have assisted him.

5.text: As one that would have cast off this care and concern by seeking rest and quietness.

6.text: As they had called on their idols, which declares that idolaters have no rest nor certainty, but in their troubles seek what they do not even know.

7.text: Which declares that the matter was very extreme and in doubt, which was God’s way of getting them to test for the cause: and this may not be done except in matters of great importance.

14.text: This declares that the very wicked in their time of need flee to God for help, and also that they are touched with a certain fear of shedding man’s blood, whereas they know no manifest sign of wickedness.

16.text: They were touched with a certain repentance of their past life, and began to worship the true God by whom they saw themselves as wonderfully delivered. But this was done for fear, and not from a pure heart and affection, neither according to God’s word.

17.text: Thus the Lord would chastise his Prophet with a most terrible spectacle of death, and by this also strengthened and encouraged him of his favour and support in this duty which was commanded him.

1.text: Being now swallowed up by death, and seeing no remedy to escape, his faith broke out to the Lord, knowing that out of this very hell he was able to deliver him.

2.text: For he was now in the fishes belly as in a grave or place of darkness.

4.text: This declared what his prayer was, and how he laboured between hope and despair, considering the neglect of his vocation, and God’s judgments for it: but yet in the end faith gained the victory.

6.text: You have delivered me from the belly of the fish and all these dangers, as it were raising me from death to life.

8.text: Those that depend upon anything except on God alone.
They refuse their own felicity, and that goodness which they would otherwise receive from God.

1.text: This is a great declaration of God’s mercy, that he receives him again, and sends him forth as his Prophet, who had before shown such great weakness.

3.text: Read Geneva (c) " Jonah 1:2 "

4.text: He went forward one day in the city and preached, and so he continued until the city was converted.

5.text: For he declared that he was a Prophet sent to them from God, to make known his judgments against them.

7.text: Not that the dumb beasts had sinned or could repent, but that by their example man might be astonished, considering that for his sin the anger of God hung over all creatures.

8.text: He exhorted that the men should earnestly call to God for mercy.

9.text: For partly from the threatening of the prophet, and partly from his own conscience, he doubted whether God would show them mercy.

10.text: That is, the fruits of their repentance, which proceeded from faith, which God had planted by the ministry of his Prophet.
Read Geneva " Jeremiah 18:8 "

1.text: Because by this he would be taken as a false prophet, and so the name of God, which he preached, would be blasphemed.

2.text: Read Jonah 1:3 .

3.text: Thus he prayed from grief, fearing that God’s name by this forgiveness might be blasphemed, as though he sent his Prophets forth to make known his judgments in vain.

4.text: Will you judge when I do things for my glory, and when I do not?

5.text: For he doubted as yet whether God would show them mercy or not, and therefore after forty days he departed out of the city, to see what God would do.

6.text: Which was a further means to cover him from the heat of the sun, as he remained in his booth.

9.text: This declares the great inconveniences into which God’s servants fall when they give place to their own affections, and do not in all things willingly submit themselves to God.

11.text: Thus God mercifully reproves him who would pity himself and this gourd, and yet would keep God from showing his compassion to so many thousand people.
Meaning that they were children and infants.

1.text: Born in Mareshah, a city of Judah.

2.text: Because of the malice and obstinacy of the people, whom he had so often exhorted to repentance, he summons them to God’s judgments, taking all creatures, and God himself as witness, that the preaching of the Prophets, which they have abused, will be avenged.

3.text: Meaning by this that God will come to judgment against the strong cities and strongholds.

5.text: Samaria, which should have been an example to all Israel of true religion and justice, was the dirty pool and the tank that all idolatry and corruption was kept alive in, and who prided themselves in their father Jacob, and boasted of him.
That is, the idolatry and infection.

7.text: Which they gathered by evil practices, and thought that their idols had enriched them with these wages because of their service to them.
The gain that came by their idols will be consumed as a thing of nothing: for as the wages or riches of harlots are wickedly gotten, so are they vilely and quickly spent.

10.text: Lest the Philistines our enemies rejoice at our destruction.
Which was a city near to Jerusalem Joshua 18:23 , there called Ophrah, and signifies dust: therefore he wants them to mourn and roll themselves in the dust, for their dusty city.

11.text: These were cities by which the enemy would pass as he came to Judah.
He will not depart before he has overcome you, and so you will pay for his staying.

12.text: For Rabshakeh had shut up Jerusalem, so that they could not send to help them.

13.text: To flee away: for Sennacherib laid siege first to that city, and remained there when he sent his captains and army against Jerusalem.
You first received the idolatry of Jeroboam, and so infected Jerusalem.

14.text: You will bribe the Philistines your neighbours, but they will deceive you, as well as those of Jerusalem.

15.text: He prophesies against his own city: and because it signified a heritage, he says that God would send an heir to possess it.
For so they thought themselves because of the strength of their cities.

1.text: As soon as they rise, they execute their wicked devices of the night, and according to their ability hurt others.

4.text: Thus the Jews lament and say that there is no hope of restitution, seeing their possessions are divided among the enemies.

5.text: You will have no more lands to divide as you had in times past, and as you used to measure them in the Jubilee.

6.text: Thus the people warn the prophets that they speak to them no more, for they cannot endure their threatenings.
God says that they will not prophesy, nor receive any more of their rebukes or taunts.

7.text: Are these your works according to his Law?
Do not the godly find my words comfortable?

8.text: That is, in past times.
The poor can have no benefit from them, but they rob them, as though they were enemies.

9.text: That is, their substance and living, which is God’s blessing, and as it were part of his glory.

10.text: Jerusalem will not be your safeguard, but rather the cause of your destruction.

11.text: That is, show himself to be a prophet.
He shows what prophets they delight in, that is, in flatterers, who tell them pleasant tales, and speak of their benefits.

12.text: To destroy you.

13.text: The enemy will break their gates and walls, and lead them into Chaldea.
To drive them forward, and to help their enemies.

1.text: That thing which is just and lawful, both to govern my people properly, and also to clear your own conscience.

2.text: The Prophet condemns the wicked governors not only of covetousness, theft, and murder, but compares them to wolves, lions, and most cruel beasts.

4.text: That is, when I will punish their wickedness: for though I hear the godly before they cry Isaiah 65:24 , yet I will not hear these even though they cry; Isaiah 1:15 Ezekiel 8:18 James 2:13 1 Peter 3:11-12 .

5.text: They devour all their substance, and then flatter them, promising that all will go well. But if someone does not feed them, then they invent all ways to do evil.

6.text: As you have loved to walk in darkness, and to prophesy lies, so God will reward you with gross blindness and ignorance, so that when all others will see the bright beams of God’s grace, you will as blind men grope as in the night.

7.text: When God will reveal them to the world, they will be afraid to speak: for all will know that they were but false prophets, and did give a false notion of the word of God.

8.text: The Prophet being assured of his vocation by the Spirit of God, sets himself alone against all the wicked, showing how God gave him gifts, ability and knowledge, to discern between good and evil, and also steadfastness and endurance to reprove the sins of the people, and not to flatter them.

10.text: They will say that they are the people of God, and abuse his name, as a pretence to disguise their hypocrisy.

12.text: Read Jeremiah 26:18 .

1.text: When Christ will come, and the temple will be destroyed.
Read Geneva (a),(b),(c) " Isaiah 2:2 "

2.text: He shows that there is no true Church, except where the people are taught by God’s pure word.

3.text: By his corrections and threatenings he will bring the people into subjection who are in the utmost corners of the world.
They will abstain from all evil doing, and exercise themselves in godliness and in well doing to others.
Read Isaiah 2:4

5.text: He shows that the people of God ought to remain constant in their religion, even if all the world should give themselves to their superstition and idolatry.

7.text: I will cause that Israel, who is now as one lame and halting, and so almost destroyed, to live again, and grow into a great people.

8.text: Meaning Jerusalem, where the Lord’s flock was gathered.
The flourishing state of the kingdom, as it was under David and Solomon, which thing was accomplished for the Church by the coming of Christ.

9.text: In the meantime he shows that they would endure great troubles and temptations, when they saw themselves neither to have king nor counsel.

12.text: He shows that the faithful ought not to measure God’s judgments by the braggings and threatenings of the wicked, but by these are admonished to lift up their hearts to God to call for deliverance.

13.text: God gives his Church this victory, as often as he overcomes their enemies: but the accomplishment of this will be at the last coming of Christ.

1.text: He forewarns them of the dangers that will come before they enjoy these comforts, showing that inasmuch as Jerusalem was accustomed with her garrisons to trouble others, the Lord would now cause other garrisons to vex her, and that her rulers would be hit on the face most contemptuously.

2.text: For so the Jews divided their country that for every thousand there was a chief captain: and because Bethlehem was not able to make a thousand, he calls it little. But yet God will raise up his captain and governor in it: and thus it is not the least by reason of this benefit. See Geneva " Matthew 2:6 "
He shows that the coming of Christ and all his ways were appointed by God from all eternity.

3.text: He compares the Jews to women with child, who for a time would have great sorrows, but at length they would have a comfortable deliverance; John 16:21 .

4.text: That is, Christ’s kingdom will be stable and everlasting, and his people, the Gentiles as well as the Jews, will dwell in safety.

5.text: This Messiah will be a sufficient safeguard for us, and though the enemy invades us for a time, yet will God stir up many who will be able to deliver us.

6.text: These whom God will raise up for the deliverance of his Church, will destroy all the enemies of it, who are meant here by the Assyrians and Babylonians, who were the chief enemies at that time.
By these governors will God deliver us when the enemy comes into our land.

7.text: This remnant or Church which God will deliver will only depend on God’s power and defence (as does the grass of the field), and not on the hope of man.

10.text: I will destroy all things in which you put your confidence, such as your vain self-reliance and idolatry, and in doing this I will be helping you.

15.text: It will be so terrible that nothing like it has been heard of.

1.text: He took the high mountains and hard rocks as witnesses against the obstinacy of his people.

4.text: I have not hurt you, but bestowed infinite benefits upon you.

5.text: That is, remember my benefits from the beginning, how I delivered you from Balaam’s curse, and also spared you from Shittim which was in the plain of Moab, until I brought you into the promised land.
That is, the truth of his promise and his manifold benefits toward you.

6.text: Thus the people by hypocrisy ask how to please God, and are content to offer sacrifices, but will not change their lives.

7.text: There is nothing so dear to man, but the hypocrites will offer it to God, if they think by this to avoid his anger. But they will never by brought to mortify their own affections, and to give themselves willingly to serve God as he commands.

8.text: The Prophet in few words calls them to the observation of the second table of the ten commandments, to know if they will obey God correctly or not, saying that God has commanded them to do this.

9.text: Meaning, that when God speaks to any city or nation, the godly will acknowledge his majesty and not consider the mortal man that brings the threatening, but God that sends it.

12.text: That is, of Jerusalem.

14.text: You will be consumed with inward grief and evils.
Meaning that the city would go about to save her men, as they that lay hold of that which they would preserve.

16.text: You have received all the corruption and idolatry with which the ten tribes were infected under Omri and Ahab his son: and to excuse your doings, you allege the King’s authority by his statutes, and also wisdom and policy in so doing, but you will not escape punishment. But as I have shown you great favour, and taken you for my people, so will your plagues be according as your sins; Lu 12:47 .

1.text: The Prophet takes upon himself the voice of the earth, which complains that all her fruits are gone, so that none are left: that is, that there is no godly man remaining, for all are given to cruelty and deceit, so that none spares his own brother.

2.text: He shows that the prince, the judge, and the rich man are all linked together to do evil, and to disguise the deeds of one another.

3.text: That is, the rich man that is able to give money, abstains from no wickedness or injury.
These men agree among themselves, and conspire with one another to do evil.

4.text: They that are of most estimation and are counted most honest among them, are but thorns and briers to prick.
Meaning the prophets and governors.

7.text: The Prophet shows that the only remedy for the godly in desperate evils, is to flee to God for help.

8.text: This is spoken in the voice of the Church, which calls the malignant church her enemy.

11.text: That is, when God will show himself to be a deliverer of his Church, and a destroyer of his enemies.
Meaning the cruel empire of the Babylonians.

12.text: When the Church will be restored, those that were enemies before will come out of all the corners of the world to her, so that neither fortresses, rivers, seas, nor mountains will be able to stop them.

13.text: Before this grace appears, he shows how grievously the hypocrites themselves will be punished, seeing that the earth itself, which cannot sin, will be made waste because of their wickedness.

14.text: The Prophet prays to God to be merciful to his Church, when they would be scattered abroad as in solitary places in Babylon, and to be beneficial to them as in times past.

15.text: God promises to be favourable to his people, as he had been before.

16.text: They will be as dumb men, and dare brag no more.
They will be astonished and afraid to hear men speak, lest they should hear of their destruction.

17.text: They will fall flat on the ground because of fear.

18.text: As though he did not see it, ignoring it.

19.text: Meaning his elect.

20.text: The Church is assured that God will perform the truth of his merciful promise, which he had made long ago to Abraham, and to all that would apprehend the promise by faith.

1.text: Read Geneva " Isaiah 13:1 "
The vision or revelation, which God commanded Nahum to write concerning the Ninevites.
That is, born in a poor village in the tribe of Simeon.

2.text: Meaning, of his glory.
With his own he is but angry for a time, but his anger is never appeased toward the reprobate, even though he defers it for a time.

3.text: Thus the wicked would make God’s mercy an occasion to sin, but the Prophet wishes them to consider his power and justice.

6.text: If all creatures are at God’s commandment, and none are able to resist his wrath, will man flatter himself, and think by any means to escape, when he provokes his God to anger?

7.text: Lest the faithful should be discouraged by hearing the power of God, he shows them that his mercy appertains to them, and that he has care over them.

8.text: Signifying that God will suddenly destroy Nineveh and the Assyrians in such a way, that they will lie in perpetual darkness, and never recover their strength again.

9.text: He shows that the undertakings of the Assyrians against Judah and the Church were against God, and therefore he would so destroy them the first time, that he would not need to return the second time.

10.text: Though the Assyrians think themselves like thorns that prick on all sides, yet the Lord will set fire on them, and as drunken men are not able to stand against any force, so they will not be able to resist him at all.

11.text: Which may be understood either of Sennacherib, or of the whole body of the people of Nineveh.

12.text: Though they think themselves in most safety, and of greatest strength, yet when God will pass by, he will destroy them: nonetheless, he comforts his Church, and promises to stop punishing them by the Assyrians.

14.text: Meaning, Sennacherib, who would have no more children, but be slain in the house of his gods; 2 Kings 19:36-37 .

15.text: Which peace the Jews would enjoy by the death of Sennacherib.

1.text: That is, Nebuchadnezzar is in readiness to destroy the Assyrians: and the Prophet derides the undertakings of the Assyrians who prepared to resist him.

2.text: Seeing God has punished his own people Judah and Israel, he will now punish the enemies by whom he scourged them; read Isaiah 10:12 .
Signifying that the Israelites were utterly destroyed.

3.text: Both to put fear into the enemy, and also that they themselves should not so soon detect blood among one another, to discourage them.
Meaning their spears would shake and crash together.

5.text: Then the Assyrians will seek by all means to gather their power, but all things will fail them.

8.text: The Assyrians will flatter themselves and say that Nineveh is so ancient that it can never perish, and is as a fishpool, whose waters cannot be touched by those that walk on the banks. But they will be scattered, and will not look back, even if men call them.

9.text: God commands the enemies to spoil Nineveh, and promises them infinite riches and treasures.

10.text: That is, Nineveh, and the men of it will be after this manner.
Read Geneva " Joel 2:6 "

11.text: Meaning, Nineveh, whose inhabitants were cruel like the lions, and given to all oppression, and spared no violence or tyranny to provide for their wives and children.

13.text: That is, as soon as my wrath begins to burn.
Signifying the heralds, who were accustomed to proclaim war. Some read, "of you gum teeth", with which Nineveh was accustomed to bruise the bones of the poor.

1.text: It never ceases to spoil and rob.

2.text: He shows how the Chaldeans will hasten, and how courageous their horses will be in beating the ground when they come against the Assyrians.

4.text: He compares Nineveh to a harlot, who by her beauty and subtilty entices young men, and brings them to destruction.

8.text: Meaning Alexandria, which had a compact of peace with so many nations, and yet was now destroyed.

15.text: Signifying that God’s judgments would suddenly destroy the Assyrians, as these vermin do with rain or change of weather.

18.text: Your princes and counsellors.

19.text: Meaning that the Assyrians had done hurt to all people.

2.text: The Prophet complains to God, and bewails that among the Jews is left no fairness and brotherly love: but instead of these reigns cruelty, theft, contention, and strife.

4.text: To suppress him, if any should show himself zealous of God’s cause.
Because the judges who should remedy this excess, are as evil as the rest.

5.text: As in times past you would not believe God’s word, so you will not now believe the strange plagues which are at hand.

7.text: They themselves will be your judges in this cause, and none will have authority over them to control them.

9.text: For the Jews most feared this wind, because it destroyed their fruits.
They will be so many in number.

10.text: They will cast up mounds against it.

11.text: The Prophet comforts the faithful that God will also destroy the Babylonians, because they will abuse this victory, and become proud and insolent, attributing the praise of this to their idols.

12.text: He assures the godly of God’s protection, showing that the enemy can do no more than God has appointed, and also that their sins require such a sharp rod.

14.text: So that the great devours the small, and the Chaldeans destroy all the world.

16.text: Meaning that the enemies flatter themselves, and glory in their own strength, power, and intellect.

17.text: Meaning, that they would not.

1.text: I will renounce my own judgment, and only depend on God to be instructed what I will answer those that abuse my preaching, and to be armed against all temptations.

2.text: Write it in great letters, that he that runneth may read it.

3.text: Which contained the destruction of the enemy, and the comfort of the Church. And even though God does not execute this according to man’s hasty affections, yet the issue of both is certain at his appointed time.

4.text: To trust in himself, or in any worldly thing, is never to be at peace: for the only rest is to trust in God by faith; Romans 1:17 , Galatians 3:11 , Hebrews 10:38 .

5.text: He compares the proud and covetous man to a drunkard that is without reason and sense, whom God will punish and make a laughing stock to all the world: and this he speaks for the comfort of the godly, and against the Chaldeans.

6.text: Signifying that all the world will wish the destruction of tyrants, and that by their oppression and covetousness, they heap but upon themselves more heavy burdens: for the more they get, the more are they troubled.

7.text: That is, the Medes and persians, that would destroy the Babylonians?

10.text: Signifying that the covetous man is the ruin of his own house, when he thinks to enrich it be cruelty and oppression.

11.text: The stones of the house will cry, and say that they are built from blood, and the wood will answer and say the same of itself.

13.text: Meaning, that God will not defer his vengeance long, but will come and destroy all their labours, as though they were consumed with fire.

14.text: In the destruction of the Babylonians his glory will appear through all the world.

15.text: He reproaches by this the king of Babylon, who as he was drunken with covetousness and cruelty, so he provoked others to the same, and inflamed them by his madness, and so in the end brought them to shame.

16.text: Whereas you thought to have the glory of these your doings, they will turn to your shame: for you will drink of the same cup with others in your turn.

17.text: Because the Babylonians were cruel not only against other nations, but also against the people of God, which is meant by Lebanon and the beast in it, he shows that the same cruelly will be executed against them.

18.text: He shows that the Babylonian gods could not help them at all, for they were but blocks or stones. See Geneva Jer "10:8"

19.text: If you will consider what it is, and how it has neither breath nor life, but is a dead thing.

1.text: "upon Shigionoth" or "for the ignorance". The prophet instructs his people to pray to God, not only because of their great sins, but also for those they had committed in ignorance.

2.text: Thus the people were afraid when they heard God’s threatenings, and prayed.
That is, the state of your Church which is now ready to perish, before it comes to half a perfect age, which would be under Christ.

3.text: Teman and Paran were near Sinai, where the Law was given: by which is signified that his deliverance was as present now as it was then.

4.text: By which is meant a power that was joined with his brightness, which was hidden to the rest of the world, but was revealed at Mount Sinai to his people; Psalms 31:16 .

6.text: Signifying that God has wonderful means, and always has a marvellous power when he will deliver his Church.

7.text: The iniquity of the king of Syria in vexing your people was made manifest by your judgment, to the comfort of your Church, Jud 5:10 , and also of the Midianites, who destroyed themselves, Jud 7:22 .

8.text: Meaning that God was not angry with the waters, but that by this means he would destroy his enemies, and deliver his Church.
And so did use all the elements as instruments for the destruction of your enemies.

9.text: That is, your power.
For he had not only made a covenant with Abraham, but renewed it with his posterity.
Read Numbers 20:11 .

10.text: He alludes to the Red Sea and Jordan, which gave passage to God’s people, and showed signs of their obedience as it were by the lifting up of their hands.

11.text: As appears in Joshua 10:12 .
According to your command the sun was directed by the weapons of your people, that fought in your cause, as though it dare not go forward.

13.text: Signifying that there is no salvation, except by Christ.
From the top to the bottom you have destroyed the enemies.

14.text: God destroyed his enemies both great and small with their own weapons, though they were ever so fierce against his Church.

16.text: He returns to that which he spoke as in, Habakkuk 3:2 and shows how he was afraid of God’s judgments.
He shows that the faithful can never have true rest, except that which they feel before the weight of God’s judgments.
That is, the enemy, but the godly will be quiet, knowing that all things will turn to good for them.

18.text: He declares in what the joy of the faithful consists, though they see ever so great afflictions prepared.

19.text: The chief singer upon the instruments of music, will have occasion to praise God for this great deliverance of his Church.

3.text: Not that God was angry with these dumb creatures, but because man was so wicked for whose cause they were created, God makes them to take part of the punishments with him.

4.text: Who were an order of superstitious priests appointed to minister in the service of Baal, and were as his special chaplains; read 2 Kings 23:5 , Hosea 10:5 .

5.text: He alludes to their idol Molech, which was forbidden; read Leviticus 20:2 , yet they called him their king, and made him as a god: therefore he here notes those that will both say they worship God, and yet will swear by idols and serve them: which faltering is here condemned, as in Ezekiel 20:39 , 1 Kings 18:21 , 2 Kings 17:33 .

8.text: Meaning, the courtiers, who did imitate the strange apparel of other nations to win their favour by it, and to appear glorious in the eyes of all others; read Ezekiel 23:14-15 .

9.text: He means the servants of the rulers who invade other men’s houses, and rejoice and leap for joy, when they can get any gain to please their master with.

10.text: Signifying that all the corners of the city of Jerusalem would be full of trouble.

11.text: This is meant of the street of the merchants which was lower than the rest of the place around it.

12.text: So that nothing will escape me.
By their prosperity they are hardened in their wickedness.

14.text: They that trusted in their own strength and condemned the Prophets of God.

1.text: He exhorts them to repentance, and wills them to descend into themselves and gather themselves, lest they be scattered like chaff.

3.text: That is, who have lived uprightly and godly according as he prescribes by his word.

4.text: He comforts the faithful in that God would change his punishments from them to the Philistines their enemies, and other nations.

5.text: That is, Galilee: by these nations he means the people that dwelt near to the Jews, and instead of friendship were their enemies: therefore he calls them Canaanites, whom the Lord appointed to be slain.

7.text: He shows why God would destroy their enemies, because their country would be a resting place for his Church.

8.text: These nations presumed to take from the Jews that country which the Lord had given them.

11.text: When he will deliver his people and destroy their enemies and idols, his glory will shine throughout all the world.

14.text: Read Isaiah 34:11

15.text: Meaning, Nineveh, which rejoicing so much of her strength and prosperity, should be thus made waste, and God’s people delivered.

1.text: That is, Jerusalem.

3.text: They are so greedy, that they eat up bones and all.

5.text: The wicked thus boasted that God was ever among them, but the Prophet answers that that cannot excuse their wickedness: for God will not bear with their sins. Yet he did patiently abide and sent his Prophets continually to call them to repentance, but he profited nothing.

6.text: By the destruction of other nations he shows that the Jews should have learned to fear God.

7.text: They were most earnest and ready to do wickedly.

8.text: Seeing that you will not repent, you can expect my vengeance as well as other nations.

9.text: Lest any should then think that God’s glory should have perished when Judah was destroyed, he shows that he will proclaim his grace through all the world.

10.text: That is, the Jews will come as well as the Gentiles: which is to be understood as referring to the time of the Gospel.

11.text: For they will have full remission of their sins, and the hypocrites who boasted of the temple, which was also your pride in times past, will be taken from you.

15.text: That is, the punishment for your sin.
As the Assyrians, Chaldaeans, Egyptians, and other nations.
To defend you, as by your sins you have put him away, and left yourself naked, as in Exodus 32:25 .

17.text: Signifying, that God delights to show his love and great affection toward his Church.

18.text: That is, those that were held in hatred and reviled for the Church, and because of their religion.

19.text: I will deliver the Church, which now is afflicted, as in Micah 4:6 .
As among the Assyrians and Chaldaeans, who mocked them and put them to shame.

1.text: Who was the son of Histaspis and the third king of the Persians, as some think.

Because the building of the temple began to cease, by reason that the people were discouraged by their enemies: and if these two notable men had need to be stirred up and admonished of their duties, what will we think of other governors, whose doings are either against God, or very cold in his cause?

2.text: Not that they condemned the building of it, but they preferred policy and personal profit to religion, being content with small beginnings.

4.text: Showing that they sought not only their necessities, but their very pleasures before God’s honour.

6.text: Consider the plagues of God upon you for preferring your policies to his religion, and because you do not seek him above all else.

8.text: Meaning, that they should leave their own benefits, and go forward in the building of God’s temple, and in the setting forth of his religion.
That is, I will hear your prayers according to my promise; 1 Kings 8:22 ; 1 Kings 8:29 .
That is, my glory will be set forth by you.

9.text: And so bring it to nothing.

12.text: This declares that God was the author of the doctrine, and that Haggai was but the minister, as in Exodus 14:31 , Jud 7:20, Acts 15:28 .

14.text: Which declares that men are unable and dull to serve the Lord, neither can they obey his word or his messengers, before God reforms their hearts, and gives them new spirits; John 6:44 .

3.text: For the people according as had been prophesied in Isaiah 2:2 and Ezekiel 41:1-26 , thought this temple should have been more excellent than Solomon’s temple, which was destroyed by the Babylonians, but the Prophets meant the spiritual Temple, the Church of Christ.

4.text: That is, go forward in building the temple.

6.text: He exhorts them to patience though they do not see as yet this temple so glorious as the Prophets had declared: for this should be accomplished in Christ, by whom all things should be renewed.

7.text: Meaning Christ, whom all ought to look for and desire: or by desire he may signify all precious things, such as riches, and things like them.

8.text: Therefore when his time comes he can make all the treasures of the world to serve his purpose: but the glory of this second Temple does not consist of material things, neither can it be built.

9.text: Meaning all spiritual blessings and felicity purchased by Christ; Philippians 4:7 .

12.text: That is, the flesh of the sacrifices, by which he means that a thing which of itself is good, cannot make another thing so: and therefore they ought not to justify themselves by their sacrifices and ceremonies: but contrary to this, he that is unclean and not pure of heart, does corrupt those things and make them detestable to God, which otherwise are good and godly.

15.text: Consider how God plagued you with famine before you began to build the temple.

16.text: That is, before the building was begun.

18.text: From the time they began to build the temple, he promises that God would bless them: and even though the fruit has not yet come forth, yet in the gathering they would have plenty.

19.text: He exhorts them to have patience, and to remain until the harvest came, and then they would see God’s blessings.

21.text: I will make a change, and renew all things in Christ, of whom Zerubbabel is here a figure.

22.text: By this he shows that there will be no stop or hindrance, when God will make this wonderful restitution of his Church.

23.text: Signifying that his dignity would be most excellent, which thing was accomplished in Christ.

1.text: Who was the son of Histaspis.

This was not the Zechariah, of which mention is made in 2 Chronicles 24:20 , but he had the same name, and is called the son of Berechiah, as he was, because he came of those progenitors, as of Joiada or Berechiah, and Iddo.

2.text: He speaks this to make them afraid of God’s judgments, so that they should not provoke him as their fathers had done, whom he so grievously punished.

3.text: Let your fruits declare that you are God’s people, and that he has wrought in you by his Spirit, and mortified you: for otherwise man has no power to return to God, but God must convert him; Jeremiah 31:18 Lamentations 5:21 Isaiah 31:6 ; Isaiah 45:21

5.text: Though your fathers are dead, yet God’s judgments in punishing them ought still to be before your eyes: and though the prophets are dead, yet their doctrine remains for ever; 2 Peter 1:15 .

6.text: Seeing you saw the force of my doctrine in punishing your fathers, why do you not fear the threatenings contained in the same, and declared by my Prophets?
As men astonished with my judgments, and not that they were touched with true repentance.

7.text: Which includes part of January and part of February.

8.text: This vision signifies the restoration of the Church: but as yet it would not appear to man’s eyes, which is here meant by the night, by the bottom, and by the myrtle trees, which are black, and give a dark shadow. Yet he compares God to a King who has his posts and messengers abroad, by whom he still works his purpose and brings his matters to pass.
Who was the chief among the rest of the horsemen.
These signify the various offices of God’s angels, by whom God sometimes punishes, and sometimes comforts, and brings forth his works in various ways.

12.text: That is, Christ the mediator prayed for the salvation of his Church, which was now troubled, when all the countries about them were at rest.

14.text: Though for a time God defers his help and comfort from his Church, yet this declares that he still loves them most dearly, as a most merciful father his children, or a husband his wife, and when it is expedient for them, his help is ever ready.

15.text: In destroying the reprobate, I showed myself but a little angry toward my Church, but the enemy would have destroyed them also, and did not consider the goal of my chastisements.

16.text: To measure out the buildings.

17.text: The abundance will be so great, that the places of storage will not be able to contain these blessings that God will send, but will even break because of fullness.

18.text: Which signifies all the enemies of the Church: east, west, north, and south.

20.text: These craftsmen or smiths are God’s instruments, who with their mallets and hammers break these hard and strong horns which would overthrow the Church, and declare that no enemies’ horn is so strong, but God has a hammer to break it in pieces.

1.text: This is the angel who was Christ: for in respect of his office he is often called an angel, but in respect of his eternal essence, is God, and so called.

4.text: Meaning himself, Zechariah.

Signifying the spiritual Jerusalem and Church under Christ, which would be extended by the Gospel through all the world, and would need no material walls, nor trust in any worldly strength, but would be safely preserved and dwell in peace among all their enemies.

5.text: To defend my Church, to strike fear in the enemies, and to destroy them if they approach near.
In me they will have their full felicity and glory.

6.text: He calls to those who partly for fear, and partly for their own case, remained still in captivity, and so preferred their own personal benefits to the benefits of God promised in his Church.
As it was I that scattered you, so I have power to restore you.

7.text: By fleeing from Babylon, and coming to the Church.

8.text: Seeing that God had begun to show his grace among you by delivering you, he continues the same still toward you, and therefore sends me his angel and his Christ to defend you from your enemies, so that they will not hurt you, neither along the way nor at home.
You are so dear to God, that he can no more allow your enemies to hurt you, than a man can endure to be thrust in the eye; Psalms 17:8 .

9.text: Upon the heathen your enemies.
They will be your servants, as you have been theirs.
This must necessarily be understood of Christ, who being God equal with his Father, was sent, as he was Mediator to dwell in his Church and to govern them.

1.text: He prayed to Christ the Mediator for the state of the Church.
Which declares that the faithful do not only war with flesh and blood, but with Satan himself, and spiritual wickedness; Ephesians 6:12 .

2.text: That is, Christ speaks to God as the mediator of his Church, that he would rebuke Satan: and here he shows himself to be the continual preserver of his Church.
Meaning that Joshua was wonderfully preserved in the captivity, and now Satan sought to afflict and trouble him when he was doing his office.

3.text: With regard to the glorious garments and precious stones that the priests wore before the captivity: and by this contemptible state the Prophet signifies, that these small beginnings would be made excellent when Christ will make the full restitution of his Church.

4.text: See Geneva " Zechariah 3:3 "
He shows of what apparel he speaks, which is, when our filthy sins are taken away, and we are clothed with God’s mercies, which refers to the spiritual restitution.

5.text: The Prophet prays that besides the raiment, the Priest might also have attire for his head accordingly, that is, that the dignity of the priesthood might be perfect: and this was fulfilled in Christ, who was both Priest and King. And here all those are condemned, that can content themselves with any average reformation in religion, seeing the Prophet desires the perfection, and obtains it.

7.text: That is, have rule and government in my Church, as your predecessors have had.
By which he means to have the whole charge and ministry of the Church.
That is, the angels, who represented the whole number of the faithful: signifying that all the godly would willingly receive him.

8.text: Because they follow my word, they are condemned in the world, and esteemed as monsters. See Geneva " Isaiah 8:18 "

That is, Christ, who did so humble himself, that he not only became the servant of God, but also the servant of men: and therefore in him they should have comfort, even though in the world they are condemned; Isaiah 11:1 Jer 23:5 33:14-15 .

9.text: He shows that the ministers cannot build before God lay the first stone, which is Christ, who is full of eyes, both because he gives light to all others, and that all ought to seek light from him; Zechariah 4:10 .
That is, I will make perfect in all points, as a thing done by the hand of God.
Though I have punished this land for a time, yet I will even now be pacified, and punish their sins no more.

10.text: You will then live in peace and quietness, that is, in the kingdom of Christ; Isaiah 2:2 Micah 4:4 Ha 2:9 .

2.text: Which was ever in the midst of the temple, signifying that the graces of God’s Spirit would shine, here in most abundance, and in all perfection.

Which conveyed the oil that dropped from the trees into the lamps, so that the light never went out: and this vision was to strengthen and encourage the faithful that God had sufficient power in himself to continue his graces, and to bring his promise to pass even though he had no help from man.

6.text: Who was a figure of Christ, and therefore this doctrine was directed to all the Church who are his body and members.
He shows that God’s power alone is sufficient to preserve his Church, even though he does not use man’s help to do it.

7.text: He compares the power of the adversaries to a great mountain, who thought the Jews were nothing with regard to them, and would have hindered Zerubbabel, who represented Christ, whom the enemies daily labour to stop in the building of his spiritual Temple, but all in vain.

Though the enemies think to stop this building, yet Zerubbabel will lay the highest stone of it, and bring it to perfection, so that all the godly will rejoice, and pray to God that he would continue his grace and favour toward the Temple.

9.text: Meaning, the Prophet, that I am Christ sent from my Father for the building and preservation of my spiritual temple.

10.text: Signifying that all were discouraged at the small and poor beginnings of the temple.

By which he signifies the plummet and line, that is, that Zerubbabel who represented Christ, would go forward with his building to the joy and comfort of the godly, though the world was against him, and though his own for a while were discouraged, because they do not see things pleasant to the eye.
That is, God has seven eyes: meaning, a continual providence, so that neither Satan nor any power in the world, can go about to bring anything to pass to hinder his work; Zechariah 5:9 .

14.text: Which were always green and full of oil, so that still they poured forth oil into the lamps: signifying, that God will continually maintain and preserve his Church, and endue it still with abundance and perfection of grace.

2.text: Because the Jews had provoked God’s plagues by condemning his word, and casting off all judgment and equity, he shows that God’s curses written in this book had justly happened both to them and their fathers. But now if they would repent, God would send the same among the Chaldeans and their former enemies.

3.text: That is, does any injury toward his neighbour.
Meaning, wherever he is in the world.
He that transgresses the first table of the ten commandments, and does not serve God correctly but abuses his name.

6.text: Which was a measure in dry things, containing about five gallons.
That is, all the wickedness of the ungodly is in God’s sight, which he keeps in a measure, and can shut it or open it at his pleasure.

7.text: To cover the measure.
Which represents iniquity, as in the next verse.
