8.text: Signifying that Satan would not have such power against the Jews to tempt them, as he had in times past, but that God would shut up iniquity in a measure as in a prison.

9.text: Which declared that God would execute his judgment by the means of the weak and infirm.

11.text: To remove the iniquity and affliction that came from Judah because of the judgment, to place it forever in Babylon.

1.text: By chariots here, as by horses before, he means the swift messengers of God to execute and declare his will.

By the mountains he means the external counsel and providence of God, by which he has from before all eternity declared what will come to pass, and that which neither Satan nor all the world can alter.

2.text: Which signifies the great cruelty and persecution that the Church had endured under different enemies.
Signifying that they had endured great afflictions under the Babylonians.

3.text: These represented their state under the Persians, who restored them to their liberty.
Which signified that God would sometimes give his Church rest, and pour his plagues upon their enemies, as he did in destroying Nineveh and Babylon, and other of their enemies.

5.text: Meaning, all the actions and motions of God’s Spirit, whom according to his unchangeable counsel he causes to appear through all the world.

6.text: That is, towards Egypt, and other countries there about.

7.text: That is, those of different colours, which ask permission, to signify that Satan has no power to hurt or afflict, until God gives it to him; Job 1:12 .

8.text: By punishing the Chaldeans my anger ceased, and you were delivered.

10.text: To receive from him and the other three, money to make the two crowns: who were men of great authority among the Jews, and doubted of the restitution of the kingdom, and of the priesthood, and hurt others by their example.

11.text: Because this could not be attributed to any one according to the Law, therefore it follows that Joshua must represent the Messiah, who was both Priest and King.

12.text: Meaning Christ, of whom Joshua was the figure: for in Greek they were both called Jesus.
That is, of himself without the help of man.
Which declares that no one could build this temple of which Haggai speaks, but only Christ: and therefore it was spiritual, and not material; Ha 2:9 .

13.text: Of which Joshua had but a shadow.
The two offices of the kingdom and priesthood, will be joined together in such a way, that they will no longer be separated.

14.text: Who was also called Heldai.
He was also called Joshias.
That they may acknowledge their infirmity, who thought that all things would be restored immediately: and of this their infidelity these two crowns will remain as tokens; Acts 1:6 .

15.text: That is, the Gentiles by the preaching of the Gospel, will help toward the building of the spiritual temple.
If you will believe and remain in the obedience of faith.

1.text: Which contained part of November and part of December.

2.text: That is, the rest of the people that yet remained in Chaldea, sent to the Church at Jerusalem for the resolution of these questions, because these feasts were consented upon by the agreement of the whole Church, the one in the month that the temple was destroyed, and the other when Gedaliah was slain; Jeremiah 41:2 .

3.text: By weeping and mourning are shown what exercises they used in their fasting.
That is, prepare myself with all devotion to his fast.
Which had been since the time the temple was destroyed.

5.text: For there were both of the people, and of the priests, those who doubted with regard to this controversy, besides those who as yet remained in Chaldea, and argue about it, as of one of the chief points of their religion.

For they thought they had gained favour with God because of this fast, which they invented by themselves: and though fasting of itself is good, yet because they thought it a service toward God, and trusted in it, it is here reproved.

6.text: Did you not eat and drink for your own benefit and necessity, and so likewise you abstained according to your own imaginings, and not after the command and direction of my Law.

7.text: By this he condemns their hypocrisy, who thought by their fasting to please God, and by such things as they invented, and in the meantime would not serve him as he had commanded.

9.text: He shows that they did not fast with a sincere heart, but because of hypocrisy, and that it was not done from a pure religion, because they lacked these offices of charity which should have declared that they were godly; Matthew 23:23 .

11.text: And would not carry the Lord’s burden, which was sweet and easy, but would bear their own, which was heavy and grievous to the flesh, thinking to gain merit by it: which metaphor is taken from oxen, which shrink at the yoke; Nehemiah 9:29 .

12.text: Which declares that they did not only rebel against the Prophets, but against the Spirit of God that spoke in them.

14.text: That is, after they were taken captive.
By their sins by which they provoked God’s anger.

2.text: I loved my city with a singular love, so that I could not endure that any should do her any injury.

3.text: Because she will be faithful and loyal toward me her husband.

4.text: Though their enemies did greatly molest and trouble them, yet God would come and dwell among them, and so preserve them as long as nature would allow them to live, and increase their children in great abundance.

6.text: He shows in what our faith consists, that is, to believe that God can perform that which he has promised, though it seem ever so impossible to man; Genesis 13:14 , Romans 4:20 .

8.text: So that their return will not be in vain: for God will accomplish his promise, and their prosperity will be sure and stable.

9.text: Let neither respect of your personal benefits, neither counsel of others, nor fear of enemies, discourage you in the going forward with the building of the temple, but be steadfast and obey the Prophets, who encourage you to that.

10.text: For God cursed your work, so that neither man nor beast had profit from their labours.

14.text: Read Ezekiel 18:20 .

15.text: Which declares that man cannot turn to God until he changes man’s heart by his Spirit, and so begin to do good to them, which is to pardon his sins and to give him his graces.

19.text: Which fast was appointed when the city was besieged, and was the first fast of these four. And here the prophet shows that if the Jews will repent, and turn wholly to God, they will have no more occasion to fast, or to show signs of heaviness, for God will send them joy and gladness.

20.text: He declares the great zeal that God would give the Gentiles to come to his Church, and to unite with the Jews in his true religion, which would be in the kingdom of Christ.

1.text: By which he means Syria.
God’s anger will remain upon their chief city, and not spare even as much as that.
When the Jews will convert and repent, then God will destroy their enemies.

2.text: That is, by Damascus: meaning, that Harnath or Antiochia would be under the same rod and plague.
He secretly shows the cause of their destruction, because they deceived all others by their craft and subtilty, which they cloaked with this name of wisdom.

4.text: Though those of Tyre think themselves invincible by reason of the sea that surrounds them, yet they will not escape God’s judgments.

6.text: Meaning, that all would be destroyed, save a very few, that would remain as strangers.

7.text: He promises to deliver the Jews when he will take vengeance on their enemies for their cruelty, and the wrongs they did to them.
As the Jebusites had been destroyed, so would Ekron and all the Philistines.

8.text: He shows that God’s power alone will be sufficient to defend his Church against all adversaries, be they ever so cruel, or assert their power ever so often.
That is, God has now seen the great injuries and afflictions with which they have been afflicted by their enemies.

9.text: That is, he has righteousness and salvation in himself for the use and benefit of his Church.

Which declares that they should not look for such a king as would be glorious in the eyes of man, but should be poor, and yet in himself have all power to deliver his own: and this is meant of Christ, as in Matthew 21:5 .

10.text: No power of man or creature will be able to stop this kingdom of Christ, and he will peaceably govern them by his word.
That is, from the Red Sea, to the Sea called Syriacum: and by these places which the Jews knew, he meant an infinite space and area over the whole world.
That is, from the Euphrates.

11.text: Meaning Jerusalem, or the Church which is saved by the blood of Christ, of which the blood of the sacrifices was a figure. And it is here called the covenant of the Church, because God made it with his Church: and left it with them because of the love that he had for them.
God shows that he will deliver his Church out of all dangers, no matter how great they may seem.

12.text: That is, into the holy land where the city and the temple are, where God will defend you.
Meaning the faithful, who seemed to be in danger of their enemies on every side, and yet lived in hope that God would restore them to liberty.
That is, double benefits and prosperity, in respect of that which your fathers enjoyed from David’s time to the captivity.

13.text: I will make Judah and Ephraim, that is, my whole Church, victorious against all enemies, which he here means by the Greeks.

15.text: He promises that the Jews will destroy their enemies, and have abundance and excess of all things, as there is abundance on the altar when the sacrifice is offered. And these things are not to move them to excess, but to sobriety, and a thankful remembrance of God’s great liberality.

16.text: The faithful will be preserved, and reverenced by all, that their very enemies will be compelled to esteem them: for God’s glory will shine in them, as Josephus declares of Alexander the great when he met Jadi the high priest.

1.text: The Prophet reproves the Jews, because by their own infidelity they turn away God’s promised graces, and so famine came by God’s just judgment. Therefore to avoid this plague, he exhorts them to turn to God, and to pray in faith to him, and so he will give them abundance.

2.text: He calls to remembrance God’s punishments in times past, because they trusted not in him, but in their idols and sorcerers who always deceived them.
That is, the Jews went into captivity.

3.text: Meaning, the cruel governors who did oppress the poor sheep; Ezekiel 34:16-17 .
He will be merciful to his Church, and cherish them as a king or prince does his best horse, which will be for his own use in war.

4.text: Out of Judah will the chief governor proceed, who will be as a corner to uphold the building, and as a nail to fasten it together.
Over their enemies.

6.text: That is, the ten tribes, which would be united under Christ to the rest of the Church.

8.text: By which he declares the power of God, who needs no great preparation when he will deliver his own: for with a gesture or hiss he can call them suddenly from all places.

9.text: Though they will yet be scattered and seem to be lost, yet it will be profitable to them: for there they will come to the knowledge of my name, which was accomplished under the Gospel, among whom it was first preached.
Not that they would return into their country, but be gathered and joined in one faith by the doctrine of the Gospel.

11.text: He alludes to the deliverance of the people out of Egypt, when the angel smote the floods and rivers.

1.text: Because the Jews thought themselves so strong by reason of this mountain, that no enemy could come to hurt them, the Prophet shows that when God sends the enemies, it will show itself ready to receive them.

2.text: Showing that if the strong men were destroyed, the weaker were not able to resist.
Seeing that Lebanon was destroyed, which was the strongest fortress, the weaker places could not hope to hold out.

3.text: That is, the fame of Judah and Israel would perish.

4.text: Which being now destined to be slain, were delivered as out of the lion’s mouth.

5.text: Their governors destroy them without any remorse of conscience, or yet thinking that they do evil.

He notes the hypocrites, who always have the name of God in their mouths, though in their life and doings they deny God, attributing their gain to God’s blessings, which comes from the wealth of their brethren.

6.text: I will cause one to destroy another.
Their governors will execute cruelty over them.

7.text: That is, the small remnant, whom he though worthy to show mercy to.

God shows his great benefits toward his people to convince them of greater ingratitude, who would neither be ruled by his most beautiful order of government, neither continue in the bands of brotherly unity, and therefore he breaks both the one and the other. Some read "Destroyers" instead of "Bands", but in Zechariah 11:14 the second reading is confirmed.

8.text: By which he shows his care and diligence that he would not allow them to have evil rulers, so that they would consider his great love.
Meaning, the people, because they would not acknowledge these great benefits of God.

11.text: He shows that the least always profit by God’s judgments.

12.text: Besides their ingratitude, God accuses them of malice and wickedness, who did not only forget his benefits, but esteemed them as nothing.

13.text: Showing that it was too little to pay his wages with, which could hardly suffice to make a few tiles to cover the temple.

15.text: Signifying that they should have a certain type of regiment and outward show of government: but in effect it would be nothing, for they would be wolves, and devouring beasts instead of shepherds.

16.text: And is in health and sound.

17.text: By the arm he signifies strength, as he does wisdom and judgments by the eye: that is, the plague of God will take away both your strength and judgment.

1.text: That is, the ten tribes, which neglected God’s benefit in delivering their brethren, and had rather remain in captivity, than to return home when God called them.

2.text: Jerusalem will be defended against all her enemies: so will God defend all Judah also, and will destroy the enemies.

5.text: Every captain, that had many under him before, will now think that the small power of Jerusalem will be sufficient to defend them against all enemies, because the Lord is among them.

7.text: The people who are now as it were dispersed by the fields, and lie open to their enemies, will be preserved by my power just as if they were under their kings (which is meant by the house of David), or in their defended cities.

10.text: They will have the feeling of my grace by faith, and know that I have compassion on them.
That is, whom they have continually vexed with their obstinacy, and grieved my Spirit. In John 19:37 it is referred to Christ’s body, whereas here it is referred to the Spirit of God.
They will turn to God by true repentance, whom before they had so grievously offended by their ingratitude.

11.text: They will exceedingly lament and repent for their offences against God.
Which was the name of a town and place near to Megiddo, where Josiah was slain; 2 Chronicles 35:22 .

12.text: That is, in all places where the Jews will remain.
Signifying, that this mourning or repentance would not be a vain ceremony: but every one touched with his own griefs will lament.
Under these certain families he includes all the tribes, and shows that both the kings and the priests had by their sins pierced Christ.

13.text: Also called Simeon.

14.text: That is, who were elect by grace, and preserved from the common destruction.

1.text: He shows what will be the fruit of their repentance, that is, remission of sins by the blood of Christ, which will be a continual running fountain, and purge them from all uncleanness.

2.text: He promises that God will also purge them from all superstition, and that their religion will be pure.
Meaning, the false prophets and teachers, who are the corrupters of all religion, whom the Prophet here calls unclean spirits.

3.text: That is, when they will prophesy lies, and make God, who is the author of truth, a cloak for them.
He shows what zeal the godly will have under the kingdom of Christ; De 13:6,9 .

4.text: God will make them ashamed of their errors and lies, and bring them to repentance, and they will no more wear prophet’s apparel to make their doctrine seem more holy.

5.text: They will confess their former ignorance, and be content to labour for their living.

6.text: By this he shows that though their parents and friends dealt more gently with them, and did not put them to death, yet they would so punish their children that became false prophets, that the marks and signs would remain forever.

7.text: The Prophet warns the Jews, that before this great comfort under Christ would come, there would be a horrible dissipation among the people: for their governors and pastors would be destroyed, and the people would be as scattered sheep. And the evangelist applies this to Christ, because he was the head of all pastors; Matthew 26:31 .

8.text: The greatest part will have no portion of these blessings, and yet they that will enjoy them will be tried with great afflictions, so that is will be known that only God’s power and his mercies preserve them.

1.text: He arms the godly against the great temptations that would come, before they enjoyed this prosperous estate promised under Christ, that when these dangers came, they might know that they were warned of them before.

3.text: As your fathers and you have had experience both at the Red Sea, and at all other times.

4.text: By this manner of speech the Prophet shows God’s power and care over his Church, and how he will as it were by a miracle save it.
So that out of all the parts of the world, they will see Jerusalem, which was before his with this mountain: and this he means of the spiritual Jerusalem the Church.

5.text: He speaks of the hypocrites, who could not abide God’s presence, but would flee into all places, where they might hide themselves among the mountains.
Read Amos 1:1 .

Because they did not credit the Prophet’s words, he turns to God and comforts himself in that that he knew that these things would come, and says, "You, O God, with your angels will come to perform this great thing."

7.text: Signifying, that there would be great troubles in the Church, and that the time of it is in the Lord’s hands, yet at length (which is here meant by the evening) God would send comfort.

8.text: That is, the spiritual graces of God, which would always continue in most abundance.

9.text: All idolatry and superstition will be abolished, and there will be one God, one faith, and one religion.

10.text: This new Jerusalem will be seen through all the world, and will excel the first in excellency, wealth, and greatness.

13.text: God will not only raise up war outside, but sedition at home to test them.
To hurt and oppress him.

14.text: The enemies are rich, and therefore will not come to entreat, but to destroy and shed blood.

15.text: As the men would be destroyed, Zechariah 14:12 .

18.text: By the Egyptians, who were the greatest enemies to true religion, he means all the Gentiles.

20.text: Signifying to whatever service they were put now
The one as precious as the other, because they will be sanctified.

21.text: But all will be pure and clean, and there will neither by hypocrites, nor any that will corrupt the true service of God

1.text: See Geneva " Isaiah 13:1 "

2.text: Which declares their great ingratitude that did not acknowledge this love, which was so evident, in that he chose Abraham from out of all the world, and next chose Jacob the younger brother from whom they came, and left Esau the elder.

3.text: For besides this the signs of my hatred appeared even when he was made servant to his younger brother, being yet in his mother’s belly, and also afterward in that he was put from his birthright. Yet even now before your eyes the signs of this are evident, in that his country lies waste, and he will never return to inhabit it.
Whereas you my people, whom the enemy hated more than them, are by my grace and love towards you delivered; read Romans 9:13 .

6.text: Besides the rest of the people he mainly condemns the priests, because they should have reproved others for their hypocrisy, and for not yielding to God, and should not have hardened them by their example to do greater evils.
He notes their great hypocrisy, who would not see their faults, but most impudently covered them, and so were blind guides.

7.text: You receive all types of offerings for your own greediness, and do not examine whether they are according to my Law or not.
Not that they said this, but by their doings they declared it.

8.text: You make it no fault: and by this he condemns them that think it sufficient to serve God partly as he has commanded, and partly after man’s fantasy, and so do not come to the pureness of religion, which he requires. And therefore in reproach he shows them that a mortal man would not be content to be served in such a way.

9.text: He derides the priests who deceived the people in saying that they prayed for them, and shows that they were the occasion that these evils came upon the people.
Will God consider your office and state, seeing you are so covetous and wicked?

10.text: Because the Levites who kept the doors did not test whether the sacrifices that came in were according to the Law, God wishes that they would rather shut the doors, than to receive such as were not perfect.

11.text: God shows that their ingratitude and neglect of his true service will be the cause of the calling of the Gentiles: and here the Prophet that was under the Law, used words that the people would understand, and by the altar and sacrifice he means the spiritual service of God, which should be under the Gospel, when an end would be made to all these legal ceremonies by Christ’s sacrifice alone.

12.text: Both the priests and the people were infected with this error, that they did not regard what was offered: for they thought that God was as well content with the lean, as with the fat. But in the meantime they did not show the obedience to God which he required, and so committed impiety, and also showed their contempt of God, and covetousness.

13.text: The priests and people were both weary with serving God, and did not regard what manner of sacrifice and service they gave to God: for that which was least profitable, was thought good enough for the Lord.

14.text: That is, has ability to serve the Lord according to his word, and yet will serve him according to his covetous mind.

1.text: He speaks mainly to them, but under them he includes the people also.

2.text: To serve me according to my word.
That is, the abundance of God’s benefits.

3.text: The seed you sow will come to no profit.
You boast of your holiness, sacrifices, and feasts, but they will turn to your shame and be as vile as dung.

4.text: The Priests objected against the Prophet that he could not remove them without speaking against the priesthood, and the office established by God by promise. But he shows that the office is nothing slandered, when these villains and dung are called by their own names.

5.text: He shows what were the two conditions of the covenant made with the tribe of Levi on God’s part, that he would give them long life and felicity, and on their part, that they should faithfully serve him according to his word.
I commanded Levi a certain law to serve me.
He served me and set forth my glory with all humility and submission.

6.text: He shows that the priests ought to have knowledge to instruct others in the word of the Lord.

7.text: He is as the treasure house of God’s word, and ought to give to everyone according to their need, and not to reserve it for himself.
Showing that whoever does not declare God’s will, is not his messenger, and priest.

10.text: The Prophet accuses the ingratitude of the Jews toward God and man: for seeing they were all born of one father Abraham, as God had elected them to be his holy people, they ought neither to offend God nor their brethren.
By which they had bound themselves to God to be a holy people.

11.text: They have united themselves in marriage with those that are of another religion.

12.text: That is, the priest.

13.text: Yet cause the people to lament, because God does not regard their sacrifices, so that they seem to sacrifice in vain.

14.text: This is another fault, of which he accuses them, that is, that they broke the laws of marriage.
As the one half of yourself.
She that was united to you by a solemn covenant, and by the invocation of God’s name.

15.text: Did not God make man and woman as one flesh and not many?
By his power and strength he could have made many women for one man.
Those who should be born in lawful and moderate marriage, in which is no excess of lusts.
Contain yourselves within your bounds, and be sober in mind, and bridle your affections.

16.text: Not that he allows divorce, but of two faults he shows which is the less.
He thinks it sufficient to keep his wife still, even though he takes others, and so as it were covers his fault.

17.text: You murmur against God, because he did not hear you as soon as you called.
In thinking that God favoured the wicked, and had no respect for those that serve him.
Thus they blasphemed God in condemning his power and justice, because he did not judge according to their imaginings.

1.text: This is meant of John the Baptist, as Christ interprets it; Lu 7:27 .
Meaning, the Messiah, as in Psalms 40:17 Daniel 9:17 ; Daniel 9:25 .

That is, Christ, by whom the covenant was made and ratified, who is called the angel or messenger of the covenant, because he reconciles us to his Father, and is Lord or King, because he has the rule of his Church.

2.text: He shows that the hypocrites who wish so much for the Lord’s coming will not remain when he draws near: for he will consume them, and purge his own and make them clean.

3.text: He begins at the priests, that they might be lights, and shine unto others.

6.text: They murmured against God, because they did not see his help which was ever present to defend them: and therefore he accuses them of ingratitude, and shows that in that they are not daily consumed, it is a sign that he still defends them, and so his mercy towards them never changes.

7.text: Read Zechariah 1:3 .

8.text: There are none of the heathen so barbarous, that will defraud their gods of their honour, or deal deceitfully with them.
By which the service of God should have been maintained, and the priests and the poor relieved.

10.text: Not having respect how much you need, but I will give you in all abundance, so that you will lack place to put my blessings in.

11.text: Meaning the caterpillar, and whatever destroys corn and fruits.

13.text: The Prophet condemns them of double blasphemy against God: first, in that they said that God had no respect for those that served him, and next, that the wicked were more in his favour than the godly.

15.text: They are not only preferred to honour, but also delivered from dangers.

16.text: After these admonitions of the Prophet, some were strongly touched, and encouraged others to fear God.
Both because the thing was strange that some turned to God in that great and universal corruption, and also that this might be an example of God’s mercies to all repentant sinners.

17.text: When I will restore my Church according to my promise, they will be as my own proper goods.
That is, forgive their sins, and govern them with my Spirit.

1.text: He prophesies of God’s judgments against the wicked, who would not receive Christ, when God would send him for the restoration of his Church.

2.text: Meaning, Christ, who with his wings or beams of his grace would enlighten and comfort his Church; Ephesians 5:14 . And he is called the "Sun of righteousness", because in himself he has all perfection, and also the justice of the Father dwells in him: by which he regenerates us to righteousness, cleanses us from the filth of this world, and reforms us to the image of God.
You will be set at liberty, and increase in the joy of the Spirit; 2 Corinthians 3:17 .

4.text: Because the time had come that the Jews would be destitute of Prophets until the time of Christ, because they should with more fervent minds desire his coming, the Prophet exhorts them to exercise themselves diligently in studying the Law of Moses in the meantime, by which they might continue in the true religion, and also be armed against all temptations.

5.text: This Christ interprets of John the Baptist, who both for his zeal, and restoring or religion, is aptly compared to Elijah; Matthew 11:13-14 .
Which as it is true for the wicked, so does it waken the godly, and call them to repentance.

6.text: He shows in what John’s office would consist: in the turning of men to God, and uniting the father and children in one voice of faith: so that the father will turn to the religion of his son who is converted to Christ, and the son will embrace the faith of the true fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
The second point of his office was to give notice of God’s judgment against those that would not receive Christ.

1.text: Rehearsal: as the Hebrews used to speak; see Genesis 5:1 , the book of the generations.
Of the ancestors from whom Christ came.
Christ is also the son of Abraham.

11.text: That is, the captivity fell in the days of Jakim and Jechonias: for Jechonias was born before the carrying away into captivity.

17.text: All those who were considered to be in the lineage of David’s family, as they begat one another orderly in turn.

20.text: Receive her from her parents and kinsfolks hands.
Who was promised, and made sure to you to be your wife.
Of the mother’s substance by the Holy Spirit.

21.text: Save, and this shows us the meaning of the name Jesus.

23.text: There is an article added in the Hebrew and Greek text, to point out the woman and set her forth plainly: as we would say, the virgin, or a certain virgin.

25.text: The word "till", in the Hebrew language, gives us to understand that a thing will not come to pass in time to come: as Michal had no children "till" her death day, 2 Samuel 6:23 . And in the last chapter of this evangelist: Behold, I am with you "till" the end of the world.

1.text: For there was another in the tribe of Zebulun.
Wise and learned men: It is a Persian word which they use frequently.

3.text: Was much moved, for he was a foreigner, and became ruler by force; and the Jews were troubled; for wickedness is mad and raging.

4.text: The chief priests, that is, such as were of Aaron’s family, who were divided into twenty-four orders. 1 Chronicles 24:5 2 Chronicles 36:14 .
They that expound the law to the people, for the Hebrews take this word for another, which means as much as to expound and to declare.

6.text: Though you are a small town, yet you will be very famous and notable through the birth of the Messiah, who will be born in you.
That will rule and govern: for kings are rightly called leaders and shepherds of the people.

11.text: A kind of humble and lovely reverence.
The rich and costly presents, which they brought him.

12.text: God warned and told them of it, even though they did not ask him.

17.text: For God speaketh by the mouth of the prophets.

18.text: A voice of lamenting, weeping and howling.

That is to say, All who live around Bethlehem: for Rachel, Jacob’s wife who died in childbirth, was buried by the road that leads to this town, which is also called Ephratah, because of the fruitfulness of the soil, and the plentifulness of corn.

1.text: Not when Joseph went to dwell at Nazareth, but a great while after, about fifteen years: for in the 30th year of his life Jesus was baptized by John: therefore "those days" means the time when Jesus remained as an inhabitant of the town of Nazareth.

In a hilly country, which was nonetheless inhabited, for Zacharias dwelt there, Lu 1:39,40 , and there was Joab’s house, 1 Kings 2:34 ; and besides these, Joshua makes mention of six towns that were in the wilderness, Joshua 15:61-62 .

2.text: The word in the greek signifies a changing of our minds and heart from evil to better.
The kingdom of Messiah, whose government will be heavenly, and nothing but heavenly.

3.text: Make him a plain and smooth way.

4.text: Locusts were a type of meat which certain of the eastern people use, who were therefore called devourers of locusts.

5.text: The people of Jerusalem.

6.text: Acknowledging that they were saved only by free remission and forgiveness of their sins.

9.text: Think not that you have any reason to be proud of Abraham.
In your hearts.

11.text: The outward sign reminds us of this, that we must change our lives and become better, assuring us as by a seal, that we are ingrafted into Christ; by which our old man dies and the new man rises up; Romans 6:4 .

12.text: Will clean it thoroughly, and make a full riddance.

15.text: All such things as it has appointed for us to keep.

16.text: To John.

17.text: The Greek word signifies a thing of great worth and such as highly pleases a man. So then the Father says that Christ is the only man whom when he beholds, looking at what opinion he had conceived of us, he lays it clean aside.

2.text: A full forty days.

5.text: The battlement which encompassed the flat roof of the Temple so that no man might fall down: as was appointed by the law; De 22:8 .

7.text: Literally, "Thou shalt not go on still in tempting."

13.text: Which was a town a great deal more famous than Nazareth was.

15.text: Of Tiberias, or because that country went toward Tyre, which borders the eastern Mediterranean Sea.
So called because it bordered upon Tyre and Sidon, and because Solomon gave the king of Tyre twenty cities in that quarter; 1 Kings 9:11 .

17.text: Is come to you.

23.text: Their, that is, the Galilaeans.
Synagogues, that is, the Churches of the Jews.
Of the Messiah.
Diseases of all kinds, but not every disease: that is, as we say, some of every kind.
The word properly signifies the weakness of the stomach: but here it is taken for those diseases which make those that have them faint and wear away.

24.text: The word signifies properly the stone with which gold is tried: and by a borrowed kind of speech, is applied to all kinds of examinations by torture, when as by rough dealing and torments, we draw out the truths from men who otherwise would not confess: in this place it is taken for those diseases, which put sick men to great woe.
Who at every full moon or the change of the moon, are troubled and diseased.
Weak and feeble men, who have the parts of their body loosed and so weakened, that they are neither able to gather them up together, nor do with them as they wish.

3.text: Under the name of poverty are meant all the miseries, that are joined with poverty.
Whose minds and spirits are brought under control, and tamed, and obey God.

8.text: Fitly is this word "pure" joined with the heart, for as a bright and shining resemblance or image may be seen plainly in a clear and pure looking glass, even so does the face (as it were) of the everlasting God, shine forth, and clearly appear in a pure heart.

13.text: Your doctrine must be very sound and good, for if it is not so, it will be not regarded and cast away as a thing unsavoury and vain.
What will you have to salt with? And so are fools in the Latin tongue called "saltless", as you would say, men that have no salt or savour and taste in them.

14.text: You shine and give light by being made partakers of the true light.

17.text: That the prophecies may be accomplished.

19.text: He shall have no place in the Church.

22.text: He speaks of the judgment of God, and of the difference of sins, and therefore applies his words to the form of civil judgments which were then used.
Of that judgment which was ruled by three men, who had the hearing and deciding of money matters, and such other small causes.
By that judgment which stood of 23 judges, who had the hearing and deciding of weighty affairs, as the matter of a whole tribe or of a high priest, or of a false prophet.

Whereas we read here "hell", it is in the text itself "Gehenna", which is one Hebrew word made out of two, and is as if to say "as the Valley of Hinnom", which the Hebrews called Topheth: it was a place where the Israelites cruelly sacrificed their children to false gods, whereupon it was taken for a place appointed to torment the reprobates in Jeremiah 7:31 .

The Jews used four kinds of punishments, before their government was taken away by Herod: hanging, beheading, stoning, and burning. It is burning that Christ meant, because burning was the greatest punishment; therefore by making mention of a judgment, a council, and a fire, he shows that some sins are worse than others are, but yet they are all such that we must give account for them, and will be punished for them.

23.text: He applies all this speech to the state of his time, when there was then an altar standing in Jerusalem, and therefore they are very foolish that gather from this that we must build altars and use sacrifices: but they are bigger fools who consider this to be purgatory, which is spoken of as peace making and atonement one with another.

25.text: Remove all cause for enmity.

26.text: You will be dealt with in this manner, to the utmost extremity.

29.text: He names the right eye and the right hand, because the parts of the right side of our bodies are the chiefest, and the most ready to commit any wickedness.
Literally, do cause you to offend: for sins are stumbling blocks as it were, that is to say, rocks which we are cast upon.

37.text: Whatever you affirm, affirm it alone, and whatever you deny, deny it alone without any more words.
From an evil conscience, or from the devil.

47.text: They that were the toll masters, and had the oversight of tributes and customs: this was a type of man that the Jews hated to death, both because they served the Romans in those offices (whose heavy bondage they could not overthrow) and also because these toll masters were for the most part given to covetousness.

1.text: This word "reward" is always taken in the scriptures for a free recompense, and therefore the schoolmen fondly set it to be answerable to a deserving, which they call "merit".

2.text: Counterfeits, for hypocrites were players that played a part in a play.

7.text: Long prayers are not condemned, but vain, needless, and superstitious ones.

11.text: That which is suitable for our nature for our daily food, or such as may suffice our nature and complexion.

13.text: From the devil, or from all adversity.

16.text: They do not let their original pallor to be seen, that is to say, they mar the natural colour of their faces, that they may seem lean and palefaced.

22.text: The judgment of the mind: that as the body is with the eyes, so our whole life may be ruled with right reason, that is to say, with the Spirit of God who gives light to us.

24.text: Who are at odds with one another, for if two agree they are as one.
This word is a Syrian word, and signifies all things that belong to money.

26.text: Of the air, or that line in the air: in almost all languages the word "heaven" is taken for the air.

27.text: He speaks of care which is joined with thought of mind, and has for the most part distrust yoked with it.

28.text: By labour.

6.text: A pearl is known among the Greeks for its oriental brightness: and a pearl was in ancient times greatly valued by the Latins: for a pearl that Cleopatra had was valued at two hundred and fifty thousand crowns: and the word is now borrowed from that, to signify the most precious heavenly doctrine.

12.text: That is to say, The doctrine of the law and prophets.

14.text: The way is straight and narrow: we must pass through this rough way and suffer, endure, be changed and so enter into life.

22.text: By "name" here is meant mighty working power of God, which every man witnesses that calls upon him.
Properly, powers: Now these excellent works which are done are called powers because of those things which they bring to pass, for by them we understand how mighty the power of God is.

23.text: This is not of ignorance, but because he will cast them away.
You that are given to all kinds of wickedness, and seem to make an art of sin.

11.text: A metaphor taken of banqueters, for they that sit down together are fellows in the banquet.

12.text: Who are outside the kingdom: For in the kingdom is light, and outside the kingdom is darkness.

16.text: Of all sorts.

18.text: For Capernaum was situated upon the lake of Tiberias.

20.text: Literally, "shades made with boughs".

30.text: On a hill, as Mark and Luke witness: Now Gederah, as Josephus records, book seventeen chapter thirteen, lived after the order of the Greeks and therefore we must not be surprised if there were swine there.

34.text: Where men live as swine, there Christ does not abide, but demons.

1.text: Into Capernaum, for as Theophylact says, Bethlehem brought him forth, Nazareth brought him up, and Capernaum was his dwelling place.

2.text: Knowing by a manifest sign.

3.text: To blaspheme, signifies among the divines, to speak wickedly: and among the more eloquent Greeks, to slander.

9.text: At the table where the tax was received.

10.text: The publicans who were placed by the Romans, after that time Judea was brought into the form of a province, to gather the taxes, and therefore by the rest of the Jews they were called sinners, that is to say, very vile men.

15.text: A Hebrew idiom, for they that are admitted into the marriage chamber are as the bridegroom’s closest friends.

16.text: Raw, which was never processed by the fuller.

23.text: It appears that they used minstrels at their mournings.

38.text: Literally, "cast them out": for men are very slow in a work so holy.

2.text: Theophylact says that Peter and Andrew are called the first, because they were first called.

4.text: A man of Kerioth. Now Kerioth was in the tribe of Judah; Joshua 15:25 .

9.text: For this journey, namely, both that nothing might hinder them, and also that they might feel some taste of God’s providence: for at their return back, the Lord asked of them whether they lacked anything by the way, Lu 22:35 .

10.text: God will provide you with food.

13.text: It is an idiom taken from the Hebrews, by which they meant every type of happiness.

16.text: You will be in great danger.

You will not so much as take revenge for an injury: and by the mixing of these beast’s natures together, he will not have our wisdom to be malicious, nor our simplicity mad, but a certain form of good nature which is composed exquisitely of both of them.

17.text: For in the cause of religion men are wolves to each other.

23.text: Bring to an end, that is, you will not have gone through all the cities of Israel and preached in them.

25.text: It was the idol of the Acronites, which we call the god of flies.

26.text: Truth will not always be hidden.

27.text: Openly, and in the highest places. For the tops of their houses were made in such a way that they might walk upon them; Acts 10:9 .

28.text: Though tyrants rage and are cruel, yet we must not fear them.

29.text: The fourth part of an ounce or seven grams.

39.text: They are said to find their life, who deliver it out of danger: and this is spoken against the opinion of the people, who think those that die are certainly lost, because they think not of the life to come.

41.text: As a Prophet.

42.text: Who in the sight of the world are vile and abject.

1.text: Of instructing them with precepts.
The disciples’ cities, that is to say, in Galilee, where many of them were born; Acts 2:7 .

11.text: In the new state of the Church where the true glory of God shines: the people are not compared together, but the types of doctrines, the preaching of John with the law and the prophets: and again, the most clear preaching of the gospel is compared with John’s.

13.text: They prophesied of things to come, which are now present, and clearly and plainly seen.

16.text: He blames the perverseness of this age, by a proverb, in that they could be moved neither with rough nor gentle dealing.

19.text: Wise men acknowledge the wisdom of the gospel when they receive it.

25.text: Through the ministry of Christ, who alone shows the truth of all things pertaining to God.

26.text: This word shows that he contents himself in his Father’s council.
God’s will is the only rule of righteousness.

30.text: May easily be carried. For his commandments are not grievous, for all who are born of God overcome the world; 1 John 5:4 .

4.text: The Hebrews call it "bread of faces", because it stood before the Lord all the week upon the golden table appointed for that service; Leviticus 24:6 .

5.text: When the priests do God’s service on the sabbath day, they do not break the law: much less does the Lord of the Sabbath break the sabbath.

18.text: By judgment is meant a godly kingdom, because Christ was to proclaim true religion among the Gentiles, and to cast out superstition; and wherever this is done, the Lord is said to reign and judge there, that is to say, to govern and rule matters.

20.text: He will pronounce sentence and judgment, in spite of the world and Satan, and show himself conqueror over all his enemies.

39.text: Bastard, who fell from Abraham’s faith or forsook the true worship of God.

For Sheba is situated in the farthest coast of Arabia at the mouth of the Arabian Sea.

19.text: Though there is mention made of the heart, yet this sowing is referred to as hearing without understanding. For whether the seed is received in the heart or not, yet he that sows, sows to the heart.

2.text: By works he means that force and power by which works are performed, and not the works which are often seen before.

6.text: There were three Herods: the first of them was Antipater’s son, who is also called Ascalonius, in whose reign Christ was born, and it was he that caused the children to be slain. The second was called Antipas, Magnus his son, whose mother’s name was Malthaca or Martaca, and he was called Tetrarch, because he enlarged his dominion, when Archelaus was banished to Vienna in France. The third was Agrippa, Magnus his nephew by Aristobulus, and it was he that slew James.

25.text: By the fourth watch is meant the time nearer to day break: for in ancient times they divided the night into four watches in which they posted watches.

26.text: A spirit, as it is taken here, is that which a man imagines to himself vainly in his mind, persuading himself that he sees something when he sees nothing.

34.text: This Gennesaret was a lake near Capernaum, which is also called the Sea of Galilee or Tiberias; so the country itself grew to be called Gennesaret.

2.text: Which they received handed down from their ancestors, or their elders allowed, who were the governors of the Church.

4.text: By honour is meant every duty which children owe to their parents.

5.text: The meaning is this: whatever I bestow upon the temple, is to your profit, for it is as good as if I gave it to you, for (as the Pharisees of our time say) it will be meritorious for you: for under this form of religion, they gathered all to themselves, as though he that had given anything to the temple, had done the duty of a child.

6.text: As much as you could, you destroyed the power and authority of the commandment: for otherwise the commandments of God stand fast in the Church of God, in spite of the world and Satan.

22.text: Of the people of the Canaanites, who dwelt in Phoenicia.

32.text: Go not from my side.

35.text: Literally, "to lie down backwards", as rowers do in rowing, when they draw their oars to themselves.

1.text: To see whether he could do that which they desired, but their purpose was useless for they thought to find something in him by it, in which case they might have just occasion to reprehend him: or else distrust and curiosity moved them to do so, for by such means also is God said to be tempted, that is to say, provoked to anger, as though men would strive with him.

3.text: The outward show and countenance, as it were, of all things, is called in the Hebrew language, a face.

9.text: That five thousand men were filled with so many loaves?

"Spake" for commanded.

The other was Caesarea Philippi, which Herod the great the Tetrarch’s son by Cleopatra, built in the honour of Tiberius at the foot of Lebanon; Josephus lib. 15.

14.text: As Herod thought.

17.text: By this kind of speech is meant man’s natural procreation upon the earth, the one who was made, not being destroyed, but deformed through sin: So then this is the meaning: this was not revealed to you by any understanding of man, but God showed it to you from heaven.

18.text: Christ spoke in the Syrian tongue, and therefore did not use this discourse to distinguish between Petros, which signifies Peter, and Petra, which signifies a rock, but in both places used the word Cephas: but his meaning is what is written in Greek, in which the different word endings distinguish between Peter, who is a piece of the building, and Christ the Petra, that is, the rock and foundation: or else he named him Peter because of the confession of his faith, which is the Church’s as well as his, as the old fathers witness, for so says Theophylact. That confession which you have made, shall be the foundation of the believers.

The enemies of the Church are compared to a strong kingdom, and therefore by "gates" are meant cities which are made strong with wise preparation and fortifications, and this is the meaning: whatever Satan can do by cunning or strength. So does Paul, calling them strongholds; 2 Corinthians 10:4 .

19.text: A metaphor taken from stewards who carry the keys: and here is set forth the power of the ministers of the word, as Isaiah 22:22 says, and that power is common to all ministers, as Matthew 18:18 says, and therefore the ministry of the gospel may rightly be called the key of the kingdom of heaven.

They are bound whose sins are retained; heaven is shut against them, because they do not receive Christ by faith: on the other hand, how happy are they to whom heaven is open, who embrace Christ and are delivered by him, and become fellow heirs with him!

21.text: It was a name of dignity and not of age: and it is used for those who were the judges, whom the Hebrews call the Sanhedrin.

22.text: Took him by the hand and led him aside, as they used to do, which meant to talk familiarly with one.

23.text: The Hebrews call him Satan, that is to say an adversary, whom the Greeks call diabolos, that is to say, slanderer, or tempter: but it is spoken of them, that either of malice, as Judas, John 6:70 , or of lightness and pride resist the will of God.
By this word we are taught that Peter sinned through a false persuasion of himself.

25.text: Shall gain himself: And this is his meaning, they that deny Christ to save themselves, not only not gain that which they look for, but also lose the thing they would have kept, that is, themselves, which is the greatest loss of all: but as for them that doubt not to die for Christ, it goes well with them otherwise.

27.text: Like a King, as Matthew 6:29 .

28.text: By his kingdom is understood the glory of his ascension, and what follows after that, Ephesians 4:10 , or the preaching of the gospel, Mr 9:1 .

6.text: Fell down flat on their faces and worshipped him, as in Matthew 2:11 .

9.text: Which they saw, otherwise the word used in this place is usually used in referring to that which is seen in a dream.

15.text: They that at certain times of the moon are troubled with the falling sickness, or any other kind of disease: but in this case, we must so understand it, that besides the natural disease he had a demonic derangement.

21.text: To help us to understand the watchfulness and diligence of earnest prayer, which cannot be without sobriety.

24.text: He does not deny, but he asks.
Should he not pay?
They that were from twenty years of age to fifty, paid half a shekel to the Sanctuary, Exodus 30:13 . This was an Attic didrachma which the Roman exacted after they had subdued Judea.

25.text: By children we must not understand subjects who pay tribute, but natural children.

27.text: The word used here is "stater", which is in value four didrachmas; every drachma is about five pence.

2.text: A child in years.

3.text: An idiom taken from the Hebrews which is equivalent to "repent".

7.text: Obstructions and hindrances which stop the course of good works. The Greek word conveys the sense of things which we stumble at.

8.text: See Geneva Mt "5:29"

15.text: If his offence is such that only you know your brother’s offence.

16.text: That is, by the word and witness; the mouth is sometimes taken for the word of speech, Numbers 3:16 , and also for a still witness, namely, when the matter speaks for itself, as below in Matthew 21:16 .
Sure and certain.

17.text: Literally, "does not condescend to hear", or "make as though he did not hear".

He speaks not of just any policy, but of an ecclesiastical assembly, for he speaks afterward of the power of loosing and binding, which belonged to the Church, and he has regard for the order used in those days, at which time the elders had the judgment of Church matters in their hands, Joh 9:22 12:42 16:2 , and used casting out of the synagogue for a punishment, as we do now by excommunication.
Profane, and void of religion: such men, the Jews called Gentiles: whose company they shunned, as they did the publicans.

19.text: This word, which is normally used of the body, is here used of the mind, for it belongs properly to poetry.

24.text: Here is set down a very great sum of six thousand crowns, that the difference may be the greater, for there is no proportion between them.

26.text: This was a polite reverence which was very common in the East.

Yield not too much to your anger against me: so is God called in the Scripture, slow to anger, that is to say, gentle, and one that refrains his fierce wrath, Psalms 86:5 ; patient and of great mercy.

1.text: Passed over the water out of Galilee into the borders of Judea.

3.text: To send her a bill of divorce; see Matthew 1:19 .

5.text: The Greek word conveys "to be glued unto", by which it signifies the union by marriage, which is between man and wife, as though they were glued together.
They who were two become one as it were: and this word "flesh" is figuratively taken for the whole man, or the body, after the manner of the Hebrews.

6.text: Has made them yokefellows, as the marriage itself is called a yoke, by a borrowed kind of speech.

8.text: Being brought about because of the hardness of your hearts.
By a political law, not by the moral law: for the moral law is a perpetual law of God’s justice; the other bows and bends as the carpenter’s bevel.

9.text: Therefore in these days the laws that were made against adulterers were not regarded: for they would have no need of divorce, if the marriage had been severed by punishment of death.

10.text: If the matter stands in this way between man and wife, or in marriage.

11.text: Receive and admit, as by translation we say, that a straight and narrow place is not able to receive many things.

12.text: A man can become a eunuch in one of two ways: the first is by castration or emasculation, and the other by natural causes, such as a rupture.
Who abstain from marriage, and live as celibates through the gift of God.

21.text: The young man did not answer truly in saying that he had kept all the commandments: and therefore Christ sets forth an example of true charity before him, to show the disease that lay lurking in his mind.

24.text: Literally, "it is of less labour".
Theophylact notes, that by this word is meant a cable rope, but Caninius alleges out of the Talmuds that it is a proverb, and the word "Camel" signifies the beast itself.

28.text: The regeneration is understood to mean that day when the elect will begin to live a new life, that is to say, when they will enjoy the heavenly inheritance, both in body and soul.

2.text: Literally, "fell in time": it is a kind of speech taken from poetry.

6.text: The last hour: for the day was twelve hours long, and the first hour began at sunrise.

15.text: Naught, that is to say, do you envy at my goodness towards them? For by an "evil eye" the Hebrews mean "envy", because such dispositions appear chiefly in the eyes, as above in Matthew 6:23 . It is set in opposition to the word "single", and it is taken there for corrupt: for whereas he said before in verse 22, "If thine eye be single", he adds in verse 23, "but if thine eye by wicked", or "corrupt", the word being the same in that place as it is here. Matthew 6:22-23

22.text: "Taking the cup" is figurative speech for that which is contained in the cup. And again, the Hebrews understand by the word "cup", sometimes the manner of punishment which is rendered to sin, as Psalms 11:6 , or the joy that is given to the faithful, as Psalms 23:5 , and sometimes a lot or condition, as Psalms 16:5 .
This is in reference to afflictions, as David commonly uses.

23.text: The almightiness of Christ’s divinity is not shut out by this, but it shows the debasing of himself by taking man’s nature upon him.

25.text: Somewhat sharply and roughly.

32.text: Himself, not by the means of other men.

3.text: He that will say anything to you will let them go, that is, the ass and the colt.

5.text: The city of Sion. This is a Hebrew idiom, common in the Lamentations of Jeremiah.

7.text: Their uppermost garment.
Upon their garments, not upon the ass and the colt.

9.text: This was an ancient kind of cry, which they voiced in the feast of Tabernacles, when they carried boughs according as God commanded; Leviticus 23:40 . And the word is corruptly made of two, for we should say, "Hoshiang-na", which is as much as to say, "Save I pray thee".
Well is it to him that comes in the Name of the Lord, that is to say, whom the Lord has given us for our King.

10.text: That is, all the men of Jerusalem were moved.

16.text: You have made most perfect. We read in David, "Thou hast established" or "grounded", and if the matter is considered well, the evangelist says here the same thing, for that which is most perfect is stable and sure.

21.text: The Greek word signifies a fixing or wavering of mind, so that we cannot tell which way to take.

23.text: Or by what power.

24.text: One thing, that is to say, I will ask you one thing first before I answer your questions.

25.text: The preaching of John is called by the figure "baptism" because he preached the baptism of repentance, etc.; Mr 1:4 Acts 19:3 .
From God, and so it is plainly seen how these are set one against another.
Beat their heads about it, and mused, or laid their heads together.

31.text: They hurry to the kingdom of God and you go slowly, so that you should at least have followed their example. Mark then that this word, "go into", is improperly taken in this place because none of them followed Christ.

32.text: Living uprightly, being of good and honest behaviour; For the Hebrews use this word "way" for life and manners.

33.text: Made the place strong: for a tower is the strongest place of a wall.

38.text: Literally, "let us hold it fast".

41.text: A kind of proverb, showing what punishment the wicked are worthy of.

42.text: Master builders, who are chief builders of the house, that is of the Church.
Began to be.
The chiefest stone in the corner is called the head of the corner: which bears up the couplings or joints of the whole building.
That matter (in that the stone which was cast away is made the head) is the Lord’s doing which we behold and greatly marvel at.

43.text: They bring forth the fruits of the kingdom of God, who bring forth the fruit of the Spirit, and not of the flesh, Galatians 5:16-26 .

44.text: As chaff used to be scattered with the wind, for he uses a word which properly signifies separating the chaff from the corn with winnowing, and to scatter it abroad.

4.text: The word used here is commonly used in sacrifices, and is by translation used for other feasts also: For feasts and banquets usually began with sacrifices.

8.text: The marriage feast.

10.text: The general calling offers the gospel to all men: but those who enter in have their life examined.

12.text: Literally, "haltered", that is to say, he held his peace, as though he had a bridle or a halter around his neck.

13.text: To those that served the guests.

15.text: Snare him in his words or talk. The Greek word is derived from snares which hunters lay.

16.text: Those who with Herod made a new religion, composed of both heathen and Jewish religion.
Truly and sincerely.
You are not moved with any appearance and outward show.

17.text: The word that is used here signifies a valuing and rating of men’s substance, according to the proportion of which they payed tribute in those provinces which were subject to tribute, and it is here taken for the tribute itself.

19.text: Before Matthew 17:24 there is mention made of a didrachma, and here of a penny, whereas a didrachma is more by the seventh part then a penny: so that there seems to be an inconsistency in these two places: but they may easily be reconciled in this way: The penny was paid to the Romans for tribute, according to the proportion they were rated at, and the drachma was payed by everyone to the Temple, which also the Romans took to themselves when they had subdued India.

24.text: Daughters are also included by this word "children", but even though they were part of his family and bore his name, the man who had only daughters was in the same position as the man who had no children at all; this is because daughters were not at this time able to carry on the family name. Therefore, by "children" here, we should understand it to be referring to "sons".

30.text: He does not say that they will be without bodies, for then they would not be men any more; but, they will be as angels, for they will neither marry nor be married.

35.text: A scribe, so it says in Mr 12:28 . To understand what a scribe is, see Geneva " Matthew 2:4 "

37.text: The Hebrew text in De 6:5 reads, "with thine heart, soul, and strength"; and in Mr 12:30 and Lu 10:27 we read, "with soul, heart, strength and thought."

39.text: Another man.

2.text: Because God appointed the order, the Lord would therefore have his word to be heard even from the mouth of hypocrites and hirelings.

3.text: Provided always that they deliver the doctrine of Moses which they profess, which thing the metaphor of the seat shows, which they occupied as teachers of Moses’ teaching.

5.text: It was a thread or ribband of blue silk in the fringe of a corner, the beholding of which made them remember the laws and ordinances of God: and therefore it was called a phylactery, or as you would say, a container. See Numbers 15:38 De 6:8 , a commandment which the Jews abused afterwards, as those do today who hang the gospel of John around their necks, which was condemned many years ago in the Council of Antioch.
Literally, "Twisted tassels of thread which hung at the outermost hems of their garments."

6.text: When assemblies and councils are gathered together.

7.text: This word "Rabbi" signifies one that is above his fellows, and is as good as any of them: and we may see by the repeating of it how proud a title it was. Now they were called Rabbi who, by the laying on of hands, were uttered and declared to the world to be wise men.

8.text: Seek not ambitiously after it: for our Lord does not forbid us to give the magistrate and our masters the honour that is due to them; Augustine in a sermon on the words of God from Matthew 11:1-30 .
He seems to allude to references in Isaiah 54:13 and Jeremiah 31:34 .

9.text: He attacks a custom of the Jews, for they called the rabbis "our fathers".

10.text: It seems that the scribes hunted very greatly after such titles, these scribes being the ones whom he called blind guides in Matthew 23:16 .

12.text: He seems to allude to the position of the rabbis, for rabbi signifies one that is in a high position.

13.text: Christ, when he reproves any man sharply, uses this word to show us that there is nothing more detestable than hypocrisy and falsehood in religion.
Who are even at the door.

14.text: Literally, "under a colour of long praying"; and the word "and" signifies a double wickedness in them: the one, that they devoured widows goods: the other that they did it under a pretence of godliness.

15.text: The dry part: now that part of the earth is called dry which the Lord has given to us to live upon.

23.text: Faithfulness in the keeping of promises.

Through all that part of the world that people live in.

18.text: This is a sign of how great the fear will be.

The whole nation would utterly be destroyed: and this word "flesh" is a figurative word for "man", as the Hebrews used to say.

28.text: Christ, who will come with speed; and his presence will be with a majesty to whom all will flock, just like Eagles.

All nations, and he alludes to the dispersion which we read of in Genesis 10-11 , or to the dividing of the people of Israel.

Sitting upon the clouds, as he was taken up into heaven.

34.text: This age: the word "generation" or "age" is here being used for the men of this age.

41.text: The Greek women and the barbarians ground and baked.

1.text: The pomp of weddings was usually preferred to be done at night, and that by young unmarried women.

5.text: Their eyes being heavy with sleep.

15.text: According to the wisdom and skill in dealing which was given to them.

21.text: Come and receive the fruit of my goodness: now the Lord’s joy is doubled; see John 15:11 : that my joy may remain in you, and your joy be fulfilled.

27.text: Bankers who have their shops or tables set up abroad, where they lend money at interest. Usury or loaning money at interest is strictly forbidden by the Bible, Exodus 22:25-27 De 23:19,20 . Even a rate as low as one per cent interest was disallowed, Nehemiah 5:11 . This servant had already told two lies. First he said the master was an austere or harsh man. This is a lie for the Lord is merciful and gracious. Next he called his master a thief because he reaped where he did not sow. Finally the master said to him sarcastically why did you not add insult to injury and loan the money out at interest so you could call your master a "usurer" too! If the servant had done this, his master would have been responsible for his servant’s actions and guilty of usury.

34.text: Blessed and happy, upon whom my Father has most abundantly bestowed his benefits.

5.text: By the word "feast" is meant the whole feast of unleavened bread: the first and eighth day of which were so holy that they were not allowed to do any work on it, though the whole company of the Sanhedrin determined otherwise: And yet it came to pass through God’s providence, that Christ suffered at that time, so that all the people of Israel might be witnesses of his everlasting sacrifice.

7.text: For these things were done before Christ came to Jerusalem: and yet some think that the evangelists have two differing accounts.
These boxes were of alabaster, which in ancient times men made hollow to put in ointments: for some write that alabaster keeps ointment without changing it in any way; Pliny, book 13, chap. 1.

8.text: This is a figure of speech called synecdoche: for it is said that only Judas was moved at this; John 12:4 .
Unprofitable spending.

12.text: In that she poured this ointment upon my body, she did it to bury me.

17.text: This was the fourteenth day of the first month: now the first day of unleavened bread should have been the fifteenth, but because the evening of this day (which after the manner of the Romans was referred to the day before) belonged by the Jews’ manner to the day following, therefore it is called the first day of unleavened bread.

20.text: Because the Law appointed them to be wearing footwear, and to have their staffs in their hands, as though they were is haste, therefore it is to be gathered that they did not sit down when they ate the Passover, but stood, for normally when they went to eat they took off their shoes: therefore he speaks here in this place, not of the Passover, but of the supper which was celebrated after the Passover was solemnly done.

23.text: That is to say, he whom I invited to come to my table, alluding in this to Psalms 41:9 , which is not to be understood as though just as the Lord spoke these words Judas had his hand in the dish (for that would have been an undoubted sign) but it refers to his tabling and eating with him.

25.text: Who was thinking of nothing else but to betray him.

26.text: Mark says, "Had given thanks": and therefore blessing is not a consecrating with a conjuring type of murmuring and power of words: and yet the bread and the wine are changed, not in nature but in quality, for without doubt they become tokens of the body and blood of Christ, not of their own nature or force of words, but by Christ his institution, which must be recited and laid forth, that faith may find what to lay hold on, both in the word and in the elements.

This is a figure of speech which is called metonymy: that is to say, the giving of one name for another: so he calls the bread his body, which is the sign and sacrament of his body: and yet nonetheless, it is a figurative and changed kind of speech meaning that the faithful do indeed receive Christ with all his gifts (though by a spiritual means) and become one with him.

27.text: Therefore they who took away the cup from the people, disobeyed the instruction of Christ.

28.text: That is, this cup or wine is my blood sacramentally, as in Geneva "Lu 22:20".
Or covenant, that is to say, by which the new league and covenant is made, for in the making of leagues they used the pouring of wine and shedding of blood.

30.text: When they had made an end of their solemn singing, which some think was six Psalms, Psalms 112:1 to Psalms 117:2 .

37.text: The word which he uses signifies great sorrow, and tremendous and deadly grief: this thing, as it indicates man’s true nature, which shuns death as a thing that entered in against nature, shows that though Christ was void of sin, yet he sustained this horrible punishment, because he felt the wrath of God kindled against us for sins, which he revenged and punished in his person.

39.text: Let it pass me, and not touch me.
That is, which is at hand, and is offered and prepared for me: an idiom which the Hebrews use for the wrath of God, and the punishment he sends. See Geneva " Matthew 20:22 ".

47.text: Sent from the high Priests.

50.text: Christ reprehends Judas tauntingly, and rebukes him sharply, for he knew well enough why he came.

52.text: They take the sword to whom the Lord has not given it, that is to say, they who use the sword and are not called to it.

54.text: By this questioning he answers a sly objection, for they might have asked him why he did not in this his great extremity of danger call to his Father for aid: but to this objection he answers by this question.

57.text: From Annas to Caiaphas, before whom the multitude was assembled; John 18:13 .

58.text: The word used here properly denotes an open large room in the front of a house, as we see in kings’ palaces and noblemen’s houses: we call it a court, for it is open to the air, and by the use of synecdoche, is understood to mean the house itself.

62.text: How does it come to pass that these men witness against thee?

64.text: This word distinguishes his first coming from the latter.
Sitting with God in like and equal honour at the right hand of his power, that is, in greatest power: for the right hand signifies among the Hebrews that which is mighty and of great power.
Clouds of heaven; see above in Matthew 24:30 .

65.text: This was a peculiar custom among the Jews: for so were they bound to do when they heard any Israelite blaspheme God, and it was a tradition of their talmud in the book of the magistrates, in the title, of the four kinds of death.

69.text: That is, outside the place where the bishop sat, but not outside of the house, for afterward he went from there into the porch.

5.text: Out of the sight of men.

6.text: The treasury of the temple.
Of life and death.

7.text: Strangers and guests, whom the Jews could not endure to be joined with even after they were dead.

9.text: As this prophecy is found in Zechariah 11:12 it cannot be denied that Jeremy’s name slipped into the text either through the fault of the Scribe, or by someone else’s ignorance: it may also be that it came out of the margin by means of the abbreviation on one of the letters, the one being "yod" and the other being "zayin", which are very similar: But in the Syrian text the Prophet’s name is not written down at all.
The evangelist does not follow the prophet’s words, but instead he follows the prophet’s meaning, which he shows to have been fulfilled.

24.text: It was a custom in ancient times that when any man was murdered, or there were other slaughters, to wash their hands in water to declare themselves guiltless.
Of the murder; a Hebrew idiom.

25.text: If there is any offence committed in slaying him, let us and our posterity suffer for it.

28.text: They threw a cloak about him and wrapped it around him, for it did not have any sleeves.

John and Mark also mention a purple robe, which is also a very pleasant red. But these profane and impudently disrespectful soldiers clad Jesus in this array to make an additional mockery of him, this one who was indeed a true King.

32.text: They compelled Simon to bear his burdensome cross, by which it appears that Jesus was so poorly handled before that he fainted along the way, and was not able to bear his cross the whole distance: for John writes that he did bear the cross, that is, at the beginning.

44.text: This is spoken using the figure of speech called synecdoche, for only one of the thieves reviled him.

46.text: That is, in this misery: And this crying out is a natural part of his humanity, which, even though it was void of sin, still felt the wrath of God, the wrath which is due to our sins.

47.text: They allude to Elias’ name, not because they did not understand what he said, but because of a profane impudence and disrespect, and he repeated those words so that this repetition of the name might be understood.

51.text: Which separated the holiest of all.

52.text: That is to say, the stones broke apart, and the graves opened themselves to show by this act that death was overcome: and the resurrection of the dead followed the resurrection of Christ, as the next verse indicates Matthew 27:53 .

65.text: The soldiers of the garrison who were appointed to guard the temple.

1.text: At the going out of the sabbath, that is, about daybreak after the Roman manner of telling time, which considers the natural day to be from the rising of the sun to the next sunrise: and not as the Hebrews, which count from evening to evening.
When the morning of the first day after the sabbath began to dawn: and that first day is the same as that which we now call Sunday, or the Lord’s day.

3.text: The beams of his eyes, and by the figure of speech called synecdoche, this is understood as the countenance.

5.text: The word "ye" is spoken with force to indicate that it was the women to whom he was speaking, as the soldiers were also afraid.

14.text: For it was to be feared that it would be brought to the governor’s ears.

19.text: Calling upon the Name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit.

20.text: Forever: and this refers to the manner of the presence of his Spirit, by means of which he makes us partakers both of himself and of all his benefits, even though he is absent from us in body.

2.text: This is the figure of speech called metonymy, by which is meant the books of the prophets Malachi and Isaiah.
The prophet uses the present tense when he speaks of a thing to come, as he is as sure of it as if he had already seen it.
A metaphor taken from the practice of kings, who used to have ushers go before them.

4.text: The Jews used many kinds of washings: but here a peculiar kind of washing is spoken of, which contains within it true baptism, amendment of life, and forgiveness of sins.

7.text: The evangelist is expressing here the condition of the basest servant.

8.text: He shows that all the power of baptism proceeds from Christ, who baptizes the inner man.

10.text: John, who went down into the water with Christ.

11.text: See Geneva " Matthew 3:17 "

12.text: "Driveth" here does not refer to something violent and forcible: but the divine power clothes Christ (who had lived until this time as a private man) with a new person, and prepares him for the battle that was at hand, and for his ministry.

21.text: From the city of Nazareth.

23.text: Literally, "a man in an unclean spirit", that is to say, possessed with an evil spirit.

24.text: He was born in Bethlehem, but through the error of the people he was called a Nazarene, because he was brought up in Nazareth.
He alludes to the name that was written in the golden plate which the high Priest wore; Exodus 28:36

26.text: See below, Mr 9:20 .

27.text: As men who were amazed.
By his own authority, or as a lord.

28.text: Not only into Galilee, but also into the countries bordering upon it.

38.text: Villages which were like cities.

1.text: In the house where he used to remain: for he chose Capernaum to dwell in and left Nazareth.

2.text: Neither the house nor the entry was able to hold them.

The word signifies the poorest kind of bed, upon which men used to lay down at noon, and at such other times to refresh themselves; we call it a couch.

6.text: In their minds disputing upon the matter, arguing both sides.

12.text: Literally, "past themselves", or "out of their wit".

14.text: Matthew’s other name.

23.text: Literally, "on the Sabbaths", that is, on the holy days.

26.text: In 1 Samuel 21:1 he is called Ahimelech and his son is called Abiathar, but by conferring other places it is plain that both of them had two names; see 1 Chronicles 24:6 2 Samuel 8:17 2 Samuel 15:29 1 Kings 2:26 2 Kings 25:18 .

28.text: Has the sabbath day in his power, and may rule it as he desires.

1.text: That is, unprofitable and dead.

4.text: He uses here the figure of speech called synecdoche, for this type of saying, "to save the life", is the same as saying "to save the man".

5.text: Men are angry when they have wrong done to them, but not without sin: but Christ is angry without sin, and he is not sorry for the injury that is done to him as much as he is for their wickedness; and therefore he had pity upon them, and because of that he is said to have been grieved.
As though their heart had been closed up and had grown together, so that wholesome doctrine had no effect upon them.

6.text: See Matthew 22:16 .

8.text: With free and wandering blasts as it wishes.

That is, has any spiritual light and understanding, or ever had any, but only the Son of God who came down to us.

That which is proper to the divinity of Christ, is here spoken of the whole Christ, to show us that he is but one person in which two natures are united.

Not only the people of the Jews, but whoever will believe in him.

That is, with God, God as it were going before.
