Is characterized by nothing but corruption, ignorance, dulness, etc.

That is, very few.

It was almost noon.

20.text: The name of this mountain is Gerizim, upon which Sanabaletta the Cuthite built a temple with the permission of Alexander of Macedonia, after the victory of Issica: and he made high priest there Manasses his son in law; Josephus, book 11.

24.text: By the word "spirit" he means the nature of the Godhead, and not the third person in the Trinity.

37.text: That proverb.

43.text: Into the towns and villages of Galilee, for he would not live in his country of Nazareth, because they despised him, and where (as the other evangelists write) the efficacy of his benefits was hindered because of their being incredibly stiffnecked.

2.text: Of which cattle drank, and used to be plunged in, since there was a great abundance of water at Jerusalem.
That is to say, the house of pouring out, because a great abundance of water was poured out into that place.

18.text: That is, his alone and no one else’s, which they gather from his saying, "And I work", applying this word "work" to himself which properly belongs to God, and therefore makes himself equal to God.

19.text: Not only without his Father’s authority, but also without his mighty working and power.

This must be understood of the person of Christ, which consists of two natures, and not simply of his Godhead: so then he says that his Father moves and governs him in all things, but yet nonetheless, when he says he works with his Father, he confirms his Godhead.

In like sort, jointly and together. Not because the Father does some things, and then the Son works after him and does the same, but because the might and power of the Father and the Son work equally and jointly together.

22.text: This word "judgeth" is taken by the figure of speech synecdoche to represent all governing.

These words are not to be taken as though they simply denied that God governed the world, but rather they deny that he governed as the Jews imagined it, who separate the Father from the Son, whereas indeed, the Father does not govern the world, but only in the person of his Son, being made manifest in the flesh: so he says below in John 5:30 , that he came not to do his own will: that his doctrine is not his own, that the blind man and his parents did not sin John 7:16 John 9:3 , etc.

27.text: That is, high and sovereign power to rule and govern all things, in so much that he has power over life and death.
That is, he will not only judge the world as he is God, but also as he is man, he received this from his Father, to be judge of the world.

29.text: From their graves.
To that resurrection which has everlasting life following it: against which is set the resurrection of condemnation, that is, which is followed by condemnation.

30.text: See above in John 5:22 .
As my Father directs me, who dwells in me.

31.text: Faithful, that is, worthy to be credited; see John 8:14 .

35.text: A little while.

42.text: Love toward God.

1.text: Not that he cut across the lake of Tiberias, but by sailing across the large creeks he made his journey shorter: therefore he is said to have gone over the sea, when in reality he passed over from one side of the creek to the other.

17.text: In Mr 6:45 they are told to go ahead to Bethsaida, for Bethsaida was along the way to Capernaum.

21.text: They were afraid at first, but when they recognized his voice they became new men and took him willingly into the ship, the very one whom they had shunned and fled from before.

That is, whom God the Father had distinguished from all other men by planting his own power in him, as though he had sealed him with his seal, so that he might be a vivid example and representation of him: and furthermore he installed him to this office, to reconcile us men to God, and bring us to everlasting life, which office belongs only to Christ.

28.text: Which please God: for they think that everlasting life depends upon the condition of fulfilling the law: therefore Christ calls them back to faith.

29.text: That is, this is the work that God requires, that you believe in me, and therefore he calls them back to faith.

35.text: Which has life and gives life.

38.text: See above in John 5:22 .

That is, they will be children of the Church, for so the prophet Isaiah expounds it in Is 54:13 ; that is to say, ordained to life, see Geneva " Acts 13:48 ", and therefore the knowledge of the heavenly truth is the gift and work of God, and does not rest in any power of man.

46.text: If only the Son has seen the Father, then it is only he that can truly teach us and instruct us.

That is to say, whoever is truly a partaker of Christ, who is our food.

Christ means that although he is man, yet his flesh can give life, not by its own nature, but because his flesh lives by the Father, that is to say, sucks and draws out of the Father that power which it has to give life.

63.text: Spirit, that is, that power which flows from the Godhead causes the flesh of Christ (which is otherwise nothing but flesh) both to live in itself and to give life to us.

Born and begotten of Abraham.

The author of it.

With the eyes of faith; Hebrews 11:13 .

And in all places of the Scripture the full comfort of the Church is considered to be that day when God will be all in all, and is therefore called the day of redemption.

Now whereas he said before that no man saw God at any time, it is to be understood in this way: without Christ, or were it not through Christ, no man could ever see God, nor ever saw God, at any time: for as Chrysostom says, the Son is a very concise and plain setting forth of the Father’s nature to us.

12.text: That is, not only do them, but I can also give other men power to do greater.

Worldly men.

He refers to the time that followed his ascension, when as all those opposed were manifestly reproved, through the pouring out of the Holy Spirit upon the Church: so that the very enemies of Christ were reproved of sin, in that they were forced to confess that they were deceived, in that they believed not, and therefore they said to Peter in Acts 2:37 , "Men and brethren, what shall we do?"

10.text: Of Christ himself: for when the world will see that I have poured out the Holy Spirit they will be forced to confess that I was just, and was not condemned by my Father when I went out of this world.

16.text: When a little time is past.

19.text: Either the doors opened to him of their own accord, or the very walls themselves were a passage to him.

With his relatives.

1.text: Literally, "was fulfilled": that is, was begun, as in Lu 2:21 . Will be always open to me.

In danger of present death.

24.text: He alludes to that which is written in De 25:3 . And moreover this place shows us that Paul suffered many more things which Luke omitted in writing Acts.

25.text: By the Roman magistrates.

27.text: Painfulness is a troublesome sickness, as when a man who is weary and wants rest is forced to begin new labour.

2.text: I speak this in Christ, that is, it is spoken without boastfulness, for I seek nothing but Christ Jesus only.
Into the highest heaven: for we do not need to dispute subtly upon the word "third". But yet this passage is to be marked against those who would make heaven to be everywhere.

4.text: So the Greeks name that which we call a park, that is to say, a place where trees are planted, and wild beasts kept. Which no man is able to utter.

Which sets those lusts on fire.

8.text: Often.

9.text: That I might feel the power of Christ more and more: for the weaker that our tabernacles are, the more does Christ’s power appear in them.

4.text: Out of that most corrupt state which is without Christ.

Profane people who did not know God.
